essay.en:
The surah opens by calling all people, not the faithful alone, to be wary of their Lord. Tabatabai reads the choice of address as deliberate: the description that follows, who created you from a single soul, takes in everyone, and it belongs to lordship, which takes charge of nurture and completion, rather than to divinity [1]. The single soul is Adam, al-Tusi says, by the agreement of the exegetes, and the warning against cutting blood ties is set here because of what is coming, the charge concerning children, women and the weak, so that people may know they are all from one soul [12].

What follows is law. Tabatabai treats these verses on orphans and women as ground laid for the rulings on inheritance and marriage, two of the largest and greatest chapters of law governing human society [2]. The orphan's property comes first: give the orphans their property, do not replace the good with the bad, do not eat it up with your own. Then the hardest sentence in the passage, which ties the fear of not dealing justly with orphans to marrying two, three, or four. Al-Tusi records six accounts of what occasioned it and puts Aisha's first: the orphan girl in her guardian's care whose wealth and beauty he desires, whom he would marry below the dower her peers command [14]. Then dowries, handed over to the women themselves; then the rule that property is kept from those who would waste it; then the test that ends a guardianship, and witnesses at the handover.

Verse seven states the principle the surah will spell out. Tabatabai reads it as a general rule set down to announce that there is no exclusion from inheritance once birth or kinship is established [3]; al-Tabrisi reports that the Arabs had passed inheritance to males alone and that the verse came down against them [9]; al-Qummi reads the general statement as superseded by the fixed shares that follow [27]. The last three verses close the door. Provide for the kin, orphans and needy who attend the division. Do not urge a dying man into a bequest that damages his heirs, but fear for another's children as you would for your own [19]. And know that the threat falls on eating that property wrongfully, since a guardian may take the wage his work is worth or eat in an honourable manner [20].

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports Abu Ali al-Farisi: the accusative reading of 'blood relations' admits two constructions, the second being 'be wary of Allah and be wary of blood relations, so join them and do not sever them' [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هي طاعته فلا يعصى، وأن يذكر فلا ينسى، وأن يشكر فلا يكفر

text.en: He was asked about wariness of God. He said: It is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He be remembered and not forgotten, that He be thanked and not denied.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه سئل عن خلق حواء وقيل له أن أناساً عندنا يقولون ان الله خلق حواء من ضلع آدم اليسرى الأقصى قال سبحان الله تعالى عن ذلك علواً كبيراً … ثم قال ان الله تبارك وتعالى لما خلق آدم من طين وأمر الملائكة فسجدوا له القى عليه السبات ثم ابتدع له حواء

text.en: He was asked about the creation of Hawwa, and told that some among us say God created her from Adam's lowest left rib. He said: Glory be to God, far exalted above that. When God had created Adam from clay and the angels prostrated to him, He cast slumber upon him, then originated Hawwa for him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نحن أصل الإيمان بالله وملائكته وتمامه، ومنا الرقيب على خلق الله، وبه إسداد أعمال الصالحين، ونحن قسم الله الذي يُسأل به ونحن وصية الله في الأولين ووصيته في الآخرين
narrations.chain: Furat, from Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, from Jafar ibn Muhammad

text.en: We are the root of faith in God and His angels, and its completion. From us is the watcher over God's creation, and by him the deeds of the righteous are set straight. We are God's oath by which one is adjured, and God's testament among the first and the last.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports that when this verse came down guardians disliked mingling with orphans and complained to the Prophet, until 2:220 was revealed; that account, he says, is narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألته عن رجل أكل مال اليتيم، هل له توبة؟ فقال … يؤدي إلى أهله، لأن الله يقول
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Samaa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked him about a man who had consumed an orphan's property: is there repentance for him? He said: He returns it to its people, because God says that those who consume the property of orphans wrongfully only ingest fire into their bellies, and says that it is a great sin.

note.en: Al-Qummi holds that half of this verse came down with 4:127 and was set at the head of the surah, since men would not marry the orphan girls they had raised and asked the Prophet about it [23].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أما قوله عز وجل: { فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تَعْدِلُواْ فَوَٰحِدَةً } يعني في النفقة، وأما قوله: { وَلَن تَسْتَطِيعُوۤاْ أَن تَعْدِلُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلاَ تَمِيلُواْ كُلَّ ٱلْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ } [النساء: 129] يعني في المودة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shuayb and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan

text.en: As for His words, marry women that you like, two, three, or four, but if you fear you will not treat them fairly, then one, that means in maintenance. And as for His words, you will not be able to be just between wives even if you are eager, that means in affection.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا يحل لماء الرجل أن يجري في أكثر من أربعة أرحام من الحراير

text.en: It is not lawful for a man's seed to run in more than four wombs of free women.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi's third reading takes 'the feeble-minded' as every fool, whether a child, a madman, or one interdicted for squandering, and places near it al-Sadiq's word that the fool is the wine-drinker and his like [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فالسفهاء النساء والولد، إذا علم الرجل أن امرأته سفيهة مفسدة وولده سفيه مفسد لا ينبغي له يسلط واحداً منهما على ماله الذي جعله الله له (قياماً) يقول معاشاً
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The feeble-minded are the wife and the child. If a man knows that his wife is foolish and wasteful, and his child foolish and wasteful, he should not set either of them over the property God made his support, that is, his livelihood.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: شارب الخمر لا تصدقوه إذا حدث ولا تزوجوه إذا خطب ولا تعودوه إذا مرض ولا تحضروه إذا مات ولا تأتمنوه على أمانة … لأن الله يقول ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم وأي سفيه أسفه من شارب الخمر
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The wine-drinker: do not believe him when he speaks, do not marry him when he proposes, do not visit him when he is ill, do not attend him when he dies, and do not entrust him with a trust. For God says, do not give the feeble-minded your property, and what fool is more foolish than a wine-drinker?

note.en: Al-Tabrisi reports his companions' rule that the limit of maturity is the completion of fifteen years, or reaching the age of marriage, or the growth of hair [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إيناس الرشد: حفظ المال

text.en: He was asked about God's words, then if you discern in them maturity, deliver to them their property. He said: Discerning maturity is the safekeeping of property.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من كان يلي شيئا لليتامى وهو محتاج ليس له ما يقيمه فهو يتقاضى أموالهم، ويقوم في ضيعتهم، فليأكل بقدر الحاجة ولا يسرف، فإذا كانت ضيعتهم لا تشغله عما يعالج لنفسه فلا يرزأن أموالهم شيئا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaa, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Whoever manages anything for orphans and is in need, having nothing to keep him, so that he collects their revenues and looks after their estate, let him eat to the measure of need and not exceed it. If their estate does not keep him from his own work, let him take nothing of their property.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألته عن اليتمية، متى يدفع إليها مالها؟ قال … إذا علمت أنها لا تفسد ولا تضيع
narrations.chain: with his chain from Safwan, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked him about the orphan girl: when is her property handed over to her? He said: When you know that she will not spoil it or waste it.

note.en: Fayd Kashani holds that abrogating the obligation does not remove the permissibility or the recommendation, so the giving stands as a commended act [44].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نسختها آية الفرائض
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: On God's words, and when the division is attended by relatives, the orphans and the needy, provide for them out of it: the verse of the fixed shares abrogated it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أنه سئل أمنسوخة هي قال لا إذا حضروك فاعطهم

text.en: He was asked whether the verse is abrogated. He said: No. When they are present with you, give them.

note.en: Al-Tusi gathers four readings of the verse; the first, from Ibn Abbas and others, makes it a prohibition against a bequest that damages the heirs [19].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أوعد الله تبارك و تعالى في مال اليتيم عقوبتين: إحداهما عقوبة الآخرة النار، وأما عقوبة الدنيا فقوله عز وجل: { وَلْيَخْشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُواْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافاً خَافُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ } الآية، يعني ليخش أن أخلفه في ذريته كما صنع بهؤلاء اليتامى
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Samaa

text.en: God has threatened two punishments over the orphan's property. One is the punishment of the hereafter, the Fire. The punishment of this world is His word, let those fear who, were they to leave behind weak offspring, would be concerned on their account: let him fear that I deal with his offspring as he dealt with these orphans.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من ظلم يتيماً سلط الله عليه من يظلمه أو على عقبه أو على عقب عقبه ثم تلا هذه الآية

text.en: Whoever wrongs an orphan, God sets over him one who wrongs him, or over his posterity, or over the posterity of his posterity. Then he recited this verse.

note.en: Al-Tusi ties the threat to the word 'wrongfully', since a guardian may take the wage his work is worth, eat in an honourable manner, or take from it as a loan against himself [20].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) عَنْ أَكْلِ مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ فَقَالَ هُوَ كَمَا قَالَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ … ثُمَّ قَالَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ مَنْ عَالَ يَتِيماً حَتَّى يَنْقَطِعَ يُتْمُهُ أَوْ يَسْتَغْنِيَ بِنَفْسِهِ أَوْجَبَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَهُ الْجَنَّةَ كَمَا أَوْجَبَ النَّارَ لِمَنْ أَكَلَ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ajlan Abu Salih

text.en: I asked him about consuming an orphan's property. He said: It is as God has said. Then he said, without my asking him: Whoever cares for an orphan until his orphanhood ends or he becomes self-sufficient, God makes Paradise binding for him, as He made the Fire binding for whoever consumes an orphan's property.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: لما أسري بي إلى السماء رأيت قوماً تقذف في أجوافهم النار وتخرج من أدبارهم، فقلت من هؤلاء يا جبرائيل؟ فقال هؤلاء الذين يأكلون أموال اليتامى ظلماً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When I was taken up to heaven I saw a people into whose bellies fire was hurled and it came out of their backs. I said: Who are these, Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who consume the property of orphans wrongfully.

perspectives.en: Verse seven's general wording divides the traditions. Al-Tabrisi holds that since God ordained a share for men and a share for women, the doctrine of the agnatic residuaries collapses, and that the wording reaches the relatives by the womb, who are among those men and women; he notes that Abu Hanifa holds this too [9]. Al-Razi reports his companions' reply in two parts: 'a share ordained' means a fixed portion, and by consensus the relatives by the womb have no fixed portion, so they are not included in this verse; and the nearest kin are none but the parents and the children, so this text does not take them in [76].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ومن هناك تظهر نكتة توجيه الخطاب إلى الناس دون المؤمنين خاصة وكذا تعليق التقوى بربهم دون أن يقال اتقوا الله ونحوه

sources.gloss: From here appears the point of directing the address to mankind rather than to the believers in particular, and of attaching the wariness to their Lord rather than saying 'be wary of Allah' and the like.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الأيات تتمة التهميد والتوطئة التي وضعت في أول السورة لبيان أحكام المواريث وعمدة أحكام التزويج كعدد النساء وتعيين المحارم وهذان البابان من أكبر أبواب القوانين الحاكمة في المجتمع الإنساني وأعظمها

sources.gloss: These verses complete the ground laid at the head of the surah for setting out the rulings of inheritance and the main rulings of marriage, such as the number of wives and the naming of forbidden degrees; and these two chapters are among the largest and greatest chapters of the law governing human society.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان شروع في تشريع أحكام الإرث بعد تمهيد ما مهدت من المقدمات وقد قدم بيان جملي لحكم الإرث من قبيل ضرب القاعدة لإيذان أن لا حرمان في الإرث بعد ثبوت الولادة أو القرابة

sources.gloss: This begins the legislation of the rulings of inheritance after the prefaces already laid down; a summary statement of the ruling of inheritance is put first, by way of laying down a rule, to announce that there is no exclusion from inheritance once birth or kinship is established.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال أبو علي: من نصب الأرحام احتمل انتصابه وجهين: أحدهما: أن يكون معطوفاً على موضع الجار والمجرور، والآخر: أن يكون معطوفاً على اتقوا وتقديره: واتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام فَصِلوها ولا تقطعوها

sources.gloss: Abu Ali said: whoever reads 'blood relations' in the accusative, its accusative admits two constructions. One is that it is coordinated with the position of the prepositional phrase; the other is that it is coordinated with 'be wary', the sense being: be wary of Allah and be wary of blood relations, so join them and do not sever them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقد روي أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية كرهوا مخالطة اليتامى، فشقّ ذلك عليهم فشكوا ذلك إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأنزل الله سبحانه: { ويسألونك عن اليتامى قل إصلاح لهم خير وإن تخالطوهم فإخوانكم في الدين } [البقرة: 220] الآية عن الحسن وهو المروي عن السيدين الباقر ع والصادق ع

sources.gloss: It is narrated that when this verse came down they disliked mingling with orphans, and that weighed on them, so they complained of it to the Messenger of Allah, and Allah sent down: 'They ask you concerning the orphans. Say: It is better to set right their affairs, and if you intermingle with them, they are your brethren' (2:220) - on the authority of al-Hasan, and it is what is narrated from the two masters al-Baqir and al-Sadiq.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وثالثها: أنها عام في كل سفيه من صبي أو مجنون أو محجور عليه للتبذير وقريب منه ما روي عن أبي عبد الله ع أنه قال: إن السفيه شارب الخمر ومن جرى مجراه

sources.gloss: The third: that it is general for every fool, whether a child, or a madman, or one interdicted for squandering; and near to it is what is narrated from Abu Abdillah, that he said: the fool is the wine-drinker and whoever runs his course.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال أصحابنا: حد البلوغ إما كمال خمس عشرة سنة أو بلوغ النكاح أو الإنبات

sources.gloss: Our companions said: the limit of maturity is either the completion of fifteen years, or reaching the age of marriage, or the growth of hair.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذه الآية تدلّ على بطلان القول بالعصبة لأن الله تعالى فرض الميراث للرجال وللنساء فلو جاز منع النساء من الميراث في موضع لجاز أن يجري الرجال مجراهُنَّ في المنع من الميراث وتدل أيضاً على أن ذوي الأرحام يرثون لأنهم من جملة النساء والرجال الذين مات عنهم الأقربون على ما ذهبنا إليه وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة أيضاً

sources.gloss: This verse shows the invalidity of the doctrine of the agnatic residuaries, because Allah ordained inheritance for men and for women; were it permissible to bar women from inheritance in any case, it would be permissible for men to be treated as they are and barred as well. It also shows that the relatives by the womb inherit, because they are among the women and men whose near kin have died, as we hold, and it is Abu Hanifa's school too.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وحذر من قطع الارحام لما أراد من الوصية بالاولاد والنساء والضعفاء، فأعلمهم انهم جميعاً من نفس واحدة

sources.gloss: He warned against severing blood ties because of the charge He intended concerning children, women and the weak, so He informed them that they are all from a single soul.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أولها - ما روي عن عائشة انها قالت: نزلت في اليتيمة التي تكون في حجر وليها فيرغب في مالها وجمالها، ويريد أن ينكحها بدون صداق مثلها

sources.gloss: The first of them is what is narrated from Aisha, who said: it came down concerning the orphan girl who is in her guardian's care, so that he desires her wealth and her beauty and wishes to marry her for less than the dower of her like.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text:
قيل في معنى الآية أربعة أقوال:
أحدها - النهي عن الوصية بما يجحف بالورثة، ويضرّ بهم، هذا قول ابن عباس، في بعض الروايات، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، وقتادة، والسدي، والضحاك، ومجاهد.

sources.gloss: Four positions have been given on the meaning of the verse. The first is the prohibition of a bequest that damages the heirs and harms them; this is the position of Ibn Abbas in some reports, and of Said ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak and Mujahid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما علق الله تعالى الوعيد في الآية لمن يأكل أموال اليتامى ظلماً، لأنه قد يأكله على وجه الاستحقاق، بأن يأخذ منه أجرة المثل، على ما قلناه. أو يأكل منه بالمعروف على ما فسرناه، أو يأخذه قرضاً على نفسه

sources.gloss: Allah attached the threat in the verse to whoever consumes the property of orphans wrongfully, because one may consume it by entitlement, taking from it the wage that his like would earn, as we have said, or eating from it in an honourable manner, as we have explained, or taking it as a loan against himself.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فنصف الآية في أول السورة ونصفها على رأس المائة وعشرين آية، وذلك أنهم كانوا لا يستحلون أن يتزوجوا يتيمة قد ربوها فسألوا الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله عن ذلك

sources.gloss: So half of the verse stands at the head of the surah and half of it at the hundred and twentieth verse; and that is because they did not consider it lawful to marry an orphan girl they had raised, so they asked the Messenger about it.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لأن الله يقول ولا تؤتوا السفهاء أموالكم وأي سفيه أسفه من شارب الخمر

sources.gloss: Because Allah says, 'Do not give the feeble-minded your property', and what fool is more foolish than a wine-drinker?

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهي منسوخة بقوله { يوصيكم الله في أولادكم }

sources.gloss: It is abrogated by His words, 'Allah enjoins you concerning your children.'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: لما أسري بي إلى السماء رأيت قوماً تقذف في أجوافهم النار وتخرج من أدبارهم

sources.gloss: When I was taken up to heaven I saw a people into whose bellies fire was hurled and it came out of their backs.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سئل الصادق (عليه السلام) عن التقوى، فقال (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq was asked about wariness of God, and he said.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سألته عن رجل أكل مال اليتيم، هل له توبة؟

sources.gloss: I asked him about a man who consumed an orphan's property: is there repentance for him?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يعني في النفقة، وأما قوله: { وَلَن تَسْتَطِيعُوۤاْ أَن تَعْدِلُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلاَ تَمِيلُواْ كُلَّ ٱلْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ } [النساء: 129] يعني في المودة

sources.gloss: That means in maintenance; and as for His words, 'You will not be able to be just between wives, even if you are eager to. Yet do not turn away from one altogether, leaving her as if in suspense' (4:129), that means in affection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إيناس الرشد: حفظ المال

sources.gloss: Discerning maturity is the safekeeping of property.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نسختها آية الفرائض

sources.gloss: The verse of the fixed shares abrogated it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أوعد الله تبارك و تعالى في مال اليتيم عقوبتين: إحداهما عقوبة الآخرة النار، وأما عقوبة الدنيا فقوله عز وجل

sources.gloss: God has threatened two punishments concerning the orphan's property: one of them is the punishment of the hereafter, the Fire; and as for the punishment of this world, it is His words.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنه سئل عن خلق حواء وقيل له أن أناساً عندنا يقولون ان الله خلق حواء من ضلع آدم اليسرى الأقصى قال سبحان الله تعالى عن ذلك علواً كبيراً

sources.gloss: He was asked about the creation of Hawwa, and it was said to him that some people among us say that God created Hawwa from Adam's lowest left rib. He said: Glory be to God, far exalted above that.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لا يحل لماء الرجل أن يجري في أكثر من أربعة أرحام من الحراير

sources.gloss: It is not lawful for a man's seed to run in more than four wombs of free women.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أقول: نسخ الوجوب لا ينافي بقاء الجواز والاستحباب

sources.gloss: I say: the abrogation of the obligation does not negate the remaining permissibility and recommendation.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: ونحن قسم الله الذي يُسأل به ونحن وصية الله في الأولين ووصيته في الآخرين

sources.gloss: We are God's oath by which one is adjured, and we are God's testament among the first and among the last.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: وأجاب أصحابنا عنه من وجهين: أحدهما: انه تعالى قال في آخر الآية { نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً } أي نصيبا مقدرا، وبالاجماع ليس لذوي الأرحام نصيب مقدر، فثبت أنهم ليسوا داخلين في هذه الآية … وما ذاك إلا الوالدان والأولاد، فثبت أن هذا النص لا يدخل فيه ذو الأرحام

sources.gloss: Our companions answered him in two ways. The first is that He said at the end of the verse 'a share ordained', that is, a fixed portion, and by consensus the relatives by the womb have no fixed portion, so it is established that they are not included in this verse ... and that is none but the parents and the children, so it is established that this text does not take in the relatives by the womb.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: مَنْ عَالَ يَتِيماً حَتَّى يَنْقَطِعَ يُتْمُهُ أَوْ يَسْتَغْنِيَ بِنَفْسِهِ أَوْجَبَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَهُ الْجَنَّةَ كَمَا أَوْجَبَ النَّارَ لِمَنْ أَكَلَ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ

sources.gloss: Whoever cares for an orphan until his orphanhood ends or he becomes self-sufficient, God makes Paradise binding for him, just as He made the Fire binding for whoever consumes the property of an orphan.

essay.en:
‘Allah enjoins you concerning your children’ takes the dividing of an estate out of the family’s hands. Tusi reports from al-Suddi and Ibn Abbas that before this people gave nothing to women, daughters or young sons, and inherited only the man who fought [5]. Tabrisi records two occasions: Jabir ibn Abdullah asking the Prophet what to do with his property, and the widow of Abd al-Rahman, brother of Hassan the poet, whose five brothers took the estate and left her nothing [2]. Tabatabai passes on, with approval, the reading that ‘for the male shall be the like of the share of two females’ overturns that exclusion, treating the woman’s portion as the settled measure and stating the man’s by reference to it [1].

The shares then fall in order: children, parents, the mother’s third cut to a sixth when there are brothers, each portion due only after any bequest and any debt. Tusi notes that the wording seems to grant two-thirds only above two daughters, while the community holds that two take the same, so the apparent sense is set aside [5]; Fayd Kashani reports al-Kafi deriving their two-thirds from the phrase itself [14]. Verse 12 turns to husband and wife, then to the one inherited by siblings.

The last two verses gather all of it under one name. Tabrisi reads ‘Allah’s bounds’ as God’s own detailing of what He has made obligatory, the line dividing obedience from disobedience [4], and a garden and a fire hang on which side of it a man stands.

note.en: The verse says ‘children’, not ‘sons’: Tabatabai reads the two-to-one share as belonging to those the deceased fathered directly, while grandchildren take the rank of the parent through whom they connect [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن فاطمة (صلوات الله عليها) انطلقت إلى أبي بكر فطلبت ميراثها من نبي الله (صلى الله عليه وآله)، فقال: إن نبي الله لا يورث، فقالت: أكفرت بالله وكذبت بكتابه؟ قال الله: { يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيۤ أَوْلَٰدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلأُنْثَيَيْنِ }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Jamila al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from some of his companions, from one of the two Imams

text.en: Fatimah went to Abu Bakr and asked for her inheritance from the Prophet of God. He said: the Prophet of God is not inherited from. She said: have you disbelieved in God and denied His Book? God said: ‘Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male shall be the like of the share of two females.’

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: قلت له: جعلت فداك، كيف صار الرجل إذا مات وولده من القرابة سواء، ترث النساء نصف ميراث الرجال، وهن أضعف من الرجال، وأقل حيلة؟ … لأن الله تبارك وتعالى فضل الرجال على النساء درجة، ولأن النساء يرجعن عيالا على الرجال
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: I said: how is it that when a man dies and his children are equal in kinship, women inherit half the inheritance of men, when they are weaker and have less means? He said: because God favoured men over women by a degree, and because women revert as dependents upon men.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما بال المرأة المسكينة الضعيفة تأخذ سهما واحدا، ويأخذ الرجل سهمين؟ … إن المرأة ليس عليها جهاد ولا نفقة ولا معقلة، فإنما ذلك على الرجل، فلذلك جعل للمرأة سهما و للرجل سهمين
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham and Hammad, from al-Ahwal

text.en: Ibn Abi al-Awja said to me: what is the matter with the poor weak woman, that she takes one share and the man takes two? One of our companions put that to him, and he said: no jihad, no maintenance and no blood money lie upon the woman; those are upon the man.

note.en: Tusi holds the kalala are the brothers and sisters: those named in this verse are from the mother’s side, while those at the end of the surah are from the father and mother, or the father [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في زوج وأبوين، قال: " للزوج النصف، وللام الثلث، وللأب ما بقي ". وقال في امرأة وأبوين، قال: " للمرأة الربع وللام الثلث، وما بقي للأب "
narrations.chain: al-Shaykh in al-Tahdhib, by his isnad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar

text.en: On a husband and two parents, he said: for the husband a half, for the mother a third, and for the father what remains. And on a wife and two parents, he said: for the wife a quarter, for the mother a third, and what remains for the father.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله أدخل الزوج والمرأة على جميع أهل المواريث، فلم ينقصهما من الربع والثمن
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Salim al-Ashall

text.en: God brought the husband and the wife in upon all the people of inheritance, and did not reduce them below the quarter and the eighth.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أنكم تقرؤون في هذه الآية الوصية قبل الدين وأن رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم قضى بالدين قبل الوصية

text.en: You recite in this verse the bequest before the debt, yet the Messenger of God ruled the debt before the bequest.

note.en: Fayd Kashani takes ‘these’ to point back over all the preceding rulings, on orphans, bequests and inheritance alike, and reads God’s bounds as His delimited laws, which may not be overstepped [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: مَنْ يُطِعِ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يَكُنْ سَبِيلُ الرَّشَادِ سَبِيلَهُ وَنُورُ التَّقْوَى دَلِيلَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُخْطِئِ السَّدَادَ كُلَّهُ وَلَنْ يَضُرَّ إِلا نَفْسَهُ
narrations.chain: Ahmad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Harith, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Whoever obeys God and His Messenger, the path of right guidance becomes his path and the light of piety his guide. Whoever disobeys God and His Messenger misses soundness altogether, and harms none but himself.

note.en: Tabrisi rejects the reading that this threatens every grave sinner with the Fire for ever: ‘transgresses the bounds’ names the man who oversteps all of God’s bounds, and that is the description of the disbelievers [4].

narrations.speaker: The Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: وقد أبلغتكم ما أرسلت به إليكم في علي، فمن أطاعني فيه فقد أطاع الله، ومن عصاني فيه فقد عصى الله عز وجل، ولا حجة له عند الله عز وجل، وكان مصيره إلى ما قال الله عز وجل في كتابه: (ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده يدخله نارا خالدا فيها)
narrations.chain: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Said al-Hashimi, from Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Zahir, from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Abdi, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Wasiti, from Muhammad ibn Rabia, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas

text.en: Whoever obeys me regarding Ali has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me regarding him has disobeyed God and has no plea before God; his end is what God said in His Book: ‘whoever disobeys Allah and His Apostle and transgresses the bounds set by Allah, He shall make him enter a Fire.’

perspectives.en: Both traditions read these shares as fixed, yet they divide differently when a woman dies leaving a husband and both parents. In al-Burhan, al-Baqir gives the husband a half, the mother a full third, and the father what remains [11]; Tusi adds that the parents are never reduced below their two sixths, since proportional reduction is void [6]. Qurtubi records the other course: Ibn Abbas put that same case to Zayd ibn Thabit, who gave the husband a half and the mother a third of what remains, and when pressed said he held it by his own opinion, not from the Book [22].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ففي انتخاب هذا التعبير إشعار بإبطال ما كانت عليه الجاهلية من منع توريث النساء فكأنه جعل إرث الأنثى مقرراً معروفاً وأخبر بأن للذكر مثله مرتين

sources.gloss: In the choice of this expression there is an intimation of the abolition of what the Jahiliyya held, barring women from inheriting; it is as though the female's inheritance were made settled and known, and He announced that the male has twice the like of it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: مرضت فعادني رسول الله وأبو بكر وهما يمشيان فأُغمي عليّ، فدعا بماء، فتوضأ، ثم صبّه عليّ فأفقت فقلت: يا رسول الله كيف أصنع في مالي؟ فسكت رسول الله فنزلت آية المواريث فيّ … نزلت في عبد الرحمن أخي حسان الشاعر وذلك أنه مات وترك امرأة وخمسة إخوان فجاءت الورثة فأخذوا ماله ولم يعطوا امرأَته شيئاً

sources.gloss: I fell ill and the Messenger of God and Abu Bakr visited me on foot. I fainted, so he called for water, performed ablution, then poured it over me and I came to. I said: Messenger of God, how shall I deal with my property? He was silent, and the verse of inheritance came down about me. And it is said: it came down about Abd al-Rahman, brother of Hassan the poet, who died leaving a wife and five brothers; the heirs came and took his property and gave his wife nothing.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وثالثها: تلك تفصيلات الله لفرائضه وهو الأَقوى فيكون المراد هذه القسمة التي قسمها الله لكم والفرائض التي فرضها الله لأَحيائكم من أمواتكم فصول بين طاعة الله ومعصيته … قولـه ويتعد حدوده يدلُّ على أن المراد به من تعدى جميع حدود الله وهذه صفة الكفار

sources.gloss: The third view: these are God's detailings of what He has made obligatory, and it is the strongest; so what is meant is this division that God has apportioned for you and the shares He has ordained for your living from your dead, separations between obedience to God and disobedience to Him. ... His saying 'and transgresses His bounds' shows that what is meant is one who transgresses all of God's bounds, and this is the description of the disbelievers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال السدي، وابن عباس: إن سبب نزولها، أن القوم لم يكونوا يورثون النساء والبنات والبنين الصغار، ولم يورثوا إلا من قاتل وطاعن … لكن أجمعت الأمة أن حكم البنتين حكم من زاد عليهما من البنات، فتركنا له الظاهر

sources.gloss: Al-Suddi and Ibn Abbas said: the reason for its revelation is that the people would not give inheritance to women, daughters or young sons, and gave it only to one who fought and thrust the spear. ... But the community has agreed that the ruling of two daughters is the ruling of those beyond two, so we set aside the apparent sense for it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعندنا أن الكلالة هم الاخوة والأخوات، فمن ذكر في هذه الآية هو من كان من قبل الأم، ومن ذكر في آخر السورة فهو من قبل الأب والأم، أو من قبل الأب … وكذلك الأبوان لا ينقصان في حال من الأحوال من السدسين، لأن العول عندنا باطل

sources.gloss: In our view the kalala are the brothers and sisters: those mentioned in this verse are from the mother's side, and those mentioned at the end of the surah are from the father and mother, or from the father. ... Likewise the two parents are in no case reduced below the two sixths, because proportional reduction is void in our view.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن فاطمة (صلوات الله عليها) انطلقت إلى أبي بكر فطلبت ميراثها من نبي الله (صلى الله عليه وآله)، فقال: إن نبي الله لا يورث، فقالت: أكفرت بالله وكذبت بكتابه؟

sources.gloss: Fatimah went to Abu Bakr and asked for her inheritance from the Prophet of God. He said: the Prophet of God is not inherited from. She said: have you disbelieved in God and denied His Book?

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: للزوج النصف، وللام الثلث، وللأب ما بقي

sources.gloss: For the husband a half, for the mother a third, and for the father what remains.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنكم تقرؤون في هذه الآية الوصية قبل الدين وأن رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم قضى بالدين قبل الوصية

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from Amir al-Muminin: you recite in this verse the bequest before the debt, yet the Messenger of God ruled the debt before the bequest.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: { تِلْكَ } إشارة الى ما تقدم من الاحكام في أمر اليتامى والوصايا والمواريث { حُدُودُ اللهِ } شرائعه المحدودة التي لا يجوز تجاوزها

sources.gloss: 'These' points to the rulings that preceded on the matter of orphans, bequests and inheritances; 'the bounds of God' are His delimited laws, which it is not permitted to overstep.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فقلنا ان الله جعل حظ الانثيين الثلثين بقوله للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين وذلك أنّه إذا ترك الرجل بنتاً وإبناً فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين وهو الثلثان فحظ الانثيين الثلثان

sources.gloss: So we said: God made the share of two females two-thirds by His saying 'for the male the like of the share of two females'; for when a man leaves a daughter and a son, the male has the like of the share of two females, which is two-thirds, so the share of two females is two-thirds.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أرسل ابن عباس إلى زيد بن ثابت يسأله عن ٱمرأة تركت زوجها وأبويها. قال: للزوج النصف، وللأُمّ ثلث ما بقي. فقال: تجده في كتاب الله أو تقوله برأي؟ قال: أقوله برأي لا أفضل أُمّا على أبٍ

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas sent to Zayd ibn Thabit asking him about a woman who left her husband and her two parents. He said: for the husband a half, and for the mother a third of what remains. He said: do you find it in the Book of God, or do you say it by opinion? He said: I say it by opinion; I do not prefer a mother over a father.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فمن أطاعني فيه فقد أطاع الله، ومن عصاني فيه فقد عصى الله عز وجل

sources.gloss: So whoever obeys me regarding him has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me regarding him has disobeyed God, the Mighty and Majestic.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: مَنْ يُطِعِ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يَكُنْ سَبِيلُ الرَّشَادِ سَبِيلَهُ وَنُورُ التَّقْوَى دَلِيلَهُ

sources.gloss: Whoever obeys God and His Messenger, the path of right guidance becomes his path and the light of piety his guide.

essay.en:
The passage opens on a penalty, pauses over repentance, and ends by closing a door that the Jahiliyya had left open.

Verses 15 and 16 give the first Medinan ruling on indecency. Tabrisi reports that the commentators are agreed the indecency meant here is fornication [4]. Tabatabai observes that the confinement is made to rest on the testimony rather than on the act being established, so that a woman known to have done it but not testified against is left alone, and he counts this among God's favours to the community [1]. The words "or Allah decrees a course for them" already look past themselves, and Tusi reports that most commentators hold the ruling abrogated by stoning for the married and flogging for the unmarried, as is related from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq [9]. The chastisement of verse 16 was not simply cancelled, he adds: the offender is still rebuked and blamed, and what lapsed was stopping there [10].

Verses 17 and 18 turn to the door behind every penalty. God accepts the repentance of those who do evil out of ignorance and repent promptly, which Tabrisi glosses as before death, since what lies between a person and death is near [5]. Verse 18 shuts that door on the man who waits until death is in the room. Tusi records the agreement of the exegetes that it takes in the disobedient among the people of prayer, and rejects the reading that confines it to hypocrites [12].

From verse 19 the surah returns to women. Tabrisi reports from Muqatil that it came down when Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died and his son threw his garment over the widow, Kubaysha bint Ma'n, thereby inheriting the marriage, and that the like is related from al-Baqir [6]. Tabatabai calls "Consort with them in an honourable manner" a Quranic foundation for the social life of the woman [3]. Verses 20 and 21 forbid taking back any of the dower from a wife a husband has tired of and wants gone [7]. Verse 22 then ends the practice at its root: the woman the father married is not the son's to marry.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هذه منسوخة، والسبيل هو الحدود
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: This one is abrogated, and the course is the prescribed penalties.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كانت المرأة إذا فجرت، فقام عليها أربعة شهود، ادخلت بيتا ولم تحدث، ولم تكلم، ولم تجالس، وأوتيت فيه بطعامها وشرابها حتى تموت … جعل السبيل الجلد، والرجم، والإمساك في البيوت
narrations.chain: from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: When a woman fornicated and four witnesses stood against her, she was put in a house; she was not spoken to, not addressed, not sat with, and her food and drink were brought to her there until she died. The course He appointed is flogging, stoning and confinement in the houses.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يعني البكر إذا أتت الفاحشة التي أتتها هذه الثيب { فَآذُوهُمَا } - قال- تحبس
narrations.chain: from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: This means the unmarried woman, when she commits the indecency that the married woman committed. As for "chastise them both", he said: she is confined.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كل ذنب عمله العبد وإن كان عالماً فهو جاهل حين خاطر بنفسه في معصية ربه

text.en: Every sin a servant commits, even if he knows better, he commits as one ignorant, since he gambled with himself in disobeying his Lord.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: كلما عاد المؤمن بالاستغفار والتوبة عاد الله عليه بالمغفرة، وإن الله غفور رحيم، يقبل التوبة ويعفو عن السيئات، فإياك أن تقنط المؤمنين من رحمة الله
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Whenever the believer comes back with asking forgiveness and repenting, God comes back to him with forgiveness. God is all-forgiving, all-merciful; He accepts repentance and pardons misdeeds. So beware of making the believers despair of God's mercy.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أنه قيل له فان عاد وتاب مراراً قال يغفر الله له قيل إلى متى قال حتى يكون الشيطان هو المحسور

text.en: He was asked: and if he goes back to it and repents, again and again? He said: God forgives him. It was said: until when? He said: until it is Satan who is worn out.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: من تاب قبل موته بسنة تاب الله عليه … وإن الساعة لكثيرة، ومن تاب [قبل موته] وقد بلغت روحه هذه- و أهوى بيده إلى حلقه- تاب الله عليه
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh in al-Faqih, from the Messenger of God

text.en: Whoever repents a year before his death, God turns to him ... and an hour is much: whoever repents when his spirit has reached here, and he pointed with his hand to his throat, God turns to him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ذلك إذا عاين أمر الآخرة

text.en: He was asked about this verse and said: that is when he beholds the matter of the hereafter.

note.en: Tusi prefers reading "a gross indecency" here of every act of disobedience, since the general wording requires it, and reports the same from al-Baqir [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الرجل تكون في حجره اليتيمة فيمنعها من التزويج ليرثها بما تكون قريبة له … الرجل تكون له المرأة فيضربها حتى تفتدي منه، فنهى الله عن ذلك
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A man has an orphan girl in his care and keeps her from marrying so as to inherit from her, since she is a relative of his. And of pressing them: a man has a wife and beats her until she ransoms herself from him; God forbade that.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فإنه كان في الجاهلية في أول ما أسلموا من قبائل العرب إذا مات حميم الرجل وله امرأة ألقى الرجل ثوبه عليها، فورث نكاحها بصداق حميمه الذي كان أصدقها، يرث نكاحها كما يرث ماله
narrations.chain: Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: In the Jahiliyya, and at the beginning of Islam among the Arab tribes, when a man's kinsman died leaving a wife, he would throw his garment over her and inherit the marriage for the dower his kinsman had paid, inheriting the marriage as he inherited the property.

note.en: Tusi notes that taking a wife's property is forbidden in every case; the exchange was singled out because one might imagine the second wife takes what the first was given [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن جاز مهر السنة فليس هذا مهرا، إنما هو نحل، لأن الله يقول: { وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَاراً فَلاَ تَأْخُذُواْ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً } إنما عنى النحل ولم يعن المهر … إن مهر المؤمنات خمس مائة، و هو مهر السنة
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: If it passes the dower of the sunnah, this is not a dower but a gift; God meant the gift and not the dower when He said that nothing is to be taken back from a quintal. The dower of believing women is five hundred, and that is the dower of the sunnah.

note.en: Tusi gives four readings of the solemn covenant; the first, related from al-Baqir, is "retaining in honour or release with kindness" [15], reported in Majma al-Bayan as the pledge taken at the contract [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الميثاق هي الكلمة التي عقد بها النكاح، وأما قوله: { غَلِيظاً } فهو ماء الرجل يفضيه إلى امرأته
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub, from Burayd, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The covenant is the word by which the marriage was contracted. As for His saying "solemn", that is the man's seed which he conveys to his wife.

note.en: Tusi: every woman the father contracted is forbidden to the son, whether the father consummated the marriage or not, without dispute [16].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لَوْ لَمْ يَحْرُمْ عَلَى النَّاسِ أَزْوَاجُ النَّبِيِّ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) لِقَوْلِ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَما كانَ لَكُمْ أَنْ تُؤْذُوا رَسُولَ اللهِ وَلا أَنْ تَنْكِحُوا أَزْواجَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ أَبَداً حَرُمْنَ عَلَى الْحَسَنِ وَالْحُسَيْنِ (عَلَيْهِما السَّلام) لِقَوْلِ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ وَلا يَصْلُحُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَنْكِحَ امْرَأَةَ جَدِّه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two

text.en: Had the wives of the Prophet not been forbidden to people by God's words, "nor may you ever marry his wives after him", they would have been forbidden to al-Hasan and al-Husayn by His words, "Do not marry any of the women whom your fathers had married." A man may not marry his grandfather's wife.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: يا علي إن عبدالمطلب سن في الجاهية خمس سنن أجارها الله له في الاسلام، حرم نساء الآباء على الابناء فأنزل الله عز وجل "ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء"
narrations.chain: from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Prophet

text.en: O Ali, Abd al-Muttalib set five practices in the Jahiliyya which God confirmed for him in Islam. He forbade the wives of fathers to sons, and God sent down, "Do not marry any of the women whom your fathers had married."

perspectives.en: Whether God is bound to accept repentance divides the readings. Tabatabai holds that He has bound himself: He promised to accept the repentance of whoever repents and does not break His promise, so acceptance is owed, though nothing outside Him imposes it [2]. Qurtubi denies any such obligation by reason, reading "on Allah" as on His grace and mercy, and says that when a servant repents God is at liberty to accept or not [42]. Razi puts it flatly: the claim of an obligation upon God is void [48].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: رتب الإمساك - وهو الحبس المخلد على الشهادة لا على أصل تحقق الفاحشة وإن علم به إذا لم يشهد عليه الشهود وهو من منن الله سبحانه على الأُمة من حيث السماحة والإِغماض

sources.gloss: The confinement is made to rest on the testimony, not on the indecency being established, even if it is known, so long as the witnesses do not testify to it; and this is among God's favours upon the community, in leniency and overlooking.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بل على أنه تعالى وعد عباده أن يقبل توبة التائب منهم وهو لا يخلف الميعاد فهذا معنى وجوب قبول التوبة على الله

sources.gloss: Rather, He has promised His servants that He will accept the repentance of whoever among them repents, and He does not break His promise; this is the meaning of God being bound to accept repentance.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فإنه أصل قرآني لحياة المرأة الاجتماعية

sources.gloss: It is a Quranic foundation for the social life of the woman.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فإنهم أجمعوا على أن المراد بالفاحشة هنا الزنى

sources.gloss: For they are agreed that what is meant by the indecency here is fornication.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ومعنى: { يتوبون من قريب } أي يتوبون قبل الموت لأَن ما بين الإِنسان وبين الموت قريب

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'they repent promptly' is that they repent before death, for what lies between a person and death is near.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل: إن أبا قيس بن الأَسلت لما مات عن زوجته كبيشة بنت معن ألقى ابنه محصن بن أبي قيس ثوبه عليها فورث نكاحها

sources.gloss: It is said that when Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died leaving his wife Kubaysha bint Ma'n, his son Muhsin ibn Abi Qays threw his garment over her and so inherited the marriage.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي لا ترجعوا فيما أعطيتموهُنَّ من المهر إذا كرهتموهن وأردتم طلاقهن … أن الميثاق الغليظ هو العهد المأخوذ على الزوج حالة العقد من إمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان

sources.gloss: That is, do not take back any of the dower you gave them when you dislike them and want to divorce them ... The solemn covenant is the pledge taken upon the husband at the contract, to retain in honour or release with kindness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ثم نسخ ذلك بالرجم في المحصنين، والجلد في البكرين … وأن هذا الحكم منسوخ، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر (ع) وأبي عبد الله (ع)

sources.gloss: Then that was abrogated by stoning for the married and flogging for the unmarried ... and that this ruling is abrogated, which is what is related from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فأما الأذى المذكور في الآية، فليس بمنسوخ، فان الزاني يؤذى ويعنف، ويوبخ على فعله، ويذم … وإنما نسخ الاقتصار عليه

sources.gloss: As for the chastisement mentioned in the verse, it is not abrogated, for the fornicator is chastised, rebuked, blamed for his act and censured ... what was abrogated was confining the penalty to it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وأجمع أهل التأويل على أن الآية تناولت عصاة أهل الصلاة، إلا ما حكي عن الربيع أنه قال: إنها في المنافقين، وهذا غلط لأن المنافقين كفار

sources.gloss: The people of interpretation are agreed that the verse takes in the disobedient among the people of prayer, except for what is reported from al-Rabi, who said it is about the hypocrites, and this is a mistake, for the hypocrites are unbelievers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والأولى حمل الآية على كل معصية، لأن العموم يقتضي ذلك، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر (ع)

sources.gloss: It is better to carry the verse on every act of disobedience, since the general wording requires it, and this is what is related from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فانما خص الله تعالى الاستبدال بالنهي، لأن مع الاستبدال قد يتوهم جواز الاسترجاع، من حيث أن الثانية تقوم مقام الأولى

sources.gloss: God singled out the exchange for the prohibition only because with an exchange one might imagine that taking it back is allowed, since the second wife stands in the place of the first.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قيل في معناه أربعة أقوال: أحدهما - قال الحسن، وابن سيرين، والضحاك، وقتادة، والسدي، والفراء، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر (ع) أنه قوله: { فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان }

sources.gloss: Four readings are given of its meaning. The first: al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, Qatada, al-Suddi and al-Farra said, and it is what is related from Abu Jafar, that it is His saying 'retaining in honour or release with kindness'.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكل من عقد عليها الأب من النساء تحرم على الابن، دخل بها الأب، أو لم يدخل، بلا خلاف

sources.gloss: Every woman the father contracted is forbidden to the son, whether the father consummated the marriage or not, without dispute.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هذه منسوخة، والسبيل هو الحدود

sources.gloss: This one is abrogated, and 'the course' is the prescribed penalties.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كلما عاد المؤمن بالاستغفار والتوبة عاد الله عليه بالمغفرة

sources.gloss: Whenever the believer returns with asking forgiveness and repentance, God returns to him with forgiveness.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الرجل تكون في حجره اليتيمة فيمنعها من التزويج ليرثها بما تكون قريبة له

sources.gloss: A man has an orphan girl in his care and keeps her from marrying so as to inherit from her, since she is a relative of his.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الميثاق هي الكلمة التي عقد بها النكاح

sources.gloss: The covenant is the word by which the marriage was contracted.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: حتى يكون الشيطان هو المحسور

sources.gloss: Until it is Satan who is worn out.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ذلك إذا عاين أمر الآخرة

sources.gloss: That is when he beholds the matter of the hereafter.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وإذا تاب العبد فالله سبحانه بالخيار إن شاء قبلها، وإن شاء لم يقبلها

sources.gloss: When the servant repents, God is at liberty: if He wills He accepts it, and if He wills He does not accept it.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: واعلم أن القول بالوجوب على الله باطل

sources.gloss: Know that the claim of an obligation upon God is void.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: حرم نساء الآباء على الابناء فأنزل الله عز وجل "ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء"

sources.gloss: He forbade the wives of fathers to sons, and God sent down, 'Do not marry any of the women whom your fathers had married.'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: وَلا يَصْلُحُ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَنْكِحَ امْرَأَةَ جَدِّه

sources.gloss: A man may not marry his grandfather's wife.

essay.en:
The sura has been legislating for households; here it draws the boundary line. Verse 23 names the women a man may never marry: seven through birth, then ties made by suckling, then those made by marriage - a wife's mother, a stepdaughter, a son's wife - and last the two sisters no man may hold at once. Tabatabai reads the verses as setting out every marriage prohibition without exception or qualification, which is why "As to others than these, it is lawful for you" follows [1]. Tabrisi notes that prohibition never attaches to persons, only to acts, so what is meant is the contract of marriage with them [2]. On the stepdaughter clause Tusi is blunt: whoever says she is forbidden only if she was raised in his house has erred [5].

Verse 24 closes the list with married women, then turns outward: seek with your wealth, "in wedlock, not in license". The readers agree on the vowel here, and al-muhsanat means women secured by husbands [3]; Tusi holds the strongest reading of the exception to be captive women who had husbands, citing Ali, Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas [6]. The dowry is owed, and whatever the two settle on afterwards is no sin.

Verse 25 lowers the threshold for the man who cannot reach it, tying the concession to faith rather than rank: "you are all [on a] similar [footing]". It ends on restraint: "it is better that you be continent".

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فالخوارج زعمت أن الرجل إذا كانت لأهله بنت ولم يربها ولم تكن في حجره حلت له لقول الله: { واللاتي في حجوركم } قال الصادق عليه السلام لا تحل له

text.en: The Khawarij claimed that if a man's wife has a daughter whom he did not raise and who was not in his care, she is lawful for him, citing "who are under your care". Al-Sadiq said: She is not lawful for him.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: إذا تزوج الرجل المرأة حرمت عليه ابنتها إذا دخل بالام فإذا لم يدخل بالام فلا بأس ان يتزوج بالابنة وإذا تزوج الابنة فدخل بها أو لم يدخل بها فقد حرمت عليه الأم وقال الربائب حرام كن في الحجر أولم يكنّ

text.en: If a man marries a woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him once he has gone in to the mother; if he has not, there is no harm in his marrying the daughter. If he marries the daughter, the mother is forbidden whether or not he goes in to her. Stepdaughters are forbidden, in his care or not.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.addressee: a group of the people of Iraq
narrations.arabic: فيقول الله عز و جل في آية التحريم: { حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَٰتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمْ } إلى آخرها فأخبروني هل تصلح ابنتي أو ابنة ابنتي و ما تناسل من صلبي لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أن يتزوجها لو كان حيا؟ قالوا: لا. … ففي هذا بيان أننا من آله و لستم من آله، و إلا لحرمت عليه بناتكم كما حرمت عليه بناتي، لأنا من آله و أنتم من أمته
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Muaddib and Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Jafar al-Himyari, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt

text.en: God says in the verse of prohibition, "Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters and your sisters." Tell me: could the Messenger of Allah have married my daughter, were he alive? They said no. In this is proof that we are of his family and you are not.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في الفقيه والعياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام هن ذوات الأزواج

text.en: They are women who have husbands.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال الصادق عليه السلام: { فما استمتعتم به منهن - إلى أجل مسمى - فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة } قال الصادق عليه السلام فهذه الآية دليل على المتعة

text.en: "For the enjoyment you have had from them - to a stated term - give them their dowries, by way of settlement." Al-Sadiq said: This verse is proof of temporary marriage.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لا بأس بأن تزيدها وتزيدك إذا انقطع الأجل فيما بينكما تقول استحللتك بأجل آخر برضى منها ولا تحل لغيرك حتى تنقضي عدتها وعدتها حيضتان

text.en: There is no harm in your adding for her and her adding for you when the term between you has run out. You say: I have made you lawful to me for a further term, with her consent. She is not lawful to another until her waiting period ends, and it is two menstrual cycles.

note.en: Tawl is wealth, the view of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada, and what is reported from Abu Jafar [4]. Tusi reads "faithful slave-women" as barring marriage to a slave-woman of the People of the Book [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَ الرَّجُلُ الْحُرُّ الْمَمْلُوكَةَ الْيَوْمَ إِنَّمَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ حَيْثُ قَالَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلا وَالطَّوْلُ الْمَهْرُ وَمَهْرُ الْحُرَّةِ الْيَوْمَ مَهْرُ الأمَةِ أَوْ أَقَلُّ.
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It is not fitting today that a free man marry a slave-woman. That was only when God said, "As for those of you who cannot afford." Tawl is the dowry, and the dowry of a free woman today is the dowry of a slave-woman, or less.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه سئل يتزوج الرجل بالامة بغير علم أهلها قال هو زنا ان الله تعالى يقول { فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ }

text.en: He was asked about a man marrying a slave-woman without her people's knowledge. He said: That is fornication. God says, "So marry them with their masters' permission."

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال الصادق عليه السلام وإنما صار يقتل في الثامنة لأن الله رحمه أن يجمع عليه ربق الرق وحد الحر

text.en: He is put to death on the eighth occasion only because God had mercy on him, that the yoke of slavery and the penalty of a free man should not be gathered upon him.

perspectives.en: On "married women, excepting your slave-women" al-Tabari reports that the people of interpretation differed, and that those who read the clause of captive women argued from the reports that the verse came down about the captives of Awtas [16]. Al-Qurtubi names that reading as the position of Ibn Abbas, Abu Qilaba, Ibn Zayd, Makhul, al-Zuhri and Abu Said al-Khudri, with Shafi'i holding that captivity itself cuts the marriage bond [21]. Tusi holds the same sense strongest, ascribing it to Ali, Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas, but records that its opponents weakened the Awtas report, since those captives were idolaters who had entered Islam [6].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وبالجملة جملة الآيات متضمنة لبيان كل محرم نكاحي من غير تخصيص أو تقييد وهو الظاهر من قوله تعالى بعد تعداد المحرمات { وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم } الآية

sources.gloss: In sum, the verses set out every marriage prohibition without exception or qualification, and this is plain from His words after listing them, "As to others than these, it is lawful for you".

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لا بُدَّ فيه من محذوف لأن التحريم لا يتعلق بالأعيان وإنما يتعلق بأفعال المكلف ثم يختلف باختلاف ما أضيف إليه فإذا أضيف إلى مأكول نحو قولـه: { حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم } [المائدة: 3] فالمراد الأكل، وإذا أضيف إلى النساء فالمراد العقد، فالتقدير حُرِّم عليكم نكاح أمهاتكم

sources.gloss: There must be an elided word here, for prohibition does not attach to physical things but to the acts of the one under obligation; it varies with what it is joined to. Joined to something edible, as in "Forbidden to you are carrion and blood", eating is meant; joined to women, the marriage contract is meant, so the sense is: forbidden to you is marriage with your mothers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقع الاتفاق على فتح العين من قولـه: { والمحصنات } في هذه الآية ومعناها النساء اللاتي أحصنَّ بالأزواج

sources.gloss: There is agreement on the fatha in "al-muhsanat" in this verse, and its meaning is women who have been secured by husbands.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي لم يجد منكم غنى عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع

sources.gloss: That is, whoever of you does not find wealth: from Ibn Abbas, Said ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatada and al-Suddi, and it is what is reported from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فمن قال: إنه لا تحرم بنت الزوجة إلا إذا تربت في حجره فقد أخطأ على ما قلناه

sources.gloss: So whoever says that the wife's daughter is forbidden only if she was raised in his house has erred, according to what we have said.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدها - وهو الأقوى - ما قاله علي (ع)، وابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وأبو قلابة، وابن زيد، عن أبيه، ومكحول، والزهري، والجبائي: أن المراد به ذوات الأزواج إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم، من سبي من كان لها زوج. وقال بعضهم، مستدلا على ذلك بخبر أبي سعيد الخدري، أن الآية نزلت في سبي أوطاس، ومن خالفهم ضعف هذا الخبر بأن سبي أوطاس كانوا عبدة الأوثان، دخلوا في الاسلام.

sources.gloss: The first, which is the strongest, is what Ali, Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Qilaba, Ibn Zayd from his father, Makhul, al-Zuhri and al-Jubbai said: that what is meant is women who have husbands, excepting those your right hands own from the captives who had a husband. Some argued for this from the report of Abu Said al-Khudri that the verse came down about the captives of Awtas, and their opponents weakened this report, since the captives of Awtas were idol-worshippers who entered Islam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أنه لا يجوز نكاح الأمة الكتابية، لأنه قيد جواز العقد على الاماء إذا كن مؤمنات

sources.gloss: The verse indicates that marriage to a slave-woman of the People of the Book is not permitted, since it restricted the permission of the contract over slave-women to their being believers.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فالخوارج زعمت أن الرجل إذا كانت لأهله بنت ولم يربها ولم تكن في حجره حلت له لقول الله: { واللاتي في حجوركم } قال الصادق عليه السلام لا تحل له

sources.gloss: The Khawarij claimed that if a man's wife has a daughter whom he did not raise and who was not in his care, she is lawful for him, on account of God's words "who are under your care". Al-Sadiq said: She is not lawful for him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصادق عليه السلام: { فما استمتعتم به منهن - إلى أجل مسمى - فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة } قال الصادق عليه السلام فهذه الآية دليل على المتعة

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said: "For the enjoyment you have had from them - to a stated term - give them their dowries, by way of settlement." Al-Sadiq said: This verse is proof of temporary marriage.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصادق عليه السلام وإنما صار يقتل في الثامنة لأن الله رحمه أن يجمع عليه ربق الرق وحد الحر

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said: He is put to death on the eighth occasion only because God had mercy on him, that the yoke of slavery and the penalty of a free man should not be gathered upon him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فيقول الله عز و جل في آية التحريم: { حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَٰتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمْ } إلى آخرها فأخبروني هل تصلح ابنتي أو ابنة ابنتي و ما تناسل من صلبي لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أن يتزوجها لو كان حيا؟ قالوا: لا.

sources.gloss: God says in the verse of prohibition, "Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters and your sisters," to the end of it. So tell me: could my daughter, or my daughter's daughter, or any born of my loins have been lawful for the Messenger of Allah to marry, were he alive? They said: No.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إذا تزوج الرجل المرأة حرمت عليه ابنتها إذا دخل بالام فإذا لم يدخل بالام فلا بأس ان يتزوج بالابنة وإذا تزوج الابنة فدخل بها أو لم يدخل بها فقد حرمت عليه الأم وقال الربائب حرام كن في الحجر أولم يكنّ

sources.gloss: If a man marries a woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him once he has gone in to the mother; if he has not gone in to the mother there is no harm in his marrying the daughter. If he marries the daughter, whether or not he goes in to her, the mother is forbidden to him. And he said: Stepdaughters are forbidden, whether or not they were in his care.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في الفقيه والعياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام هن ذوات الأزواج

sources.gloss: In al-Faqih and al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq: they are women who have husbands.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أنه سئل يتزوج الرجل بالامة بغير علم أهلها قال هو زنا ان الله تعالى يقول { فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ }

sources.gloss: He was asked whether a man may marry a slave-woman without her people's knowledge. He said: That is fornication, for God says, "So marry them with their masters' permission."

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: واختلف أهل التأويل في المحصنات التي عناهنّ الله في هذه الآية … واعتلّ قائلو هذه المقالة بالأخبار التي رُويت أن هذه الآية نزلت فيمن سُبي من أَوْطاس.

sources.gloss: The people of interpretation differed over the muhsanat whom God meant in this verse ... Those who held this position argued from the reports handed down that this verse came down about those taken captive at Awtas.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فقال ٱبن عباس وأبو قلابة وٱبن زيد ومَكْحُولٌ والزُّهِريّ وأبو سعيدٍ الخُدْرِيّ: المراد بالمحصَنات هنا المسْبِيّات ذواتُ الأزواج خاصة، أي هنّ محرّمات إلاَّ ما ملكت اليَمين بالسبْي من أرض الحرب، فإن تلك حلال للَّذي تقع في سهمه وإن كان لها زوج. وهو قول الشافعيّ في أن السِّباء يقطع العِصمة

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas, Abu Qilaba, Ibn Zayd, Makhul, al-Zuhri and Abu Said al-Khudri said: what is meant by al-muhsanat here is captive women who have husbands in particular, that is, they are forbidden except what the right hand owns by captivity from enemy territory, for she is lawful to the one whose share she falls into even if she has a husband. It is the position of Shafi'i that captivity cuts the marriage bond.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَتَزَوَّجَ الرَّجُلُ الْحُرُّ الْمَمْلُوكَةَ الْيَوْمَ إِنَّمَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ حَيْثُ قَالَ اللهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلا وَالطَّوْلُ الْمَهْرُ وَمَهْرُ الْحُرَّةِ الْيَوْمَ مَهْرُ الأمَةِ أَوْ أَقَلُّ.

sources.gloss: It is not fitting today that a free man marry a slave-woman. That was only when God said, "As for those of you who cannot afford." Tawl is the dowry, and the dowry of a free woman today is the dowry of a slave-woman, or less.

essay.en:
Three verses in a row announce what God desires, and each time the answer bends toward the people addressed: to explain the laws, to guide to the customs of those who were before you, and to turn toward you clemently. Tabrisi reads this as God's own account of why He has just permitted and forbidden, that He intends by it our welfare and our benefit; and he finds in it a refutation of the Mujbira, since God is shown willing nothing but good and rectitude [5]. Fayd Kashani glosses the customs of those before you as the ways of the prophets and the people of truth, so that they may be taken as a pattern [25].

Then a second will appears beside God's. Tusi says the repetition is deliberate contrast, so that we may see our own situation clearly: God wills one thing and the followers of appetite will its opposite [11]. Who are they? Mujahid said fornicators, al-Suddi the Jews and Christians, Ibn Zayd every partisan of falsehood; Tusi prefers the last, as the most general and the closest to the wording [11]. What God wills is relief, and in the promise to lighten Tusi finds a proof against the Mujbira, who hold that God may charge a servant with what he cannot bear, which would be the utmost hardening [12].

From marriage the passage turns to property. Tabatabai reads verse 29 as a move from the particular to the general: the earlier verses forbade consuming women's dowries by coercion, this forbids consuming wealth unrightfully at large [2]. Tusi finds in the exception made for trade a refutation of those who forbade earning a living [13]. The threat that follows attaches, on his strongest reading, to both wrongs together, and its qualification, in aggression and injustice, leaves killing by mistake outside it [14].

Then the door opens: avoid what is great and the small is covered, the verse itself dividing sins into two ranks [3]. Envy is cut at the root, since a wish repeated becomes hidden envy, settles in the heart, and passes into act [4]. The passage closes with heirs appointed, whom Tabrisi takes to be those with the better claim to the estate [9], and shares that must be given.

note.en: Mujahid, Tawus and Zayd referred the lightening here to the permission of marriage with bondwomen, since man was created weak in the matter of women [12].

Tusi: mutual consent is completed by the parting of the two parties, or by one choosing after the contract, on the report that they have the option so long as they have not parted; this is the Imami school [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وفي المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام الربا والقمار والبخس والظلم
narrations.chain: In Majma al-Bayan, from al-Baqir

text.en: Unrightfully: usury, gambling, short-changing and wrongdoing.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عنى بها القمار وكانت قريش تقامر الرجل بأهله وماله فنهاهم الله عن ذلك
narrations.chain: Al-Ayyashi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: By it He meant gambling. Quraysh would gamble with a man over his family and his wealth, so God forbade them that.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا تخاطروا بنفوسكم في القتال فتقاتلوا من لا تطيقونه

text.en: Do not risk your lives in fighting, and so fight those you have no strength against.

note.en: Tusi: with us all acts of disobedience are great, inasmuch as they disobey God, though some are greater than others; and He did not specify which are the major ones, lest that entice to the rest [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الْكَبَائِرُ الَّتِي أَوْجَبَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَيْهَا النَّارَ
narrations.chain: A number of our people, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Jamilah, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The major sins are those for which God has made the Fire binding.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هن في كتاب عليّ صلوات الله وسلامه عليه سبع: الكفر بالله وقتل النفس وعقوق الوالدين وأكل الربى بعد البينة وأكل مال اليتيم ظلماً والفرار من الزحف والتعرب بعد الهجرة
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq, answering Zurara

text.en: They are in the book of Ali: seven. Disbelief in God, killing a soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury after it has been made clear, consuming an orphan's property wrongfully, fleeing from battle, and returning to bedouin life after the migration.

narrations.speaker: Musa ibn Jafar
narrations.arabic: لا يخلد الله في النار إلا أهل الكفر والجحود وأهل الضلال و الشرك. ومن اجتنب الكبائر من المؤمنين لم يسأل عن الصغائر
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar al-Hamdani, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Musa ibn Jafar

text.en: God makes none abide for ever in the Fire but the people of disbelief and denial and the people of misguidance and idolatry. Whoever among the faithful avoids the major sins is not questioned about the lesser ones.

note.en: Tabrisi reports two occasions: a delegation of women asked why God mentions the men and not them, and Mujahid's report that Umm Salama wished they were men, to fight and to inherit fully [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لا يتمنى الرجل امرأة الرجل و لا ابنته، و لكن يتمنى مثلهما
narrations.chain: Al-Ayyashi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Let a man not covet another man's wife, nor his daughter; let him wish rather for the like of them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ليس من نفس إلا و قد فرض الله عز و جل لها رزقها حلالا يأتيها في عافية، و عرض لها بالحرام من وجه آخر، فإن هي تناولت شيئا من الحرام قاصها به من الحلال الذي فرض لها، و عند الله سواهما فضل كثير
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from Abu Jafar

text.en: There is no soul but that God has ordained for it its lawful provision, coming to it in ease, and has exposed it to the unlawful from another quarter. If it takes anything unlawful, He deducts it from the lawful ordained for it. Besides the two, with God is much bounty.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: ان الله تعالى أحب شيئاً لنفسه وابغضه لخلقه أبغض عز وجل لخلقه المسألة وأحب لنفسه أن يسأل وليس شيء أحب إليه من أن يسأل فلا يستحي أحدكم أن يسال الله عز وجل من فضله ولو شسع نعل
narrations.chain: In al-Faqih, from the Prophet

text.en: God has loved a thing for Himself and hated it for His creation: He hates begging for His creation, and loves for Himself to be asked. Nothing is dearer to Him than to be asked. So let none of you be ashamed to ask God of His bounty, even for a sandal strap.

note.en: Tusi records three readings of those with whom you have made a compact: sworn allies, men adopted in the way of the Jahiliyya, and those between whom the Prophet established brotherhood [17].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إنما عنى بذلك الأئمة (عليهم السلام) بهم عقد الله عز و جل أيمانكم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub

text.en: By that He meant only the Imams: it is through them that God has bound your oaths.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنما عنى بذلك اولي الأرحام في المواريث، و لم يعن أولياء النعمة، فأولاهم بالميت أقربهم إليه من الرحم التي تجره إليها
narrations.chain: Al-Tusi in al-Tahdhib, by his chain from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara

text.en: By this He meant only those of kinship in matters of inheritance, and He did not mean the patrons of manumission. The one with the better claim to the deceased is the nearest to him by the kinship that draws him.

perspectives.en: Verse 33 divides the readings. Ibn Kathir transmits from Ibn Abbas that a migrant used to inherit from his Helper brother through the brotherhood the Prophet established, that 'For everyone We have appointed heirs' abrogated this, and that what is still owed the sworn ally is help, provision and counsel, not a share of the estate [39]. Qurtubi adds that most of the early authorities held the abrogating verse to be 8:75, while a party held the clause firm and unabrogated [46]. The Shia narrations keep the clause alive and move it: al-Sadiq confines the heirs to kindred rather than patrons, and al-Rida reads those with whom you have made a compact as the Imams [24].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: في الآية شبه اتصال بما سبقتها حيث إنها تتضمن النهي عن أكل المال بالباطل وكانت الآيات السابقة متضمنة للنهي عن أكل مهور النساء بالعضل والتعدي ففي الآية انتقال من الخصوص إلى العموم

sources.gloss: The verse has something of a link with what came before it, since it contains the prohibition of consuming wealth unrightfully, while the preceding verses contained the prohibition of consuming women's dowries by coercion and transgression; so in the verse there is a move from the particular to the general.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فيتبين من الآية أولاً أن المعاصي قسمان صغيرة وكبيرة

sources.gloss: So it becomes clear from the verse, first, that acts of disobedience are of two kinds, small and great.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فيظهر الأمر أولاً في صورة التمني فإذا تكرر تبدل حسداً مستبطناً فإذا أُديم عليه فاستقر في القلب سرى إلى مقام العمل والفعل الخارجي

sources.gloss: The matter appears first in the form of a wish; when it is repeated it turns into concealed envy; and when it is persisted in and settles in the heart it passes over into the domain of act and outward deed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم بيَّن تعالى بعد التحليل والتحريم أنه يريد بذلك مصالحنا ومنافعنا … وفي هذا دلالة على بطلان مذهب المجبرة لأنه بيَّن تعالى أنه لا يريد إلا الخير والصلاح

sources.gloss: Then, after the permitting and the forbidding, God explained that He intends by it our welfare and our benefits ... And in this is a proof of the falsity of the doctrine of the Mujbira, since God has explained that He wills nothing but good and rectitude.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ما روي عن أبي عبد الله ع أن معناه لا تخاطروا بنفوسكم في القتال فتقاتلوا من لا تطيقونه

sources.gloss: What is related from Abu Abdillah, that its meaning is: do not risk your lives in fighting, and so fight those you have no strength against.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل جاءت وافدة النساء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: يا رسول الله أليس الله رَبُّ الرجال والنساء وأنت رسول الله إليهم جميعاً؟ فما بالنا يذكر الله الرجال ولا يذكرنا … وقيل: إن أم سلمة قالت: يا رسول الله يغزو الرجال ولا تغزو النساء وإنما لنا نصف الميراث فليتنا رجال فنغزو ونبلغ ما يبلغ الرجال فنزلت الآية عن مجاهد

sources.gloss: It is said that a delegation of women came to the Messenger of God and said: Messenger of God, is not God the Lord of men and women, and are you not God's messenger to them all?
