Why then does God mention the men and not mention us? ... And it is said that Umm Salama said: Messenger of God, the men fight and the women do not fight, and we have only half the inheritance; would that we were men, so that we might fight and attain what men attain. So the verse was revealed, from Mujahid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { جعلنا موالي } أي ورثة هم أولى بميراثه عن السدي. وقيل: عصبة عن ابن عباس والحسن والأول أصح

sources.gloss: 'We have appointed heirs' means heirs who have the better claim to his estate, from al-Suddi. And it is said: agnates, from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan; but the first is more correct.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أن يبين أن ارادته منا خلاف إرادة أصحاب الأهواء لنا، لنكون على بصيرة من أمرنا، وجاء الثاني على التقابل، بأن الله يريد شيئاً ويريدون خلافه … والأول أقوى، لأنه أعم فائدة، وأوفق لظاهر اللفظ

sources.gloss: That He make plain that His will for us is the contrary of the will the people of caprice have for us, so that we may have insight into our situation; and the second came by way of contrast, that God wills one thing and they will its opposite ... And the first is the stronger, because it is the more general in benefit and the more agreeable to the apparent wording.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى قوله: { يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم } ها هنا أي في نكاح الاماء، لأن الانسان خلق ضعيفاً في أمر النساء، هذا قول مجاهد، وطاووس، وزيد … وفي الآية دلالة على فساد قول المجبرة: ان الله يكلف عباده ما لا يطيقون، لأن ذلك مناف لارادة التخفيف عنهم في التكليف، من حيث أنه غاية التثقيل

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'God desires to lighten your burden' here is in the matter of marriage with bondwomen, because man was created weak in the matter of women; this is the view of Mujahid, Tawus and Zayd ... And in the verse is a proof of the falsity of the doctrine of the Mujbira, that God charges His servants with what they cannot bear, since that contradicts the will to lighten their obligation, being the utmost hardening.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فيه دلالة على بطلان قول من حرم المكاسب، لأنه تعالى حرم أكل الأموال بالباطل، وأحله بالتجارة على طريق المكاسب … إمضاء البيع بالتفرق، أو بالتخاير بعد العقد في قول شريح، وابن سيرين، والشعبي، لقوله (صلى الله عليه وسلم): " البيعان بالخيار ما لم يتفرقا أو يكون بيع خيار " وربما قالوا: أو يقول أحدهما للآخر اختر، وهو مذهبنا

sources.gloss: In it is a proof of the falsity of the view of the one who forbade earning, because God forbade consuming wealth unrightfully and made it lawful by trade in the way of earning ... The concluding of the sale is by the parting of the two, or by choosing after the contract, on the view of Shurayh, Ibn Sirin and al-Shabi, on his saying: the two parties to a sale have the option so long as they have not parted, or unless it is a sale with an option; and sometimes they said: or one of them says to the other, choose. And this is our school.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: انه على أكل الاموال بالباطل، وقتل النفس بغير حق، والوعيد بكل واحدة من الخصلتين … وإنما قيد قوله: { ومن يفعل ذلك عدواناً وظلماً } لأن من وقع منه قتل النفس على وجه السهو والخطأ في خلاف المراد، لم يتناوله الوعيد

sources.gloss: That it bears upon consuming wealth unrightfully and killing a soul without right, the threat applying to each of the two ... And He qualified His words 'whoever does that in aggression and injustice' only because one from whom the killing of a soul comes by way of forgetfulness or error, contrary to intention, is not covered by the threat.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والمعاصي وإن كانت كلها عندنا كبائر، من حيث كانت معصية لله تعالى، فانا نقول: إن بعضها أكبر من بعض … ولم يعين الكبائر التي إذا اجتنبها كفر ما عداها، لأنه لو فعل ذلك لكان فيه إغراء بما عداها

sources.gloss: Acts of disobedience, though with us they are all major, inasmuch as they are disobedience to God, we still say that some of them are greater than others ... And He did not specify the major sins whose avoidance brings the absolution of the rest, because had He done so there would have been in it an enticement to the rest.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدها - قال سعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، وعامر، والضحاك: إنهم الحلفاء. الثاني - قال الحسن، وسعيد بن المسيب: هم رجال كانوا يتبنون، على عادة الجاهلية … الثالث - في رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس، وابن زيد انهم قوم آخى بينهم رسول الله

sources.gloss: The first: Said ibn Jubayr, Qatada, Amir and al-Dahhak said they are the sworn allies. The second: al-Hasan and Said ibn al-Musayyab said they are men who used to be adopted, in the way of the Jahiliyya ... The third: in another report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd, they are a people between whom the Messenger of God established brotherhood.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لا يتمنى الرجل امرأة الرجل و لا ابنته، و لكن يتمنى مثلهما

sources.gloss: Let a man not covet another man's wife, nor his daughter, but let him wish for the like of them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إنما عنى بذلك الأئمة (عليهم السلام) بهم عقد الله عز و جل أيمانكم

sources.gloss: He meant by that only the Imams: it is through them that God has bound your oaths.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: { وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ الّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ } من الأنبياء وأهل الحق لتقتدوا بهم

sources.gloss: 'And to guide you to the customs of those who were before you': of the prophets and the people of truth, that you may take them as a pattern.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: هن في كتاب عليّ صلوات الله وسلامه عليه سبع: الكفر بالله وقتل النفس وعقوق الوالدين وأكل الربى بعد البينة وأكل مال اليتيم ظلماً والفرار من الزحف والتعرب بعد الهجرة

sources.gloss: They are in the book of Ali: seven. Disbelief in God, killing a soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury after it has been made clear, consuming an orphan's property wrongfully, fleeing from battle, and returning to bedouin life after the migration.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: فلا يستحي أحدكم أن يسال الله عز وجل من فضله ولو شسع نعل

sources.gloss: So let none of you be ashamed to ask God of His bounty, even for a sandal strap.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: كان المهاجرون لما قدموا المدينة، يرث المهاجري الأنصاري دون ذوي رحمه للأخوة التي آخى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بينهم، فلما نزلت { وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِىَ } نسخت … من النصر والرفادة والنصيحة، وقد ذهب الميراث، ويوصى له

sources.gloss: When the migrants came to Medina, the migrant would inherit from the Helper, to the exclusion of his own kin, because of the brotherhood the Prophet established between them; and when 'For everyone We have appointed heirs' was sent down, it abrogated that ... their share is of help, provision and counsel, the inheritance having gone, and a bequest may be made for him.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وروي عن جمهور السلف أن الآية الناسخة لقوله: { وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ } قوله تعالى في «الأنفال»: { وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ } … وقالت طائفة: قوله تعالى: { وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ } مُحْكَمٌ وليس بمنسوخ

sources.gloss: It is related from most of the early authorities that the verse abrogating 'and those with whom you have made a compact' is His words in al-Anfal, 'and the blood relatives are more entitled to one another' ... And a party said: His words 'and those with whom you have made a compact' are firm and not abrogated.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: ومن اجتنب الكبائر من المؤمنين لم يسأل عن الصغائر

sources.gloss: Whoever among the faithful avoids the major sins is not questioned about the lesser ones.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: الْكَبَائِرُ الَّتِي أَوْجَبَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَلَيْهَا النَّارَ

sources.gloss: The major sins are those for which God has made the Fire binding.

essay.en:
Nine verses carry the reader from inside a marriage out to the witnesses of the Last Day. Verse 34 sets men over women by Allah's apportioning and by what they spend. Tabatabai reads the run as continuous with the rulings on inheritance and marriage just given, drawing from them general principles that mend what goes wrong between men and women [1]. Tabrisi transmits from Muqatil that it came down after Sa'd ibn al-Rabi struck his wife Habiba bint Zayd; her father sought retaliation, the Prophet granted it, then withdrew it when the verse arrived, saying, "We intended a matter and Allah intended a matter, and what Allah intended is better" [3]. The remedies for a wife's misconduct are graded and kept within the bed; al-Tusi reports from Abu Ja'far that keeping away means leaving the shared bed, turning his back to her [10].

When the rift runs both ways, verse 35 lifts it out of the house. Tabrisi reports that the one told to appoint the two arbiters is the ruler before whom the couple bring their case, the view of most jurists and what appears in the reports from the two Sadiqs [4]; al-Tusi adds that in our school they are arbiters rather than agents, and may not separate the couple until they have asked their leave [11].

Verse 36 widens the circle beyond the household: parents, kin, orphans, the needy, the near and the distant neighbour, the companion at one's side, the traveller, those one owns. Tabatabai calls this practical tawhid: the good deed done for Allah's pleasure, not for one's whim [2]. Tabrisi transmits the Prophet's ranking of neighbours by their claims of neighbourhood, kinship and Islam [5], and al-Tusi records three readings of the companion at one's side, the widest sense taking in all of them [12].

Two failures answer this call. Tabrisi takes the stinginess of verse 37 generally, of anyone withholding what he owes or hiding what Allah gave him [6]; al-Zajjaj and others read the ostentatious spenders of verse 38 as the hypocrites, and al-Tusi prefers that to Mujahid's reading of the Jews, since showing off is a species of hypocrisy [14]. Verse 39's question shuts the excuse of those who claim they cannot believe [7]. Then the measure: not an atom's weight of wrong, the atom being the small red ant [8]. The passage closes with the witnesses, at which, Tabrisi reports, Ibn Masud recited and the Prophet's eyes overflowed [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام أنه يحول ظهره إليها … في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام أنه الضرب بالسواك
narrations.chain: In Majma al-Bayan, from al-Baqir

text.en: He turns his back to her. … It is a striking with the tooth-stick.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: سأل أبا جعفر (عليه السلام) رجل و أنا عنده، فقال: قال رجل لامرأته: أمرك بيدك. قال: " أنى يكون هذا و الله يقول: { ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ }! ليس هذا بشيء "
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad the sons of al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yaqub, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ibrahim ibn Muhriz

text.en: A man asked Abu Ja'far, while I was with him: a man said to his wife, "Your affair is in your own hand." He said: "How can that be, when Allah says, Men are the managers of women! This is nothing."

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: عِلَّةُ إِعْطَاءِ اَلنِّسَاءِ نِصْفَ مَا يُعْطَى اَلرِّجَالَ مِنَ اَلْمِيرَاثِ لِأَنَّ اَلْمَرْأَةَ إِذَا تَزَوَّجَتْ أَخَذَتْ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ يُعْطِي فَلِذَلِكَ وُفِّرَ عَلَى اَلرِّجَالِ … وَ عِلَّةٌ أُخْرَى فِي إِعْطَاءِ الذَّكَرِ مِثْلَيْ مَا تُعْطَى الْأُنْثَى لِأَنَّ الْأُنْثَى فِي عِيَالِ الذَّكَرِ إِنِ احْتَاجَتْ وَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَعُولَهَا وَ عَلَيْهِ نَفَقَتُهَا وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى الْمَرْأَةِ أَنْ تَعُولَ الرَّجُلَ

text.en: The reason women are given half of what men are given in inheritance is that a woman, on marrying, receives, while a man gives; so more was allotted to men. … The female is the male's dependant if she is in need: her keep and maintenance fall on him, while a woman need not maintain a man.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: " ليس للحكمين أن يفرقا حتى يستأمرا من الرجل و المرأة، و يشترطا عليهما، إن شئنا جمعنا، و إن شئنا فرقنا، فإن فرقا فجائز، و إن جمعا فجائز "
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The two arbiters have no right to separate the couple until they seek leave of the man and the woman and stipulate with them: if we wish we join, and if we wish we separate. If they separate it is valid, and if they join it is valid.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: وأتى علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام رجل وامرأته على هذه الحال فبعث حكماً من أهله وحكماً من أهلها وقال للحكمين هل تدريان ما تحكمان؟ إن شئتما فرقتما وإن شئتما جمعتما

text.en: A man and his wife in this condition came to Ali ibn Abi Talib. He sent an arbiter from the husband's family and an arbiter from hers, and said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what you are to decide? If you wish you separate them, and if you wish you join them."

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: " إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أحد الوالدين، و علي الآخر " فقلت: أين موضع ذلك في كتاب الله؟ قال: " اقرأ { وَٱعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً } "
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: "The Messenger of Allah is one of the two parents, and Ali is the other." I said: where is the place of that in the Book of Allah? He said: "Recite, Worship Allah and do not ascribe any partners to Him, and be good to parents."

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن جعفر [الصادق. ر] عليه السلام … { وبذي القربى } قال: الحسن والحسين عليهما السلام.
narrations.chain: Furat, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Ahmasi, from Ja'far

text.en: "And the relatives" - he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في الكافي عن الباقر عليه السلام حد الجوار أربعون داراً من كل جانب من بين يديه ومن خلفه وعن يمينه وعن شماله.
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi, from al-Baqir

text.en: The limit of neighbourhood is forty houses on each side, before him, behind him, on his right and on his left.

note.en: Al-Qummi remarks that by placing the stingy under "the faithless" in this verse, Allah has named the miser a disbeliever [21].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: ليس البخيل من أدى الزكاة المفروضة من ماله وأعطى الباينة في قومه انما البخيل حق البخيل من لم يؤد الزكاة المفروضة من ماله ولم يعط الباينة في قومه وهو يبذر فيما سوى ذلك.

text.en: The miser is not the one who pays the obligatory zakat from his wealth and gives the customary gift among his people. The real miser is the one who pays no obligatory zakat from his wealth and gives no gift among his people, while he squanders on everything else.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: البخيل يبخل بما في يده والشحيح يشح بما في أيدي الناس وعلى ما في يديه حتى لا يرى في أيدي الناس شيئاً إلا تمنى أن يكون له بالحل والحرام ولا يقنع بما رزقه الله.

text.en: The miser is stingy with what is in his own hand; the covetous man is greedy for what is in people's hands and for his own, so that he sees nothing in their hands without wishing it were his, lawfully or unlawfully, and is never content with what Allah provided him.

note.en: Al-Qummi reads "a witness from every nation" as the Imams: the Messenger of Allah is witness over the Imams, and they are witnesses over the people [24].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قَالَ نَزَلَتْ فِي أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) خَاصَّةً فِي كُلِّ قَرْنٍ مِنْهُمْ إِمَامٌ مِنَّا شَاهِدٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمُحَمَّدٌ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) شَاهِدٌ عَلَيْنَا.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It was revealed about the community of Muhammad in particular: in every age among them there is an Imam from us who is a witness over them, and Muhammad is a witness over us.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: يجتمعون في موطن يستنطق فيه جميع الخلق فلا يتكلم أحد { إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَاباً } [النبأ: 38] … و هو الشهيد على الشهداء، و الشهداء هم الرسل
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu Ma'mar al-Sa'di

text.en: They gather at a station where all creation is made to speak, and none speaks "except him whom the All-beneficent permits and who says what is right". … He is the witness over the witnesses, and the witnesses are the messengers.

note.en: Al-Tusi says "they will not conceal any matter from Allah" does not contradict 6:23, and gives seven ways of squaring the two [18]. Al-Qummi refers the wish to those who usurped the right of the Commander of the Faithful [25].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ختم على الأفواه فلا تكلم، فتكلمت الأيدي، و شهدت الأرجل، و نطقت الجلود بما عملوا فلا يكتمون الله حديثا
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather

text.en: The mouths are sealed and do not speak; so the hands speak, the feet bear witness, and the skins utter what they did, and they conceal no matter from Allah.

perspectives.en: Verse 41's witnesses are read differently. Al-Qummi takes "a witness from every nation" to mean the Imams, with the Messenger of Allah witness over them and they witnesses over the people [24], and al-Kulayni reports from al-Sadiq that the verse concerns Muhammad's community alone, an Imam in every age [77]. Al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Jurayj the plainer reading, that the witness is each nation's own messenger, testifying that he delivered what he was sent with [42]. Al-Qurtubi keeps the weight on the scene: the Prophet wept until his cheeks were wet, saying, "My Lord, this is for those among whom I live; what of those I have not seen?" [56]

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات مرتبطة بما تقدم من أحكام المواريث وأحكام النكاح يؤكد بها أمر الأحكام السابقة ويستنتج منها بعض الأحكام الكلية التي تصلح بعض الخلال العارضة في المعاشرة بين الرجال والنساء.

sources.gloss: These verses are connected with the foregoing rulings on inheritance and marriage; they confirm those rulings and derive from them general rulings that repair some of the flaws arising in the dealings between men and women.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: هذا هو التوحيد غير أن المراد به التوحيد العملي وهو إتيان الأعمال الحسنة - ومنها الإِحسان الذي هو مورد الكلام - طلباً لمرضاة الله وابتغاءً لثواب الآخرة دون اتباع الهوى والشرك به.

sources.gloss: This is tawhid, but what is meant by it is practical tawhid: performing good deeds, among them the kindness under discussion, seeking Allah's pleasure and the reward of the Hereafter, rather than following whim and associating it with Him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال مقاتل: " نزلت الآية في سعد بن الربيع بن عمرو وكان من النقباء وفي امرأته حبيبة بنت زيد بن أبي زهير وهما من الأنصار وذلك أنها نشزت عليه فلطمها، فانطلق أبوها معها إلى النبي، فقال: أفرشتُه كريمتي، فلطمها. فقال النبي: لتقتص من زوجها فانصرفت مع أبيها لتقتص منه، فقال النبي: " ارجعوا فهذا جبرائيل أتاني وأنزل الله هذه الآية " فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أردنا أمراً وأراد الله أمراً والذي أراد الله خير

sources.gloss: Muqatil said: the verse came down about Sa'd ibn al-Rabi, one of the chiefs, and his wife Habiba bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr, both of the Ansar. She rose against him and he slapped her; her father went with her to the Prophet and said, "I gave him my daughter and he slapped her." The Prophet said, "Let her retaliate against her husband." She left with her father to retaliate, then the Prophet said, "Come back; this is Gabriel who has come to me and Allah has revealed this verse." And the Prophet said, "We intended a matter and Allah intended a matter, and what Allah intended is better."

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: واختلف في المخاطب بانفاذ الحكمين من هو فقيل هو السلطان الذي يترافع الزوجان إليه عن سعيد بن جبير، والضحاك، وأكثر الفقهاء، وهو الظاهر في الأخبار عن الصادقين.

sources.gloss: They differed over who is addressed with sending the two arbiters. It is said to be the ruler before whom the two spouses bring their case, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and most of the jurists, and that is what is apparent in the reports from the two Sadiqs.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " الجيران ثلاثة: جار له ثلاثة حقوق، حق الجوار، وحق القرابة، وحق الإسلام. وجار له حقان: حق الجوار، وحق الإسلام، وجار له حق الجوار المشرك من أهل الكتاب

sources.gloss: It is reported from the Prophet that he said: "Neighbours are three. A neighbour with three claims: the claim of neighbourhood, the claim of kinship and the claim of Islam. A neighbour with two claims: the claim of neighbourhood and the claim of Islam. And a neighbour with the claim of neighbourhood alone: the associator from the People of the Book."

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والأولى أن تكون الآية عامة في كل من يبخل بأداء ما يجب عليه أداؤه، ويأمرون الناس به، وعامة في كل من كتم فضلاً آتاه الله تعالى من العالم وغيره.

sources.gloss: It is better that the verse be general, covering everyone who is stingy in paying what he must pay and orders people to the same, and everyone who conceals a bounty Allah gave him, whether of knowledge or otherwise.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قطع الله سبحانه بهذا عذر الكفار في العدول عن الإيمان، وأبطل به قول من قال إنهم لا يقدرون على الإيمان

sources.gloss: By this Allah cut off the excuse of the faithless for turning away from belief, and refuted with it the claim of those who say they are not able to believe.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { مثقال ذرة } أي زنة ذرة وهي النملة الحمراء الصغيرة التي لا تكاد تُرى عن ابن عباس وابن زيد وهي أصغر النمل.

sources.gloss: "An atom's weight", that is, the weight of a dharra, which is the small red ant that can hardly be seen, from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd; it is the smallest of ants.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وروي أن عبد الله بن مسعود قرأ هذه الآية على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ففاضت عيناه

sources.gloss: It is reported that Abdullah ibn Masud recited this verse to the Prophet and his eyes overflowed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال مجاهد، والشعبي، وابراهيم: هو هجر المضاجعة، وهو قول أبي جعفر (ع). وقال: يحول ظهره إليها.

sources.gloss: Mujahid, al-Sha'bi and Ibrahim said: it is abandoning the shared bed, and that is the statement of Abu Ja'far. He said: he turns his back to her.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واختلف الفقهاء في الحكمين هل هما وكيلان، أو هما حكمان، فعندنا أنهما حكمان، وقال قوم: هما وكيلان، واختلفوا هل للحكمين أن يفرقا بالطلاق إن رأياه أم لا؟ فعندنا ليس لهما ذلك إلا بعد أن يستأمراهما، أو كان اذن لهما في الأصل في ذلك

sources.gloss: The jurists differed over the two arbiters, whether they are agents or arbiters; with us they are arbiters, while some hold they are agents. They also differed over whether the arbiters may separate the couple by divorce if they see fit; with us they may not, except after seeking the couple's leave, or unless they were given leave for it at the outset.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الثالث - قال ابن زيد، وابن عباس،، في رواية أخرى عنه: إنه المنقطع اليك رجاء رفدك. وقيل إنه جميع هؤلاء، وهو أعم فائدة.

sources.gloss: The third: Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Abbas in another report from him, said he is the one who attaches himself to you hoping for your help. And it is said that it is all of these, which is the more general benefit.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الزجاج وغيره: المعني بهذه الآية المنافقون. وقال مجاهد: المعني بها اليهود، والأول أقوى وأظهر، لأن الرياء ضرب من النفاق

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj and others said: those meant by this verse are the hypocrites. Mujahid said: the Jews are meant. The first is stronger and clearer, because ostentation is a species of hypocrisy.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { ولا يكتمون الله حديثاً } لا ينافي قوله: { والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين } لأنه قيل في معنى الآية سبعة أقوال:

sources.gloss: His words "and they will not conceal any matter from Allah" do not contradict His words "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists", for seven views have been given on the meaning of the verse.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وأتى علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام رجل وامرأته على هذه الحال فبعث حكماً من أهله وحكماً من أهلها وقال للحكمين هل تدريان ما تحكمان؟ إن شئتما فرقتما وإن شئتما جمعتما

sources.gloss: A man and his wife in this condition came to Ali ibn Abi Talib, so he sent an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers and said to the two arbiters: do you know what you are to decide? If you wish you separate them, and if you wish you join them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فسمى الله البخيل كافراً.

sources.gloss: So Allah named the miser a disbeliever.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني الأئمة صلوات الله عليهم أجمعين { وجئنا بك } يا محمد { على هؤلاء شهيداً } يعني على الأئمة، فرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله شهيد على الأئمة وهم شهداء على الناس.

sources.gloss: It means the Imams. "And We bring you", O Muhammad, "as a witness to them", means over the Imams: so the Messenger of Allah is a witness over the Imams, and they are witnesses over the people.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال يتمنى الذين غصبوا أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أن تكون الأرض ابتلعتهم في اليوم الذي اجتمعوا فيه على غصبه وأن لم يكتموا ما قاله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله فيه.

sources.gloss: He said: those who usurped the right of the Commander of the Faithful will wish that the earth had swallowed them on the day they gathered to usurp it, and that they had not concealed what the Messenger of Allah said about him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: سأل أبا جعفر (عليه السلام) رجل و أنا عنده، فقال: قال رجل لامرأته: أمرك بيدك. قال: " أنى يكون هذا و الله يقول: { ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ }! ليس هذا بشيء "

sources.gloss: A man asked Abu Ja'far, while I was with him, saying: a man said to his wife, "Your affair is in your own hand." He said: "How can that be, when Allah says, Men are the managers of women! This is nothing."

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: " ليس للحكمين أن يفرقا حتى يستأمرا من الرجل و المرأة، و يشترطا عليهما، إن شئنا جمعنا، و إن شئنا فرقنا، فإن فرقا فجائز، و إن جمعا فجائز "

sources.gloss: "The two arbiters have no right to separate the couple until they seek leave of the man and the woman and stipulate with them: if we wish we join, and if we wish we separate. If they separate it is valid, and if they join it is valid."

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: " إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أحد الوالدين، و علي الآخر " فقلت: أين موضع ذلك في كتاب الله؟ قال: " اقرأ { وَٱعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً } "

sources.gloss: "The Messenger of Allah is one of the two parents, and Ali is the other." I said: where is the place of that in the Book of Allah? He said: "Recite, Worship Allah and do not ascribe any partners to Him, and be good to parents."

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و هو الشهيد على الشهداء، و الشهداء هم الرسل

sources.gloss: And he is the witness over the witnesses, and the witnesses are the messengers.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ختم على الأفواه فلا تكلم، فتكلمت الأيدي، و شهدت الأرجل، و نطقت الجلود بما عملوا فلا يكتمون الله حديثا

sources.gloss: The mouths are sealed and do not speak, so the hands speak, the feet bear witness, and the skins utter what they did, and they conceal no matter from Allah.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام أنه الضرب بالسواك

sources.gloss: In Majma al-Bayan, from al-Baqir: that it is a striking with the tooth-stick.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: البخيل يبخل بما في يده والشحيح يشح بما في أيدي الناس وعلى ما في يديه حتى لا يرى في أيدي الناس شيئاً إلا تمنى أن يكون له بالحل والحرام ولا يقنع بما رزقه الله.

sources.gloss: The miser is stingy with what is in his own hand, and the covetous man is greedy for what is in people's hands and for what is in his own, so that he sees nothing in people's hands without wishing it were his, by the lawful or the unlawful, and is not content with what Allah has provided him.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: { وبذي القربى } قال: الحسن والحسين عليهما السلام.

sources.gloss: "And the relatives" - he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: قال ابن جريج: قوله: { فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلّ أمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ } قال: رسولها، فيشهد عليها أن قد أبلغهم ما أرسله الله به إليهم

sources.gloss: Ibn Jurayj said of His words "So how shall it be, when We bring a witness from every nation": it is its messenger, who testifies against it that he delivered to them what Allah sent him with.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: بكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى اخضلت وجنتاه فقال: «يارب هذا على من أنا بين ظهرانيهم فكيف من لم أرهم»

sources.gloss: The Messenger of Allah wept until his cheeks were wet, and said: "My Lord, this is for those among whom I live; what then of those I have not seen?"

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: عِلَّةُ إِعْطَاءِ اَلنِّسَاءِ نِصْفَ مَا يُعْطَى اَلرِّجَالَ مِنَ اَلْمِيرَاثِ لِأَنَّ اَلْمَرْأَةَ إِذَا تَزَوَّجَتْ أَخَذَتْ وَ اَلرَّجُلُ يُعْطِي فَلِذَلِكَ وُفِّرَ عَلَى اَلرِّجَالِ

sources.gloss: The reason women are given half of what men are given in inheritance is that a woman, when she marries, receives, while the man gives; so more was allotted to men.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: قَالَ نَزَلَتْ فِي أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) خَاصَّةً فِي كُلِّ قَرْنٍ مِنْهُمْ إِمَامٌ مِنَّا شَاهِدٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمُحَمَّدٌ (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) شَاهِدٌ عَلَيْنَا.

sources.gloss: He said: it was revealed about the community of Muhammad in particular: in every age among them there is an Imam from us who is a witness over them, and Muhammad is a witness over us.

title.en: Prayer, purity, and the Book's people

essay.en:
The passage begins inside worship. Believers are told not to approach prayer while intoxicated, until they know what they are saying, nor in a state of ritual impurity except while passing through, and, where no water can be found, to wipe face and hands with clean ground. Tabatabai places the verse before 2:219 and before the outright prohibition of 5:90, the last of the wine verses to come down [1]. Al-Tusi records the disputed reading behind 'you have touched women': taken with the long vowel it means intercourse, the view of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah [9].

Then the address turns outward and stays there. Al-Tabrisi reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse on those given a share of the Book came down about Rifa'ah ibn Zayd and Malik ibn Dukhshum, who twisted their tongues when the Prophet spoke and found fault with him [4]. Al-Tusi reads the join as deliberate: after rulings that must be acted upon comes a warning against whoever calls to their opposite [10]. Tabatabai sees the same scene from inside, men who came to the believers with affection and the look of sincere counsel [2].

Verse 46 names the method. Words are shifted off their places; Mujahid, cited by al-Tabrisi, reads those words as the Torah, whose description of the Prophet they kept hidden [5], and al-Tusi adds that not all of them did this, only their rabbis and scholars [11]. Greetings are turned inside out, and a twist of the tongue carries the insult. Verse 47 summons them to believe before faces are blotted out; al-Tabrisi collects the readings of that threat, the first, from Ibn Abbas and Atiyyah al-Awfi, taking it of faces effaced and turned round [6].

Verse 48 sets the boundary that orders the rest: one thing God does not forgive, and everything short of it lies open to His will. The closing two verses apply it to people who have already declared themselves pure. Purity is God's to give, and no one is wronged by so much as the thread in a date-stone. Ibn Jurayj, cited by al-Tusi, reads the lie they fabricate as that very self-purification [15].

note.en: On the ground of tayammum, al-Zajjaj, cited by al-Tabrisi, holds that sa'id is not soil as such but the face of the earth, whether soil or something else [3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله سبحانه نهى المؤمنين أن يقوموا إلى الصلاة و هم سكارى، يعني سكر النوم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, both from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Allah, glory be to Him, forbade the believers to rise to prayer while they are intoxicated, meaning the intoxication of sleep.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: أن المراد به سكر الشراب ثم نسختها تحريم الخمر

text.en: What is meant by it is the intoxication of drink; then the prohibition of wine abrogated it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الحائض والجنب لا يدخلان المسجد إلا مجتازين فإن الله تعالى يقول: { ولا جنباً إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا }

text.en: The menstruating woman and the one in janabah do not enter the mosque except as passers-through, for Allah says: 'nor in the state of ritual impurity, except while passing through, until you have washed yourselves'.

note.en: Al-Qummi reads the error they purchase as their straying over Amir al-Mu'minin, and their wish that you lose the way as pulling people out of his wilayah, which is the straight path [17].

narrations.speaker: Musa ibn Jafar
narrations.arabic: كانت هذه اللفظة: (راعنا) من ألفاظ المسلمين الذين يخاطبون بها رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، يقولون: (راعنا) أي ارع أحوالنا، و اسمع منا كما نسمع منك، و كان في لغة اليهود معناه: اسمع لا سمعت
narrations.chain: al-Imam al-Askari, from Musa ibn Jafar

text.en: This word, ra'ina, was one of the expressions the Muslims used in addressing the Messenger of Allah. They would say ra'ina, that is: attend to our condition, and hear from us as we hear from you. But in the language of the Jews its meaning was: hear, may you not hear.

note.en: Reports that a verse 'came down thus', carrying more than the text does, do not prove the Quran deficient: what God revealed is wider than the Quran, Muhsini holds [60].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ان المعنى نطمسها عن الهدى فنردها على ادبارها في ضلالتها بحيث لا يفلح ابداً

text.en: The meaning is that We blot them out from guidance and turn them back upon their traces in their error, so that they never prosper.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزل جبرئيل (عليه السلام) على محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) بهذه الآية هكذا: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا في علي نورا مبينا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from al-Munakhkhal, from Jabir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Gabriel came down to Muhammad with this verse thus: O you who were given the Book, believe in what We have sent down concerning Ali, a manifest light.

note.en: The wording says God never forgives that partners be ascribed to Him; al-Tusi notes the community reads this of shirk unrepented of, since one who repents of it is forgiven [13].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ الله لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الْكَبَائِرَ فَمَا سِوَاهَا قَالَ قُلْتُ دَخَلَتِ الْكَبَائِرُ فِي الإسْتِثْنَاءِ قَالَ نَعَمْ
narrations.chain: Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes': the major sins and what is lesser than them. I said: do the major sins enter into the exception? He said: yes.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أَلاَ وَإنَّ الظُّلْمَ ثَلاَثَةٌ: فَظُلْمٌ لاَ يُغْفَرُ، وَظُلْمٌ لاَ يُتْرَكُ، وظُلْمٌ مَغْفُورٌ لاَ يُطْلَبُ. فَأَمَّا الظُّلْمُ الَّذِي لاَ يُغْفَرُ فَالشِّرْكُ بِاللهِ، قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّـهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾

text.en: Know that wrongdoing is of three kinds: a wrong that is not forgiven, a wrong that is not left unquestioned, and a wrong forgiven without being asked after. The one not forgiven is ascribing partners to Allah; Allah has said: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ما في القرآن آية أحب إلي من قوله عز وجل: (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء)
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ghalib al-Shafi'i, from Mujahid ibn A'yun ibn Dawud, from Isa ibn Ahmad al-Asqalani, from al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Israfil, from Thuwayr, from his father, from Ali

text.en: There is no verse in the Quran more beloved to me than His word: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes.'

note.en: Fatil, the measure of wrong they will not suffer: what lies in the groove of the date-stone, on the reading of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata and Qatadah [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى حيث قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة الا من كان هوداً أو نصارى

text.en: It was revealed about the Jews and the Christians, when they said 'We are the sons of God and His beloved', and said 'None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian'.

perspectives.en: On the word 'intoxicated' the two readings part. Al-Qurtubi reports that the body of scholars and jurists take it of intoxication from wine, al-Dahhak alone reading it of sleep [43], and al-Tabari transmits from Mujahid that people were forbidden to pray while drunk until the prohibition of wine abrogated the ruling [32]. The Shia narrations mostly run the other way, al-Baqir glossing the word as the intoxication of sleep [22], though al-Safi also carries from al-Kazim the reading of drink, abrogated once wine was forbidden [27].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقبل قوله تعالى { يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر … وقوله تعالى { يا أيُّها الذين آمنوا إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه } المائدة 90، وهذه آخر الآيات نزولاً

sources.gloss: and before His word 'They ask you about wine and gambling' ... and His word 'O you who have faith! Wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are an abomination of Satan's doing, so avoid it' (5:90), and this last is the latest of them in revelation

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: يلوح من هذه الآيات أن اليهود كانوا يلقون إلى المؤمنين المودة ويظهرون لهم النصح فيفتنونهم بذلك

sources.gloss: It appears from these verses that the Jews would offer the believers affection and show them sincere counsel, and by that draw them into trial

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقال الزجاج: الصعيد ليس هو التراب إنما هو وجه الأرض تراباً كان أو غيره

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj said: sa'id is not soil; it is the face of the earth, whether soil or something else

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في رفاعة بن زيد بن السائب ومالك بن دخشم كانا إذا تكلم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لويا لسانهما وعاباه عن ابن عباس

sources.gloss: It was revealed about Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Sa'ib and Malik ibn Dukhshum: when the Messenger of Allah spoke, the two would twist their tongues and find fault with him, from Ibn Abbas

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقال مجاهد: يعني بالكلم التوراة وذلك أنهم كتموا ما في التوراة من صفة النبي

sources.gloss: Mujahid said: by the words is meant the Torah, in that they concealed what the Torah holds of the description of the Prophet

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن معناه من قبل أن نمحو آثار وجوهكم حتى تصير كالأقفية ونجعل عيونها في أقفيتها فتمشي القهقرى عن ابن عباس وعطية العوفي

sources.gloss: that its meaning is: before We efface the features of your faces until they become like the backs of necks, and set their eyes in their napes so that they walk backwards, from Ibn Abbas and Atiyyah al-Awfi

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقيل: هو ما يكون في شق النواة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطا وقتادة

sources.gloss: It is said that it is what lies in the groove of the date-stone, from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata and Qatadah

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فمن قرأ { لامستم } بالف قال: معناه الجماع: وهو قول علي (ع)، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، وأبو علي الجبائي، واختاره أبو حنيفة

sources.gloss: Whoever reads lamastum with the alif says its meaning is intercourse, and that is the view of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Abu Ali al-Jubba'i, and Abu Hanifah chose it

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ووجه اتصال هذه الآية بما قبلها التأكيد للأحكام التي يجب العمل بها، بالتحذير ممن يدعو إلى خلافها، ويكذب بها

sources.gloss: The way this verse joins what precedes it is the confirming of the rulings that must be acted upon, by warning against whoever calls to their opposite and denies them

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما قال: { من الذين هادوا } لأنه ليس جميع اليهود حرّفوا، وإنما حرّف أحبارهم وعلماؤهم

sources.gloss: He said 'among the Jews' only because not all the Jews distorted; rather it was their rabbis and their scholars who distorted

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن الله تعالى لا يغفر الشرك أصلا، لكن أجمعت الامه على أنه لا يغفره مع عدم التوبة، فأما إذا تاب منه فانه يغفره

sources.gloss: The apparent sense of the verse indicates that Allah does not forgive shirk at all, but the community is agreed that He does not forgive it where there is no repentance; as for one who repents of it, He forgives him

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وافتراؤهم الكذب على الله ها هنا المراد به تزكيتهم لأنفسهم بانا { أبناء الله وأحباؤه }

sources.gloss: Their fabricating of lies against Allah here refers to their purifying of themselves by saying 'we are the sons of God and His beloved'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: الحائض والجنب لا يدخلان المسجد إلا مجتازين فإن الله تعالى يقول: { ولا جنباً إلا عابري سبيل حتى تغتسلوا }

sources.gloss: The menstruating woman and the one in janabah do not enter the mosque except as passers-through, for Allah says: 'nor in the state of ritual impurity, except while passing through, until you have washed'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني ضلوا في أمير المؤمنين { ويريدون أن تضلوا السبيل } يعني أخرجوا الناس من ولاية أمير المؤمنين، وهو الصراط المستقيم

sources.gloss: meaning they went astray concerning Amir al-Mu'minin; 'and desire that you should lose the way' means they took people out of the wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin, which is the straight path

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله سبحانه نهى المؤمنين أن يقوموا إلى الصلاة و هم سكارى، يعني سكر النوم

sources.gloss: Allah, glory be to Him, forbade the believers to rise to prayer while intoxicated, meaning the intoxication of sleep

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يقولون: (راعنا) أي ارع أحوالنا، و اسمع منا كما نسمع منك، و كان في لغة اليهود معناه: اسمع لا سمعت

sources.gloss: They would say ra'ina, that is: attend to our condition and hear from us as we hear from you; but in the language of the Jews its meaning was: hear, may you not hear

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزل جبرئيل (عليه السلام) على محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) بهذه الآية هكذا: يا أيها الذين أوتوا الكتاب آمنوا بما نزلنا في علي نورا مبينا

sources.gloss: Gabriel came down to Muhammad with this verse thus: O you who were given the Book, believe in what We have sent down concerning Ali, a manifest light

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن الكاظم عليه السلام أن المراد به سكر الشراب ثم نسختها تحريم الخمر

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from al-Kazim: what is meant by it is the intoxication of drink, and then the prohibition of wine abrogated it

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام ان المعنى نطمسها عن الهدى فنردها على ادبارها في ضلالتها بحيث لا يفلح ابداً

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from al-Baqir: the meaning is that We blot them out from guidance and turn them back upon their traces in their error, so that they never prosper

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: نزلت في اليهود والنصارى حيث قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه وقالوا لن يدخل الجنة الا من كان هوداً أو نصارى

sources.gloss: It was revealed about the Jews and the Christians, when they said 'we are the sons of God and His beloved' and said 'none will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن مجاهد في قوله: { وَأَنتُمْ سُكَـٰرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ } قال: نهوا أن يصلوا وهم سكارى، ثم نسخها تحريم الخمر

sources.gloss: From Mujahid on 'when you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying': they were forbidden to pray while intoxicated, then the prohibition of wine abrogated it

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: والجمهور من العلماء وجماعة الفقهاء على أن المراد بالسكر سكر الخمر إلا الضحاك فإنه قال: المراد سكر النوم

sources.gloss: The body of the scholars and the jurists hold that what is meant by intoxication is intoxication from wine, except al-Dahhak, who said what is meant is the intoxication of sleep

sources.author: shaykh muhammad asif al-muhsini

excerpt.text: فالروايات الواردة في بعض آيات القرآن الناطقة بأن الجملة نزلت هكذا أي زائدا على ما في القرآن الموجود لا دلالة لها على نقص القرآن و تحريفه

sources.gloss: So the reports about certain verses which state that a phrase came down in this way, that is, with more than what is in the Quran we have, carry no indication of any deficiency or alteration in the Quran

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِنَّ الله لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الْكَبَائِرَ فَمَا سِوَاهَا قَالَ قُلْتُ دَخَلَتِ الْكَبَائِرُ فِي الإسْتِثْنَاءِ قَالَ نَعَمْ

sources.gloss: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes': the major sins and what is lesser. I said: do the major sins enter into the exception? He said: yes

sources.author: al-sharif al-radi

excerpt.text: فَأَمَّا الظُّلْمُ الَّذِي لاَ يُغْفَرُ فَالشِّرْكُ بِاللهِ، قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّـهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾

sources.gloss: As for the wrong that is not forgiven, it is ascribing partners to Allah; Allah has said: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him'

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: ما في القرآن آية أحب إلي من قوله عز وجل: (إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء)

sources.gloss: There is no verse in the Quran more beloved to me than His word: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that partners should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes'

title.en: Envy, trusts and those in authority

essay.en:
Have you not regarded those who were given a share of the Book: the passage opens with a scene the Prophet is told to look at, men of scripture who believe in idols and fake deities and tell the pagans that theirs is the better guided way. Tabrisi reports the reading of most exegetes, that after Uhud Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf rode to Mecca with seventy Jewish riders to ally with Quraysh; they asked him to prostrate to two idols first, and when Abu Sufyan recited Quraysh's services to the pilgrims and asked whose way was better, Ka'b answered that theirs was [3]. Tusi lists five readings of jibt and taghut: two idols, the idols and their spokesmen, sorcery and Satan, a sorcerer and a soothsayer, or the two Jewish chiefs themselves [8]. The verdict follows: a curse, exclusion from Allah's mercy as punishment [3], and no helper who can shield a man from the punishment Allah brings [9].

Two questions then expose the motive. Do they hold sovereignty? Tabrisi answers that the judgement was never theirs to make, since the sovereignty is not, and had they held it they would not have parted with a speck [4]. Do they envy? Tusi reports the envied people as the Prophet, with al-Baqir adding: and his family; the bounty is prophethood, and in his family the Imamate; the great sovereignty is the caliphate, and whoever obeys them obeys Allah [11]. Abraham's line already held Book, wisdom and kingdom, and even there some believed and some barred the way.

Refusal is answered by fire and by skins renewed as they scorch. Tabrisi lists three readings of that renewal [5]; Tusi settles on the same skin restored rather than an innocent one punished [13]. Facing it stands the garden with its deep shade.

The address then turns to the community: deliver the trusts, judge justly. Tabrisi records three readings of the command, every trust, those in authority, or the key of the Kaaba [6], and Tabatabai notes that some counted this verse Meccan and excepted it from the Medinan surah, though he finds it tied to what precedes [1]. Then obedience. Tabatabai reads obey Allah and obey the Apostle as the ground laid for referring disputes back [2]; Tabrisi and Tusi report from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that those vested with authority are the Imams of Muhammad's family, since unrestricted obedience can be owed only to one whose infallibility is established [7][16].

note.en: Fayd Kashani: jibt was in origin the name of an idol and came to be used for whatever is worshipped besides Allah, while taghut covers Satan and every falsehood [27].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يقولون لأئمة الضلالة و الدعاة إلى النار: هؤلاء أهدى من آل محمد سبيلا … { أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ } يعني الإمامة و الخلافة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Amir al-Ashari, from Mualla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ahmad ibn Aidh, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd al-Ijli, from Abu Jafar

text.en: They say of the leaders of misguidance and those who call to the Fire: these are better guided in the way than the family of Muhammad. Do they have a share in sovereignty? means the Imamate and the caliphate.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كل راية ترفع قبل قيام القائم (عليه السلام) فصاحبها طاغوت يعبد من دون الله عز و جل
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Every banner raised before the rising of al-Qa'im: its bearer is a taghut worshipped besides Allah, the Mighty and Glorious.

note.en: Tusi records three glosses of naqir: the speck on the back of the date-stone, the grain inside it, or the mark a man scratches with his fingertip [10].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فنحن الناس ونحن المحسودون على ما أتانا الله من الإمامة دون خلق الله جميعاً … فكيف يقرّون بها في آل إبراهيم ويكذبون بها في آل محمد
narrations.chain: Jafar ibn Ahmad, with a connected chain, from Burayd, from Abu Jafar

text.en: We are the people, and we are the ones envied for the Imamate Allah has given us, to the exclusion of all Allah's creation. So how do they affirm it of the progeny of Abraham and deny it of the family of Muhammad?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قلت قوله: { فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب } قال: النبوة، قلت: والحكمة؟ قال: الفهم والقضاء قلت: وآتيناهم ملكاً عظيماً؟ قال: الطاعة المفروضة
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Yunus, from Abu Jafar al-Ahwal, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked about His words, We have certainly given the progeny of Abraham the Book. He said: prophethood. I said: and wisdom? He said: understanding and judgement. I said: and We have given them a great sovereignty? He said: the obligatory obedience.

note.en: Tusi weighs two readings of believed in him: some of the People of the Book believed in Muhammad, or some of Abraham's community believed in Abraham while others barred the way [12].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ويحك هي هي وهي غيرها … أرأيت لو أن رجلاً أخذ لبنة فكسرها ثم ردها في ملبنها فهي هي وهي غيرها

text.en: Ibn Abi al-Awja asked: what is the sin of the other skin? He said: Woe to you, it is the same and it is another. Suppose a man took a brick, broke it, then returned it to its mould: it is the same and it is another.

note.en: Tusi: a shade can be pierced by heat, so the garden's is called deep; and it is narrated that a rider travels a hundred years in the shade of its tree of eternity [14].
Tabrisi cites a report from the Imams: two verses, one of them ours and the other yours, the trust addressed to them and the obedience commanded of the community [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إيانا عنى، أن يؤدي الإمام الأول منا إلى الإمام الذي بعده الكتب و العلم و السلاح
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mualla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Ahmad ibn Aidh, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd al-Ijli, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He meant us: that the first Imam among us hands on to the Imam after him the books, the knowledge and the weapon.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: هذه مخاطبة لنا خاصة أمر الله تبارك وتعالى كل إمام منا أن يؤدي إلى الامام الذي بعده ويوصي إليه ثم هي جارية في سائر الأمانات
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman

text.en: This is an address to us in particular. Allah commanded every Imam among us to deliver to the Imam after him and to make his bequest to him; then it runs on through the rest of the trusts.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: عليكم بأداء الأمانة فلو أن قاتل أبي الحسين بن علي عليهما السلام ائتمنني على السيف الذي قتله به لأديته إليه
narrations.chain: Musa ibn Jafar, from his father, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: Hold fast to delivering the trust. If the killer of my father, al-Husayn ibn Ali, entrusted me with the sword by which he killed him, I would deliver it back to him.

note.en: Tusi: referring back to Allah means to His Book, and referring back to the Messenger means to his Sunna [16].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: هم خلفائي- يا جابر- و أئمة المسلمين من بعدي، أولهم علي بن أبي طالب، ثم الحسن، ثم الحسين، ثم علي بن الحسين، ثم محمد بن علي المعروف في التوراة بالباقر … ثم سميي و كنيي حجة الله في أرضه، و بقيته في عباده ابن الحسن بن علي
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Jafar ibn Muhammad al-Fazari, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Samaa, from Ahmad ibn al-Harith, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Jufi, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari

text.en: They are my caliphs, Jabir, and the Imams of the Muslims after me: first Ali ibn Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali, known in the Torah as al-Baqir. Then my namesake, Allah's proof in His earth, the son of al-Hasan ibn Ali.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِيانا عنى خاصة أمر جميع المؤمنين إلى يوم القيامة بطاعتنا

text.en: He meant us in particular: He commanded all the believers, to the Day of Resurrection, to obey us.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت في علي بن ابي طالب والحسن والحسين عليهم الصلاة والسلام … نزلت الصلاة ولم يسم الله لهم ثلاثاً ولا أربعاً حتى كان رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فسر ذلك لهم

text.en: It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. The prayer was revealed and Allah did not name three cycles or four for them, until it was the Messenger of Allah who explained that to them.

perspectives.en: On those vested with authority the traditions part. Tabrisi and Tusi report from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that they are the Imams of Muhammad's family, since Allah joins obedience to them with obedience to Himself without restriction, and such obedience is owed only to one whose infallibility is established [7][16]. Tabari records instead that they are the rulers, and Ibn Abbas's report that the verse came down about Abd Allah ibn Hudhafa, whom the Prophet sent out on an expedition [41]. Razi grants that absolute obedience implies an infallible, but argues no faction of the community can be meant, so the consensus of the whole community is the proof [58].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وإن ذكر بعضهم أنها مكية واستثناها في آيتين من سورة النساء المدنية … لكن الآية ظاهرة الارتباط بما قبلها من الآيات

sources.gloss: Though some mentioned that it is Meccan and excepted it, among two verses of the Medinan Surah al-Nisa ... but the verse is plainly connected to the verses before it.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولا ينبغي أن يرتاب في أن قوله أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول جملة سيقت تمهيداً وتوطئة للأمر برد الأمر إلى الله ورسوله عند ظهور التنازع

sources.gloss: There should be no doubt that His words obey Allah and obey the Apostle are a sentence brought as a preface and ground for the command to refer the matter back to Allah and His Messenger when a dispute appears.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهو قول أكثر المفسرين أن كعب بن الأشرف خرج في سبعين راكباً من اليهود إلى مكة بعد وقعة أُحد ليحالفوا قريشاً على رسول الله … فاسجد لهذين الصنمين وآمن بهما ففعل … أنتم والله أهدى سبيلاً مما عليه محمد … واللعنة: الإبعاد من رحمة الله عقاباً على معصيته

sources.gloss: It is the view of most exegetes that Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went out with seventy riders of the Jews to Mecca after the battle of Uhud to ally with Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah ... prostrate to these two idols and believe in them, and he did ... By God, you are better guided in the way than what Muhammad is upon ... and the curse is removal from the mercy of Allah as punishment for disobedience.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: بيَّن الله سبحانه أن الحكم ليس إليهم إذ الملك ليس لهم … أي لو أعطوا الدنيا، وملكها لما أعطوا الناس من الحقوق قليلاً ولا كثيراً

sources.gloss: Allah made clear that the judgement is not theirs to make, since the sovereignty is not theirs ... that is, were they given the world and its kingdom they would not give people their rights, little or much.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن الله تعالى يجدّد لهم جلوداً غير الجلود التي احترقت على ظاهر القرآن في أنها غيرها … وثانيها: أن الله يجدّدها بأن يردّها إلى الحالة التي كانت عليها غير محترقة … وثالثها: أن التبديل إنما هو للسرابيل

sources.gloss: That Allah renews for them skins other than the skins that burned, on the apparent sense of the Qur'an that they are other ... the second: that Allah renews them by returning them to the state they were in, unburnt ... the third: that the replacement is only of the garments.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أحدها: أنها في كل من اؤتمن أمانة من الأمانات … وثانيها: أن المراد به ولاة الأمر … وثالثها: أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بردِّ مفتاح الكعبة إلى عثمان بن طلحة … وروي عنهم أنهم قالوا: آيتان إحداهما لنا، والأُخرى لكم

sources.gloss: The first: that it concerns everyone entrusted with a trust ... the second: that what is meant is those in authority ... the third: that it is an address to the Prophet to return the key of the Kaaba to Uthman ibn Talha ... and it is narrated from them that they said: two verses, one of them is ours and the other is yours.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لمَّا بدأ في الآية المتقدمة بحثِّ الولاة على تأدية حقوق الرعية … ثناه في هذه الآية بحث الرعية على طاعتهم … وأما أصحابنا فإنهم رووا عن الباقر والصادق ع أن أُولي الأمر هم الأئمة من آل محمد أوجب الله طاعتهم بالإطلاق … ولا يجوز أن يوجب الله طاعة أحد على الإطلاق إلاَّ من ثبتت عصمته

sources.gloss: Since He began in the preceding verse by urging those in authority to render the rights of the people ... He followed it in this verse by urging the people to obey them ... As for our companions, they narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that those vested with authority are the Imams of the family of Muhammad, whose obedience Allah made obligatory without restriction ... and Allah may not make obedience to anyone obligatory without restriction except one whose infallibility is established.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل في معنى الجبت، والطاغوت خمسة أقوال … أحدها - قال عكرمة: إنهما صنمان … والخامس - في رواية عن ابن عباس والضحاك: ان الجبت حي بن أخطب، والطاغوت كعب بن الاشرف

sources.gloss: Five views were given on the meaning of jibt and taghut ... the first, from Ikrima: they are two idols ... the fifth, in a narration from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak: jibt is Huyayy ibn Akhtab and taghut is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فلن تجد له نصيراً } ينصره من عقاب الله الذي يحله به مما قد أعده له

sources.gloss: You will never find any helper for him: none to help him against the punishment of Allah which He brings upon him, from what He has readied for him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقيل في معنى النقير ها هنا ثلاثة أقوال … إنه النقطة التي في ظهر النواة. وقال مجاهد: هو الحبة التي في بطن النواة. وفي رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس أن النقير ما نقر الرجل باصبعه

sources.gloss: Three views were given here on the meaning of naqir ... that it is the speck on the back of the date-stone; Mujahid said it is the grain inside the stone; and in another narration from Ibn Abbas, naqir is what a man scratches with his finger.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: إنه النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم)، وهو قول أبي جعفر (ع)، وزاد فيه وآله … أحدهما - قال الحسن، وقتادة، وابن جريج: النبوة. وهو قول أبي جعفر (ع) قال وفي آله الامامة … وقال أبو جعفر (ع): انه الخلافة، من أطاعهم، أطاع الله ومن عصاهم عصى الله

sources.gloss: That it is the Prophet, which is the view of Abu Jafar, who added: and his family ... the first, from al-Hasan, Qatada and Ibn Jurayj: prophethood; and it is the view of Abu Jafar, who said: and in his family, the Imamate ... and Abu Jafar said: it is the caliphate; whoever obeys them has obeyed Allah and whoever disobeys them has disobeyed Allah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: إن من أهل الكتاب من آمن بمحمد … الثاني - فمن أمة ابراهيم من آمن بابراهيم، ومنهم من صدّ عنه

sources.gloss: That among the People of the Book are those who believed in Muhammad ... the second: among Abraham's community are those who believed in Abraham, and among them are those who barred the way from him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والجواب الثاني - اختاره البلخي والجبائي، والزجاج: ان الله تعالى يجددها بان يردها إلى الحالة التي كانت عليها غير محترقة … وهذا هو المعتمد عليه

sources.gloss: The second answer, chosen by al-Balkhi, al-Jubbai and al-Zajjaj: that Allah renews them by returning them to the state they were in, unburnt ... and this is the one relied upon.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن: ربما كان ظل ليس بظليل، لأنه يدخله الحر والسموم، فلذلك وصف ظل الجنة بأنه ظليل … وروي أن في الجنة شجرة يسير الراكب في ظلها مائة عام، لا يقطعها وهي شجرة الخلد

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: a shade may not be deep, because heat and scorching wind enter it, and for that reason the shade of the Garden is described as deep ... and it is narrated that in the Garden is a tree in whose shade a rider travels a hundred years without crossing it, and it is the tree of eternity.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فمعنى الرد إلى الله هو إلى كتابه والرد إلى رسوله هو الرد إلى سنته … وروى أصحابنا عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله (ع) أنهم الأئمة من آل محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فلذلك أوجب الله تعالى طاعتهم بالاطلاق

sources.gloss: The meaning of referring back to Allah is to His Book, and referring back to His Messenger is referring back to his Sunna ... and our companions narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah that they are the Imams of the family of Muhammad, and for that reason Allah made obedience to them obligatory without restriction.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قلت قوله: { فقد آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب } قال: النبوة، قلت: والحكمة؟ قال: الفهم والقضاء قلت: وآتيناهم ملكاً عظيماً؟ قال: الطاعة المفروضة

sources.gloss: I said: His words, We have certainly given the progeny of Abraham the Book. He said: prophethood. I said: and wisdom? He said: understanding and judgement. I said: and We have given them a great sovereignty? He said: the obligatory obedience.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يقولون لأئمة الضلالة و الدعاة إلى النار: هؤلاء أهدى من آل محمد سبيلا … { أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ } يعني الإمامة و الخلافة … كل راية ترفع قبل قيام القائم (عليه السلام) فصاحبها طاغوت يعبد من دون الله عز و جل

sources.gloss: They say of the leaders of misguidance and the callers to the Fire: these are better guided in the way than the family of Muhammad ... Do they have a share in sovereignty means the Imamate and the caliphate ... Every banner raised before the rising of al-Qa'im, its bearer is a taghut worshipped besides Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إيانا عنى، أن يؤدي الإمام الأول منا إلى الإمام الذي بعده الكتب و العلم و السلاح

sources.gloss: He meant us: that the first Imam among us delivers to the Imam after him the books, the knowledge and the weapon.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هم خلفائي- يا جابر- و أئمة المسلمين من بعدي، أولهم علي بن أبي طالب، ثم الحسن، ثم الحسين، ثم علي بن الحسين، ثم محمد بن علي المعروف في التوراة بالباقر … ثم سميي و كنيي حجة الله في أرضه، و بقيته في عباده ابن الحسن بن علي

sources.gloss: They are my caliphs, Jabir, and the Imams of the Muslims after me: the first of them is Ali ibn Abi Talib, then al-Hasan, then al-Husayn, then Ali ibn al-Husayn, then Muhammad ibn Ali, known in the Torah as al-Baqir ... then my namesake and kunya-sake, the proof of Allah in His earth and His remnant among His servants, the son of al-Hasan ibn Ali.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: أقول: الجبت في الأصل اسم صنم فاستعمل في كل ما عبد من دون الله تعالى والطاغوت يطلق على الشيطان وعلى كل باطل من معبود أو غيره

sources.gloss: I say: jibt is in origin the name of an idol, then it was used for everything worshipped besides Allah, and taghut is applied to Satan and to every falsehood, whether an object of worship or otherwise.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ويحك هي هي وهي غيرها … أرأيت لو أن رجلاً أخذ لبنة فكسرها ثم ردها في ملبنها فهي هي وهي غيرها

sources.gloss: Woe to you, it is the same one and it is another ... Consider: if a man took a brick and broke it, then returned it to its mould, it is the same one and it is another.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إِيانا عنى خاصة أمر جميع المؤمنين إلى يوم القيامة بطاعتنا … نزلت في علي بن ابي طالب والحسن والحسين عليهم الصلاة والسلام … نزلت الصلاة ولم يسم الله لهم ثلاثاً ولا أربعاً حتى كان رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فسر ذلك لهم

sources.gloss: He meant us in particular; He commanded all the believers until the Day of Resurrection to obey us ... It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan and al-Husayn ... The prayer was revealed and Allah did not name three or four for them until it was the Messenger of Allah who explained that to them.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: فنحن الناس ونحن المحسودون على ما أتانا الله من الإمامة دون خلق الله جميعاً … فكيف يقرّون بها في آل إبراهيم ويكذبون بها في آل محمد

sources.gloss: We are the people, and we are the ones envied for the Imamate Allah has given us, to the exclusion of all Allah's creation ... So how do they affirm it of the progeny of Abraham and belie it of the family of Muhammad?

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فقال بعضهم هم الأمراء … نزلت في عبد الله بن حذافة بن قيس السهمي إذ بعثه النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم في السرية

sources.gloss: Some of them said: they are the rulers ... it was revealed about Abd Allah ibn Hudhafa ibn Qays al-Sahmi when the Prophet sent him out on an expedition.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: اعلم أن قوله: { وَأُوْلِى ٱلأمْرِ مِنْكُمْ } يدل عندنا على أن إجماع الأمة حجة … فثبت قطعاً أن أولي الأمر المذكور في هذه الآية لا بد وأن يكون معصوما … لا جائز أن يكون بعض الأمة

sources.gloss: Know that His words, and those vested with authority among you, indicate for us that the consensus of the community is a proof ... so it is established with certainty that those vested with authority mentioned in this verse must be infallible ... it cannot be a part of the community.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: هذه مخاطبة لنا خاصة أمر الله تبارك وتعالى كل إمام منا أن يؤدي إلى الامام الذي بعده ويوصي إليه ثم هي جارية في سائر الأمانات … عليكم بأداء الأمانة فلو أن قاتل أبي الحسين بن علي عليهما السلام ائتمنني على السيف الذي قتله به لأديته إليه

sources.gloss: This is an address to us in particular: Allah commanded every Imam among us to deliver to the Imam after him and to bequeath to him, and then it runs on through the rest of the trusts ... You must deliver the trust: if the killer of my father al-Husayn ibn Ali entrusted me with the sword by which he killed him, I would deliver it to him.

essay.en:
The passage opens on people who claim to believe in what was sent down to Muhammad and in what came before him, and who nevertheless want their quarrels settled by fake deities. Tabatabai reads the whole run as still turning on the command to obey God and His Apostle, which he says was set down as a preface to the order that disputes be referred back to God and His Apostle [1]. Tabrisi reports that most commentators trace the verse to a quarrel between a Jew and a hypocrite: the Jew wanted the Prophet's court, knowing he took no bribe, and the hypocrite wanted Kab ibn al-Ashraf, knowing that he did [2]. Qummi names other parties, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and a Jewish man disputing over a garden [17].

Called to what God has sent down and to the Apostle, they keep away; Qummi says this verse has run upon all the enemies of the family of Muhammad [18]. Then an affliction lands, and they come swearing they desired nothing but to do good and to bring about comity, an excuse Tabrisi unpacks as the claim that they were sparing the Prophet trouble and wanted a mediator rather than a verdict that breeds rancour [3]. God knows their hearts; the Prophet is told to let them be, to advise them, and to speak words that reach all the way in.

Verse 64 says why any apostle is sent at all: to be obeyed. Verse 65 turns that into an oath. Tusi reports from al-Baqir that the quarrel behind it lay between Zubayr and Hatib ibn Abi Baltaa [13]. Faith is not faith until the verdict is taken without inward constriction and with full submission.

The hypothetical that follows measures how far such submission would go. Tusi sets it against the command once laid on the people of Musa, who did slay themselves and were led out into the wilderness [14], and reads the guidance promised afterwards as the kindness that holds a person firm in obedience; Abu Ali, whom he quotes, takes it instead as being led on the road to paradise in the hereafter, and denies that guidance here means direction to religion [15]. The passage ends on company rather than command: Tabrisi reports that it came down about Thawban, who loved the Prophet and feared that after death he would never see him again [7].

note.en: Tusi glosses taghut as one possessed of transgression: anything worshipped besides God, and anyone who judges contrary to God's ruling [8]. Tabrisi refers 'they were commanded to reject them' back to 2:256 [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وروى أصحابنا عن السيدين الباقر ع والصادق ع أن المعني به كل من يتحاكم إليه ممن يحكم بغير الحق

text.en: Our companions have narrated from the two masters al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that what is meant by it is everyone to whom a case is taken for judgment who judges by other than the truth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من تحاكم إلى الطاغوت فحكم له فانما يأخذ سحتاً وان كان حقه ثابتاً لأنه أخذ بحكم الطاغوت وقد امر الله أن يكفر به … انظروا إلى من كان منكم قد روى حديثنا ونظر في حلالنا وحرامنا وعرف أحكامنا فارضوا به حكماً فإني قد جعلته عليكم حاكماً

text.en: Asked whether two companions in dispute may go to the ruler or the judges, he said: Whoever takes a case to the taghut and is judged in his favour takes only unlawful gain, even if his right is sound. Look to one of you who has related our hadith and knows our rulings; I have appointed him judge over you.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: المصيبة هي الخسف و الله بالمنافقين عند الحوض
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur, from Abu Abdillah and from Abu Jafar

text.en: The affliction is, by God, the sinking down that takes the hypocrites at the Pool.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: فهذا مما تأويله بعد تنزيله في القيامة، تنزيله: إذا بعثهم الله حلفوا لرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) إنما أردنا بما فعلنا من إزالة الخلافة عن موضعها إلا إحسانا و توفيقا

text.en: This is of that whose interpretation comes after its revelation, at the resurrection. When God raises them they will swear to the Messenger of God: by what we did in removing the caliphate from its place we desired nothing but to do good and to bring about comity.

note.en: Tusi carries al-Hasan's reading of the far-reaching word: tell them that if they show what is in their hearts they will be killed, since nothing reaches further into them [11].

narrations.speaker: Abu al-Hasan the First
narrations.arabic: فقد سبقت عليهم كلمة الشقاء و سبق لهم العذاب
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu Junada al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhariq, from Abu al-Hasan the First

text.en: The word of wretchedness has already gone forth against them, and the punishment has already been set for them.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: { أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ } يعني من العداوة لعلي (عليه السلام) في الدنيا { فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَعِظْهُمْ وَقُل لَّهُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلاً بَلِيغاً } أي أبلغهم في الحجة عليهم و أخر أمرهم إلى يوم القيامة

text.en: 'They are the ones whom Allah knows as to what is in their hearts', meaning of enmity to Ali in this world; 'so let them alone, and advise them, and speak to them concerning themselves far-reaching words', that is, press the proof home against them, and their affair is deferred to the day of resurrection.

note.en: Tabrisi takes 'by Allah's leave' as by Allah's command, which establishes that the messengers must be obeyed [4]. Tusi adds that no one should seek forgiveness while persisting in the sin [12].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لَقَدْ خَاطَبَ الله أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) فِي كِتَابِهِ قَالَ قُلْتُ فِي أَيِّ مَوْضِعٍ قَالَ فِي قَوْلِهِ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ جاؤُكَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا الله وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُوا الله تَوَّاباً رَحِيماً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara or Burayd, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God has addressed the Commander of the Faithful in His Book. I said: in which place? He said: in His words, 'Had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you and pleaded to Allah for forgiveness, and the Apostle had pleaded for them, they would surely have found Allah all-clement, all-merciful.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاؤوك يا علي فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله تواباً رحيماً هكذا نزلت
narrations.chain: his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: 'Had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you, O Ali, and pleaded to Allah for forgiveness, and the Apostle had pleaded for them, they would surely have found Allah all-clement, all-merciful.' Thus was it revealed.

note.en: The dissent named here is a constriction of the breast; Tabrisi cites Mujahid that it means doubt that what the Prophet has said is true [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لَوْ أَنَّ قَوْماً عَبَدُوا الله وَحْدَهُ لا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَحَجُّوا الْبَيْتَ وَصَامُوا شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ ثُمَّ قَالُوا لِشَيْ‏ءٍ صَنَعَهُ الله أَوْ صَنَعَهُ رَسُولُ الله (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) أَلا صَنَعَ خِلافَ الَّذِي صَنَعَ أَوْ وَجَدُوا ذَلِكَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ لَكَانُوا بِذَلِكَ مُشْرِكِينَ … عَلَيْكُمْ بِالتَّسْلِيمِ
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: If a people worshipped God alone with no partner, kept the prayer, gave the zakat, made the hajj and fasted Ramadan, then said of something God or His Messenger had done, 'Would that it were done otherwise,' or found that in their hearts, they would be polytheists by it. Hold to submission.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: التسليم: الرضا و القنوع بقضائه
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Submission is contentment and satisfaction with His decree.

note.en: Tabrisi records that Ibn Amir alone read 'except a few' in the accusative, as it stands in the codices of Syria, while the others read it in the nominative [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ ٱقْتُلُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ } و سلموا للإمام تسليما { أَوِ ٱخْرُجُواْ مِن دِيَارِكُمْ } رضا له { مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ وَلَوْ } أن أهل الخلاف { فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتاً }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'Had We prescribed for them: Slay your folks', and submit to the Imam in full submission, 'or leave your habitations', out of contentment with him, 'they would not have done it except a few of them. And if' the people of opposition 'had done as they were advised, it would have been better for them.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هكذا نزلت هذه الآية: و لو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به في علي لكان خيرا لهم
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Abd al-Azim, from Bakkar, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Thus was this verse revealed: 'And if they had done as they were advised regarding Ali, it would have been better for them.'

note.en: Tusi says being with the blessed means enjoying the sight of the prophets, visiting them and being present with them; no one should imagine that their rank in the highest heights puts them out of reach [16].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: { وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ وَٱلصِّدِّيقِينَ } علي بن أبي طالب { وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ } الحسن و الحسين { وَٱلصَّالِحِينَ } حمزة { وَحَسُنَ أُولَـٰئِكَ رَفِيقاً } الأئمة الاثنا عشر بعدي
