narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from al-Muafa ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Abi Harasa, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Uthman ibn Abi Shayba, from Hariz, from al-Amash, from al-Hakam ibn Utayba, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Umm Salama

text.en: 'Whoever obeys Allah and the Apostle, they are with those whom Allah has blessed, including the prophets and the truthful', Ali ibn Abi Talib, 'the martyrs', al-Hasan and al-Husayn, 'and the righteous', Hamza, 'and excellent companions are they', the twelve Imams after me.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أعينونا بالورع فإنه من لقي الله عز و جل منكم بالورع كان له عند الله فرجا … فمنا النبي، و منا الصديق، و منا الشهداء، و منا الصالحون
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Help us by scrupulousness, for whoever of you meets God with scrupulousness will have relief with Him. Of us is the Prophet, of us is the truthful one, of us are the martyrs, and of us are the righteous.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا أبا محمد، لقد ذكركم الله في كتابه، فقال: … فرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) في الآية النبيون، و نحن في هذا الموضع الصديقون و الشهداء، و أنتم الصالحون، فتسموا بالصلاح كما سماكم الله عز و جل
narrations.chain: a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Abu Muhammad, God has mentioned you in His Book. The Messenger of God is the prophets in the verse; we in this place are the truthful and the martyrs; and you are the righteous. So name yourselves with righteousness, as God has named you.

perspectives.en: The phrase 'except a few of them' is where the readings part. Al-Qurtubi collects the names the Sunni tradition gives that few: Abu Bakr, Umar and Thabit ibn Qays, with al-Hasan and Muqatil adding Ammar and Ibn Masud [49]. Ibn Kathir carries the report that the Prophet pointed to Abdullah ibn Rawaha and said that had God prescribed it, this man would be among them [44]. The Shia narrations take the verse elsewhere: al-Sadiq glosses 'slay your folks' as submitting to the Imam and 'leave your habitations' as contentment with him, and al-Baqir reads what they were advised as concerning Ali [28].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولا ينبغي أن يرتاب في أن قوله أطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول جملة سيقت تمهيداً وتوطئة للأمر برد الأمر إلى الله ورسوله عند ظهور التنازع

sources.gloss: There is no room for doubt that His words 'Obey Allah and obey the Apostle' are a sentence set down as a preface and preparation for the command to refer the matter back to Allah and His Apostle when a dispute appears.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: كان بين رجل من اليهود ورجل من المنافقين خصومة. فقال اليهودي: أحاكم إلى محمد لأَنه علم أنه لا يقبل الرشوة ولا يجور في الحكم فقال المنافق: لا بل بيني وبينك كعب بن الأَشرف لأنه علم أنه يأخذ الرشوة فنزلت الآية عن أكثر المفسرين.

sources.gloss: There was a dispute between a man of the Jews and a man of the hypocrites. The Jew said, 'I take the case to Muhammad,' because he knew that he accepts no bribe and does not deviate in judgment. The hypocrite said, 'No, rather Kab ibn al-Ashraf between me and you,' because he knew that he takes bribes. So the verse came down; from most of the commentators.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي ما أردنا بالتحاكم إلى غيرك إلا التخفيف عنك، فإنا نحتشمك برفع الصوت في مجلسك، ونقتصر على من يتوسط لنا برضاء الخصمين دون الحكم المورث للضغائن

sources.gloss: That is: by taking the case to someone other than you we intended only to lighten your burden, for we are abashed before you at raising voices in your assembly, and we confined ourselves to one who would mediate for us to the satisfaction of both parties, rather than a verdict that breeds rancour.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقولـه: { بإذن الله } أي بأمر الله الذي دلّ به على وجوب طاعتهم

sources.gloss: His words 'by Allah's leave' mean by Allah's command, by which He indicated the obligation of obeying them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { حرجاً } أي شكاً في أن ما قلته حق عن مجاهد

sources.gloss: 'Any dissent' means doubt that what you have said is true; from Mujahid.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده إلا قليلاً بالنصب، وهو كذلك في مصاحف أهل الشام، وقرأ الباقون بالرفع

sources.gloss: Ibn Amir alone read 'except a few' in the accusative, and so it stands in the codices of the people of Syria; the rest read it in the nominative.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان شديد الحب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قليل الصبر عنه

sources.gloss: It came down about Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah, who loved the Messenger of Allah intensely and had little patience away from him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى الطاغوت ذو الطغيان - على جهة المبالغة في الصفة - فكل من يعبد من دون الله فهو طاغوت، وقد تسمى به الأوثان كما تسمى بأنها رجس من عمل الشيطان، ويوصف به كل من طغى، بأن حكم بخلاف حكم الله تعالى غير راض بحكمه تعالى

sources.gloss: The meaning of taghut is one possessed of transgression, by way of intensification in the description; so everyone worshipped besides Allah is a taghut, and idols are so named, as they are called a defilement of Satan's work; and the term describes everyone who transgresses by judging contrary to Allah's ruling, not content with His judgment.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الحسن: القول البليغ الذي أمر به في الآية أن يقول: إن أظهرتم ما في قلوبكم قتلتكم، فهذا يبلغ من نفوسهم كل مبلغ

sources.gloss: Al-Hasan said: the far-reaching word he is commanded to speak in the verse is that he say, 'If you show what is in your hearts I will kill you'; this reaches every extent in their souls.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولا ينبغي لأحد أن يستغفر مع كونه مصراً على المعصية بل ينبغي أن يتوب ويندم على ما فعل ويعزم على أن لا يعود إلى مثله ثم يستغفر باللسان ليتوب الله عليه

sources.gloss: No one should seek forgiveness while persisting in disobedience; rather he should repent, regret what he has done, resolve not to return to its like, then seek forgiveness with the tongue so that Allah may turn to him.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال أبو جعفر (ع) كانت الخصوصة بين الزبير، وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة

sources.gloss: Abu Jafar said the dispute was between al-Zubayr and Hatib ibn Abi Baltaa.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أي لو أنا ألزمناهم وأوجبنا عليهم { أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم } أي لو كتبنا عليهم ذلك - كما أوجبنا على قوم موسى وقتلوا أنفسهم وأخرجهم إلى التيه - ما فعله هؤلاء للمشقة التي فيه

sources.gloss: That is, had We bound them and made obligatory upon them 'Slay your folks or leave your habitations', as We made it obligatory on the people of Musa, and they slew themselves and He brought them out into the wilderness, these would not have done it, because of the hardship in it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { ولهديناهم } معناه ولفعلنا من اللطف بهم ما يثبتون معه على الطاعة، ولزوم الاستقامة … وقال أبو علي: معناه الأخذ بهم على طريق الجنة في الآخرة. قال: ولا يجوز أن يكون المراد بالهداية ها هنا الارشاد إلى الدين

sources.gloss: His words 'and We would have guided them' mean: We would have done for them of kindness that with which they would stand firm in obedience and hold to uprightness … Abu Ali said: its meaning is taking them along the road of the Garden in the hereafter. He said: it is not allowable that what is meant by guidance here be direction to religion.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ومعنى قوله: { فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين } انه يستمتع برؤية النبيين وزيارتهم، والحضور معهم. فلا ينبغي أن يتوهم من أجل أنهم في أعلى عليين انه لا يراهم.

sources.gloss: The meaning of 'they are with those whom Allah has blessed, including the prophets' is that he will enjoy the sight of the prophets, visiting them and being present with them; so let no one imagine that because they are in the highest heights he will not see them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإنها نزلت في الزبير بن العوام فإنه نازع رجلاً من اليهود في حديقة فقال الزبير ترضى بابن شيبة اليهودي فقال اليهودي ترضى بمحمد؟

sources.gloss: It came down about al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, for he disputed with a man of the Jews over a garden. Al-Zubayr said, 'Will you accept Ibn Shayba the Jew?' The Jew said, 'Will you accept Muhammad?'

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهم أعداء آل محمد كلهم جرت فيهم هذه الآية

sources.gloss: They are the enemies of the family of Muhammad; upon all of them this verse has run.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ولو أنهم إذ ظلموا أنفسهم جاؤوك يا علي فاستغفروا الله واستغفر لهم الرسول لوجدوا الله تواباً رحيماً هكذا نزلت

sources.gloss: 'Had they, when they wronged themselves, come to you, O Ali, and pleaded to Allah for forgiveness, and the Apostle had pleaded for them, they would surely have found Allah all-clement, all-merciful.' Thus was it revealed.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: المصيبة هي الخسف و الله بالمنافقين عند الحوض

sources.gloss: The affliction is, by God, the sinking down that takes the hypocrites at the Pool.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: التسليم: الرضا و القنوع بقضائه

sources.gloss: Submission is contentment and satisfaction with His decree.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هكذا نزلت هذه الآية: و لو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به في علي لكان خيرا لهم

sources.gloss: Thus was this verse revealed: 'And if they had done as they were advised regarding Ali, it would have been better for them.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فرسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) في الآية النبيون، و نحن في هذا الموضع الصديقون و الشهداء، و أنتم الصالحون

sources.gloss: The Messenger of Allah is the prophets in the verse; we in this place are the truthful and the martyrs; and you are the righteous.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: من تحاكم إلى الطاغوت فحكم له فانما يأخذ سحتاً وان كان حقه ثابتاً لأنه أخذ بحكم الطاغوت وقد امر الله أن يكفر به

sources.gloss: Whoever takes a dispute to the taghut and is judged in his favour takes only unlawful gain, even if his right is established, because he took it by the judgment of the taghut, and Allah has commanded that it be rejected.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أشار رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده هذه إلى عبد الله بن رواحة، فقال " لو أن الله كتب ذلك لكان هذا من أولئك القليل "

sources.gloss: The Messenger of Allah pointed with his hand to Abdullah ibn Rawaha and said, 'Had Allah prescribed that, this man would be among that few.'

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وكان من القليل أبو بكر وعمر وثابت بن قيس كما ذكرنا. وزاد الحسنُ ومُقاتل عمَّاراً وابنَ مسعود وقد ذكرناهما.

sources.gloss: Among the few were Abu Bakr, Umar and Thabit ibn Qays, as we mentioned; al-Hasan and Muqatil added Ammar and Ibn Masud, whom we have also mentioned.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لَقَدْ خَاطَبَ الله أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) فِي كِتَابِهِ

sources.gloss: Allah has addressed the Commander of the Faithful in His Book.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ الله (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) عَلَيْكُمْ بِالتَّسْلِيمِ

sources.gloss: Then Abu Abdillah said: You must hold to submission.

essay.en:
Tabatabai reads these verses as the matter for which the ones before them were a preface: they rouse the believers to fight in the way of Allah, and the trial upon them was severe in the days they came down [1]. The first order is 'Take your precautions.' Of the two readings Tabrisi reports, he judges the sounder to be the one narrated from Abu Jafar: the weapons themselves are called precaution, being the instrument by which what is feared is warded off [2].

Then the ranks are searched from inside. Most commentators, Tabrisi reports, hold that the man who drags his feet came down about the hypocrites, and that is al-Jubbai's choice [3]. Al-Maghribi, cited by Tusi, catches the tone: such men do not wish to be with the believers in good and ill alike, as friends do, but only when there is spoil [9].

Verse 74 answers with a command. Tabrisi holds that its apparent import is obligation, and that the fighter wins one of two goods [4]; Tusi notes that the promise attaches to the fighting itself, not to being killed or to winning [10]. Verse 75 removes the last excuse by naming who is waiting: Muslims left in Mecca who could not emigrate, whose prayer God answered when the Prophet took the city and set Attab ibn Asid over it [5]. The closing verse leaves two roads and no third, and Tabrisi records why Satan's scheme is flimsy: his friends fight on a doubt, the believers on a proof [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: خذوا أسلحتكم سمى الأسلحة حذراً لأن بها يتقى المحذور
narrations.chain: In al-Majma, from al-Baqir

text.en: Take your weapons. He called the weapons precaution because by them what is feared is warded off.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الثبات السرايا والجميع العسكر
narrations.chain: In al-Majma, from al-Baqir

text.en: The companies are the raiding parties, and the mass is the army.

note.en: Tusi explains 'among you': such men are counted among the believers by kinship and close company, and outwardly by the rulings of the law on blood, inheritance and marriage [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: والله لو قال هذه الكلمة أهل الشرق والغرب لكانوا بها خارجين من الإيمان ولكن الله قد سماهم مؤمنين بإقرارهم

text.en: By God, if the people of the East and the West said this word, they would by it be outside of faith. But God has named them believers on account of their profession.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فسماهم مؤمنين و ليس هم بمؤمنين، و لا كرامة … و لو أن أهل السماء و الأرض قالوا: قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن مع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، لكانوا بذلك مشركين
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: He named them believers, and they are not believers, and no honour to them. If the people of heaven and earth said, 'It was Allah's blessing that I was not with the Messenger of Allah,' they would by that be polytheists.

note.en: Fayd Kashani reads 'slain, or he subdues' as teaching the fighter to hold the field until he gains martyrdom or the religion gains victory, his aim being the raising of truth, not death itself [19].

narrations.speaker: the Messenger of God
narrations.arabic: فوق كل برّ بر حتى يقتل في سبيل الله فإذا قتل في سبيل الله فليس فوقه بر
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi and elsewhere, from al-Sadiq, from the Prophet

text.en: Above every act of goodness there is a goodness, until a man is killed in the way of God. When he is killed in the way of God, there is no goodness above it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من قتل في سبيل الله لم يعرفه الله شيئاً من سيئاته

text.en: Whoever is killed in the way of God, God will not make him know anything of his evil deeds.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: كانت خديجة ماتت قبل الهجرة بسنة، و مات أبو طالب بعد موت خديجة بسنة، فلما فقدهما رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) سئم المقام بمكة … فأوحى الله إليه: يا محمد، أخرج من القرية الظالم أهلها و هاجر إلى المدينة، فليس لك اليوم بمكة ناصر
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: Khadijah died a year before the Hijra, and Abu Talib a year after her. When the Messenger of God lost them both he wearied of staying in Mecca. God revealed to him: Muhammad, leave the town whose people are oppressors and emigrate to Medina; you have no helper in Mecca today.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نحن أولئك
narrations.chain: from Humran, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Of 'the oppressed men, women, and children who say, Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are oppressors,' down to 'a helper': We are those.

note.en: Tusi reports disagreement over 'fake gods', whether Satan or whatever is worshipped besides God, and says 'fight the friends of Satan' strengthens the first [12]. Qummi glosses their fighters as Quraysh's polytheists, fighting for idols [15].

perspectives.en: Tabrisi reads verse 75 of the Muslims left behind in Mecca, naming Salamah ibn Hisham, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl, and says God answered them when the Prophet took the city [5]. Qurtubi draws a standing ruling from the same verse: freeing captives is obligatory upon the whole body of Muslims, whether by fighting or by wealth, and he cites Malik that people must ransom captives with all they own [31]. The Shia narrations add an application the Sunni works do not carry: al-Baqir recited the verse of the oppressed, down to 'a helper', and said, 'We are those' [17].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بيان الآيات بالنسبة إلى ما تقدمها - كما ترى - بمنزلة ذي المقدمة بالنسبة إلى المقدمة وهي تحث وتستنهض المؤمنين للجهاد في سبيل الله وقد كانت المحنة شديدة على المؤمنين أيام كانت تنزل هذه الآيات

sources.gloss: These verses stand to what came before them as the main matter stands to its preface; they urge and rouse the believers to strive in the way of Allah, and the trial was severe upon the believers in the days these verses were coming down.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أن معناه خذوا أسلحتكم، سمى الأَسلحة حذراً لأَنها الآلة التي بها يتقى الحذر وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وغيره وأقول: إن هذا القول أصح

sources.gloss: The second is that it means: take your weapons. He called the weapons precaution because they are the instrument by which what is feared is warded off. This is what is narrated from Abu Jafar and others, and I say this view is the sounder.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقال أكثر المفسرين: نزلت في المنافقين وإنما جمع بينهم في الخطاب من جهة الجنس والنسب لا من جهة الإِيمان وهو اختيار الجبائي

sources.gloss: Most of the exegetes said it came down about the hypocrites, and that they are joined with the believers in the address by kind and lineage, not by faith. This is al-Jubbai's choice.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: هذا أمر من الله، وظاهر أمره يقتضي الوجوب … وفيه حثَّ على الجهاد فكأنه قال: هو فائز بإحدى الحسنيين إن غلب أو غلب

sources.gloss: This is a command from God, and the apparent sense of His command requires obligation. In it is an urging to struggle, as if to say: he wins one of the two goods, whether he conquers or is conquered.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل: يريد بذلك قوماً من المسلمين بقوا بمكة ولم يستطيعوا الهجرة منهم سلمة بن هشام والوليد بن الوليد وعيَّاش بن أبي ربيعة، وأبو جندل بن سهيل … فاستجاب الله تعالى دعاءهم، فلما فتح رسول الله مكة صلى الله عليه وسلم جعل الله نبيه لهم ولياً فاستعمل على مكة عتاب بن أسيد فجعله الله لهم نصيراً

sources.gloss: It is said that He means a people of the Muslims who remained in Mecca and were unable to emigrate, among them Salamah ibn Hisham, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiah and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl. God answered their supplication: when the Messenger of God opened Mecca, God made His Prophet their guardian, and he appointed Attab ibn Asid over Mecca, so God made him their helper.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: لضعف دواعي أولياء الشيطان إلى القتال إذ لا بصيرة لهم وإنما يقاتلون بما تدعو إليه الشبهة والمؤمنون يقاتلون بما تدعو إليه الحجة

sources.gloss: It is said: because the motives of Satan's friends for fighting are weak, since they have no insight; they fight only on what a doubt calls them to, while the believers fight on what a proof calls them to.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وانما أضاف المنافقين إليهم لأمرين: أحدهما - ان من عدادكم ودخلائكم. الثاني - أي منكم في الحال الظاهرة، أو حكم الشريعة من حقن الدم، ونحو ذلك من الموارثة، والمناكحة

sources.gloss: He attached the hypocrites to them for two reasons: first, that they are of your number and your intimates; second, that they are of you in outward state, or in the ruling of the sacred law regarding the protection of blood and the like, such as inheritance and marriage.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال الحسين بن علي المغربي: المعنى ليس يتمنون الكون معهم في الخبر، والشر، كأهل المودات، وانما يتمنون ذلك عند الغنيمة كالبعداء يذمهم بسوء العهد مع سوء الدين

sources.gloss: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Maghribi said: the meaning is that they do not wish to be with them in good and in ill, as people of affection do; they wish it only at the booty, like strangers. He blames them for bad faith along with bad religion.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فالوعد على القتال، لا على القتل، والغلبة

sources.gloss: The promise is for the fighting, not for being killed or for victory.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فقال قوم: هو الشيطان. وقال آخرون: هو ما عبد من دون الله … وقوله: { فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان } يقوي قول من قال: المراد بالطاغوت الشيطان

sources.gloss: Some said it is Satan; others said it is whatever is worshipped besides God. His words 'so fight the friends of Satan' strengthen the view of those who said that by fake gods Satan is meant.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال الصادق عليه السلام: والله لو قال هذه الكلمة أهل الشرق والغرب لكانوا بها خارجين من الإيمان ولكن الله قد سماهم مؤمنين بإقرارهم

sources.gloss: Al-Sadiq said: By God, if the people of the East and the West said this word, they would by it be outside of faith; but God has named them believers on account of their profession.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وهم مشركوا قريش يقاتلون على الأصنام

sources.gloss: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, who fight for the idols.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و لو أن أهل السماء و الأرض قالوا: قد أنعم الله علي إذ لم أكن مع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله)، لكانوا بذلك مشركين

sources.gloss: And if the people of heaven and earth said, 'It was Allah's blessing that I was not with the Messenger of Allah,' they would by that be polytheists.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن حمران، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، قال … نحن أولئك

sources.gloss: From Humran, from Abu Jafar, who said, of the oppressed of this verse: We are those.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام خذوا أسلحتكم سمى الأسلحة حذراً لأن بها يتقى المحذور

sources.gloss: In al-Majma, from al-Baqir: take your weapons. He called the weapons precaution because by them what is feared is warded off.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وإنما قال فيقتل أو يغلب تنبيهاً على أن المجاهد ينبغي أن يثبت في المعركة حتى يعز نفسه بالشهادة أو الدين بالظفر والغلبة وأن لا يكون قصده بالذات إلى القتل بل إلى إعلاء الحق وإعزاز الدين

sources.gloss: He said 'slain, or he subdues' only to alert us that the fighter should hold firm in the field until he honours himself by martyrdom or the religion by triumph and victory, and that his aim should not be killing itself but the raising of truth and the strengthening of the religion.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وتخليص الأسارى واجب على جماعة المسلمين إما بالقتال وإما بالأموال … قال مالك: واجب على الناس أن يَفْدُوا الأسارى بجميع أموالهم

sources.gloss: Freeing captives is obligatory upon the whole body of Muslims, whether by fighting or by wealth. Malik said: it is obligatory upon people to ransom captives with all their wealth.

essay.en:
The passage opens on believers who had once pressed for permission to fight. Majma al-Bayan gives al-Kalbi's account: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Miqdad, Qudamah ibn Mazun and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, hard pressed at Mecca, asked leave to fight and were told to keep their hands off, to pray and to give zakat [4]. Al-Tusi records that occasion and also Mujahid's view that the verse portrays the Jews, whose conduct this community is forbidden to copy [13]. Tabatabai reads the early restraint as timing: they were to hold back and raise the rites of the religion until its frame stood firm, and only then would Allah permit them to fight His enemies [1]. When fighting is prescribed, a party fears people as one fears Allah and asks for a respite, and is told that the enjoyments of this world are trifle.

Death reaches them anyway, even in towers, whether those are palaces or castles in the sky [5]. On their charge that ill comes 'from you', al-Tusi reports two readings: Ibn Zayd took it to mean 'by your bad management', while al-Jubbai, al-Balkhi and al-Zajjaj read it as the ill omen of you that has overtaken us [14].

Obedience to the Apostle is obedience to Allah, and al-Tusi draws from this that the Messenger never commands what is wrong [16]. Those who profess obedience and unsay it overnight are left to Allah: al-Tabrisi notes the Prophet is told to overlook them and not to name them, sparing them until Islam is settled [7], while Tabatabai warns that nothing in the wording fixes them as the hypocrites [2].

The test offered is the Quran itself, whose freedom from discrepancy shows its source; al-Tusi finds here the invalidity of blind imitation and the soundness of reasoning in the roots of religion [18]. Then rumour is to be referred back to the Apostle and those in authority; the Prophet is to fight though he ride out with seventy men and meet no battle [9]; every intercession returns a share of what it served [3]; and a greeting is to be met with better or with its like. The passage closes on the gathering, and on the One who cannot lie, since lying comes only of need [23].

note.en: Al-Qummi holds that the command to keep the hands off was revealed at Mecca before the migration and was abrogated when fighting was prescribed at Medina [24].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) في قول الله عز و جل: { لَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَكُمْ } ، قال: " يعني كفوا ألسنتكم "
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, both from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: About the words of Allah, 'Have you not regarded those who were told, Keep your hands off', he said: it means, restrain your tongues.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وَ اللَّهِ لَلَّذِي صَنَعَهُ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ (عليه السلام) كَانَ خَيْراً لِهَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ مِمَّا طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ وَ اللَّهِ لَقَدْ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَ آتُوا الزَّكاةَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ طَاعَةُ الْإِمَامِ وَ طَلَبُوا الْقِتَالَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ مَعَ الْحُسَيْنِ (عليه السلام) قالُوا رَبَّنا لِمَ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنَا الْقِتالَ لَوْ لا أَخَّرْتَنا إِلى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ نُجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَ نَتَّبِعِ الرُّسُلَ أَرَادُوا تَأْخِيرَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى الْقَائِمِ (عليه السلام).
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Sabbah ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: By Allah, what al-Hasan ibn Ali did was better for this community than all the sun rises upon. By Allah, this verse was revealed: it is only obedience to the Imam. They sought fighting, and when fighting was prescribed for them with al-Husayn they asked why, wanting it delayed until the Qaim.

note.en: The previous verse says all is from Allah, this one puts the ill with the servant. Al-Tusi answers that the two speak of different things: blessing and affliction there, obedience and disobedience here [15].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: قَالَ الله يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ بِمَشِيئَتِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الَّذِي تَشَاءُ لِنَفْسِكَ مَا تَشَاءُ وَبِقُوَّتِي أَدَّيْتَ فَرَائِضِي وَبِنِعْمَتِي قَوِيتَ عَلَى مَعْصِيَتِي جَعَلْتُكَ سَمِيعاً بَصِيراً قَوِيّاً مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ الله وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَذَاكَ أَنِّي أَوْلَى بِحَسَنَاتِكَ مِنْكَ وَأَنْتَ أَوْلَى بِسَيِّئَاتِكَ مِنِّي
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: Allah said: son of Adam, by My will you are the one who wills for yourself what you will; by My strength you discharged My duties; by My favour you grew strong enough to disobey Me. Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever ill from yourself.

narrations.speaker: al-Sadiqayn
narrations.arabic: الحسنات في كتاب الله على وجهين والسيئات على وجهين … وقوله: { ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك } يعني ما عملت من ذنوب فعوقبت عليها في الدنيا والآخرة فمن نفسك بافعالك

text.en: The good things in Allah's Book are of two kinds, and the evil things of two kinds. As for 'whatever ill befalls you is from yourself', it means the sins you did and were punished for in this world and the next: they are from yourself, by your own deeds.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ذروة الأمر و سنامه و مفاتحه، و باب الأشياء، و رضا الرحمن، الطاعة للإمام بعد معرفته … أما لو أن رجلا قام ليله، و صام نهاره، و تصدق بجميع ماله، و حج جميع دهره، و لم يعرف ولي الله فيواليه، و تكون جميع أعماله بدلالته إليه، ما كان له على الله عز و جل حق في ثوابه، و لا كان من أهل الإيمان
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Abdullah ibn al-Salt, both from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The summit of the matter, its peak, its keys, the gate of things and the pleasure of the Merciful is obedience to the Imam after knowing him. Were a man to pray his night, fast his day, give all his wealth and perform hajj his whole life without knowing Allah's wali, he would have no claim to reward.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: و ذكر أن الكتاب يصدق بعضه بعضا، و أنه لا اختلاف فيه، فقال سبحانه: { وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلاَفاً كَثِيراً } … و إن القرآن ظاهره أنيق، و باطنه عميق، لا تفنى عجائبه، و لا تنقضي غرائبه، و لا تكشف الظلمات إلا به

text.en: He mentioned that the Book confirms one part of itself by another and that there is no discrepancy in it, saying, 'Had it been from other than Allah, they would have surely found much discrepancy in it.' The Quran's outward is elegant and its inward deep; its wonders never end, and darkness is dispelled only by it.

note.en: Al-Tusi reports the word of Abu Jafar that those vested with authority are the infallible Imams, and holds it stronger: referring a matter to one who is not infallible cannot yield knowledge [19].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل عير أقواما بالإذاعة في قوله عز و جل: { وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُواْ بِهِ } فإياكم و الإذاعة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who heard Abu Abdillah

text.en: Allah reproached certain people for broadcasting, in His words, 'When a report of safety or alarm comes to them, they immediately broadcast it.' So beware of broadcasting.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: في قوله: { وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰ أُوْلِي ٱلأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ } ، قال: " هم الأئمة "
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Jafar

text.en: About His words, 'but had they referred it to the Apostle or to those vested with authority among them', he said: they are the Imams.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: يعني آل محمد صلوات الله عليهم وهم الذين يستنبطون من القرآن ويعرفون الحلال والحرام وهم حجة الله على خلقه
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from al-Rida

text.en: He means the family of Muhammad. They are the ones who draw the matter out from the Quran and who know the lawful and the forbidden, and they are Allah's proof over His creation.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله كلف رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) ما لم يكلف به أحدا من خلقه، كلفه أن يخرج على الناس كلهم وحده بنفسه، و إن لم يجد فئة تقاتل معه، و لم يكلف هذا أحدا من خلقه قبله و لا بعده، ثم تلا هذه الآية: { فَقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُكَلَّفُ إِلاَّ نَفْسَكَ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Ali ibn Hadid, from Marazim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Allah charged the Messenger of Allah with what He charged none of His creation: He charged him to go out against all the people alone, by himself, even if he found no party to fight with him, and He charged this to no one before him or after him. Then he recited this verse.

note.en: Al-Tusi reports that the kifl of an evil intercession is the burden of its sin, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, and that this is also the word of Abu Jafar [21].
Al-Tabrisi reports from al-Suddi, Ata, Ibrahim and Ibn Jurayj that both the better greeting and the plain return are owed to a Muslim who greets you, and calls this the stronger view [11].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): السلام تطوع، و الرد فريضة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The greeting of peace is voluntary, and returning it is obligatory.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Hasan
narrations.arabic: جاءت جارية للحسن عليه السلام بطاق ريحان فقال عليه السلام أنت حرة لوجه الله فقيل له في ذلك فقال أدبنا الله تعالى فقال وإذا حييتم بتحية الآية

text.en: A slave-girl brought al-Hasan a spray of basil, and he said: you are free, for the sake of Allah. When he was asked about it he said: Allah taught us manners, for He said, 'When you are greeted with a salute, greet with a better one than it.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: إذا عطس أحدكم فسمتوه، قولوا: رحمكم الله، و هو يقول: يغفر الله لكم و يرحمكم، قال الله تبارك و تعالى: { وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ }
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: When one of you sneezes, bless him: say, may Allah have mercy on you, and he says, may Allah forgive you and have mercy on you. Allah said: 'When you are greeted with a salute, greet with a better one than it, or return it.'

perspectives.en: The readings part over 'those vested with authority'. Al-Tusi reports the word of Abu Jafar that they are the infallible Imams, and argues that referring a matter to one who is not infallible cannot produce knowledge, since error is possible for him, whether he be a commander of expeditions or a scholar [19]. Al-Qurtubi instead lists the people of knowledge and fiqh, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, the governors, from al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, and the commanders of expeditions [65]. Al-Razi reduces it to the same two options, men of knowledge and judgement or the commanders [76].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فأمرهم الله بالكفّ عن ذلك، وإقامة شعائر الدين من صلاة وزكاة ليشتد عظم الدين ويقوم صلبه فيأذن الله لهم في جهاد أعدائه

sources.gloss: So Allah commanded them to hold back from that and to establish the rites of the religion, prayer and zakat, so that the bone of the religion might grow strong and its spine stand, and then Allah would permit them to fight His enemies.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ولا دليل في الآية يدل على كون المحكي عنهم هم المنافقين، كما ذكره بعضهم، بل الأمر بالنظر إلى اتصال السياق على خلاف ذلك.

sources.gloss: There is no evidence in the verse that those reported of are the hypocrites, as some have said; rather, given the connection of the context, the matter is otherwise.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالشفيع ذو نصيب من الخير أو الشر المرتب على الشفاعة

sources.gloss: The intercessor has a share of the good or the evil that follows upon the intercession.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال الكلبي: نزلت في عبد الرحمن بن عوف الزهري، والمقداد بن الأسود الكندي، وقدامة بن مظعون الجمحي وسعد بن أبي وقاص

sources.gloss: Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Zuhri, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, Qudamah ibn Mazun al-Jumahi and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل: يعني بالبروج القصور عن مجاهد وقتادة وابن جريج. وقيل: قصور في السماء باعينها عن السدي والربيع.

sources.gloss: It is said that the towers mean palaces, from Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj; and it is said they are actual palaces in the sky, from al-Suddi and al-Rabi.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أمرَ الله نبيه بالإعراض عنهم. وأن لا يسميهم بأعيانهم إبقاء عليهم وستراً لأمورهم إلى أن يستقر أمر الإسلام

sources.gloss: Allah commanded His prophet to turn away from them and not to name them individually, sparing them and covering their affairs until the matter of Islam was settled.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فخرج رسول الله في سبعين راكباً حتى أتى موسم بدر فكفأهم الله بأس العدو ولم يوافهم أبو سفيان ولم يكن قتال يومئذٍ

sources.gloss: So the Messenger of Allah went out with seventy riders until he came to the season of Badr; Allah kept the enemy's might from them, Abu Sufyan did not meet them, and there was no fighting that day.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل: إن قولـه: { أو ردّوها } للمسلمين خاصة أيضاً عن السدي وعطاء وإبراهيم وابن جريج قالوا: إذا سلَّم عليك المسلم فردّ عليه بأحسن مما سلم عليك أو بمثل ما قال. وهذا أقوى

sources.gloss: It is said that 'or return it' is also for the Muslims in particular, from al-Suddi, Ata, Ibrahim and Ibn Jurayj, who said: when a Muslim greets you, return it better than his greeting or with its like. This is stronger.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الثاني - قال مجاهد: نزلت في اليهود. نهى الله هذه الأمة أن يصنعوا مثل صنيعهم.

sources.gloss: The second view: Mujahid said it was revealed about the Jews; Allah forbade this community to do as they did.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { من عندك } قيل في معناه قولان: أحدهما - قال ابن زيد: معناه بسوء تدبيرك. والثاني - قال الجبائي، والبلخي، والزجاج. أي بشؤمك الذي لحقنا

sources.gloss: As for His words 'from you', two views are given on its meaning. The first: Ibn Zayd said it means, by your bad management. The second: al-Jubbai, al-Balkhi and al-Zajjaj said it means, by the ill omen of you that has overtaken us.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الثاني - ان معناهما مختلف، فالاول عند أكثر أهل العلم ان المراد به النعمة، والمصيبة من الله تعالى. وفي الآية الثانية المراد به الطاعة، والمعصية.

sources.gloss: The second answer: their meanings differ. In the first, according to most people of knowledge, what is meant is blessing and affliction from Allah; in the second verse what is meant is obedience and disobedience.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على ان الرسول لا يأمر بالخطأ، لأن الله تعالى جعل طاعته طاعة نفسه.

sources.gloss: The verse indicates that the Messenger does not command error, because Allah made obedience to him obedience to Himself.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أحدها - على بطلان التقليد، وصحة الاستدلال في اصول الدين، لأنه حث ودعا إلى التدبر.

sources.gloss: The first: it shows the invalidity of blind imitation and the soundness of reasoning in the roots of religion, since it urges and calls to contemplation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والرد إلى من ليس بمعصوم، لا يوجب العلم لجواز الخطأ عليه بلا خلاف سواء كانوا امراء السرايا، أو العلماء.

sources.gloss: Referring a matter to one who is not infallible does not necessitate knowledge, since error is possible for him without dispute, whether they be commanders of expeditions or scholars.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والكفل: قال الحسن، وقتادة: هو الوزر، وهو قول أبي جعفر (ع).

sources.gloss: The kifl: al-Hasan and Qatadah said it is the burden of sin, and that is the word of Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لا أحد أصدق من الله في الخبر الذي يخبر به من حيث لا يجوز عليه الكذب في شيء من الاشياء، لأنه لا يكذب إلا محتاج يجتلب به نفعاً، أو يدفع به ضرراً

sources.gloss: No one is more truthful than Allah in the report He gives, since falsehood is impossible for Him in anything, because only one in need lies, to draw a benefit or repel a harm.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإنها نزلت بمكة قبل الهجرة فلما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله إلى المدينة وكتب عليهم القتال نسخ هذا

sources.gloss: It was revealed at Mecca before the migration; then when the Messenger of Allah migrated to Medina and fighting was prescribed for them, this was abrogated.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أن معنى القولين جميعاً عن الصادقين عليهم السلام أنهم قالوا الحسنات في كتاب الله على وجهين والسيئات على وجهين

sources.gloss: The meaning of both statements, from al-Sadiqayn, is that they said: the good things in Allah's Book are of two kinds and the evil things of two kinds.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) في قول الله عز و جل: { لَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَكُمْ } ، قال: " يعني كفوا ألسنتكم "

sources.gloss: From Abu Abdillah, about Allah's words 'those who were told, Keep your hands off': he said, it means restrain your tongues.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ذروة الأمر و سنامه و مفاتحه، و باب الأشياء، و رضا الرحمن، الطاعة للإمام بعد معرفته

sources.gloss: The summit of the matter, its peak, its keys, the gate of things and the pleasure of the Merciful is obedience to the Imam after knowing him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و إن القرآن ظاهره أنيق، و باطنه عميق، لا تفنى عجائبه، و لا تنقضي غرائبه، و لا تكشف الظلمات إلا به

sources.gloss: The Quran's outward is elegant and its inward deep; its wonders do not run out and its marvels do not end, and the darknesses are dispelled only by it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، في قوله: { وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰ أُوْلِي ٱلأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ } ، قال: " هم الأئمة "

sources.gloss: From Abu Jafar, about His words 'had they referred it to the Apostle and to those vested with authority among them': he said, they are the Imams.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله كلف رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) ما لم يكلف به أحدا من خلقه، كلفه أن يخرج على الناس كلهم وحده بنفسه

sources.gloss: Allah charged the Messenger of Allah with what He charged none of His creation: He charged him to go out against all the people alone, by himself.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): السلام تطوع، و الرد فريضة

sources.gloss: The Messenger of Allah said: the greeting of peace is voluntary and returning it is obligatory.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: والعياشي عن الرضا عليه السلام يعني آل محمد صلوات الله عليهم وهم الذين يستنبطون من القرآن ويعرفون الحلال والحرام وهم حجة الله على خلقه

sources.gloss: Al-Ayyashi, from al-Rida: He means the family of Muhammad; they are the ones who draw it out from the Quran and know the lawful and the forbidden, and they are Allah's proof over His creation.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المناقب جاءت جارية للحسن عليه السلام بطاق ريحان فقال عليه السلام أنت حرة لوجه الله

sources.gloss: In al-Manaqib: a slave-girl came to al-Hasan with a spray of basil, and he said, you are free for the sake of Allah.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: أو أُولو الأمر وهم أهل العلم والفقه عن الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما. السُّدِّي وابن زيد: الوُلاةُ. وقيل: أمراء السرايا.

sources.gloss: Or those in authority, who are the people of knowledge and fiqh, from al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd: the governors. And it is said: the commanders of the expeditions.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: المسألة الأولى: في { أُوْلِى ٱلأَمْرِ } قولان: أحدهما: إلى ذوي العلم والرأي منهم. والثاني: إلى أمراء السرايا

sources.gloss: First question: on 'those vested with authority' there are two views: the first, the men of knowledge and judgement among them; the second, the commanders of the expeditions.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: وَ اللَّهِ لَقَدْ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَ آتُوا الزَّكاةَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ طَاعَةُ الْإِمَامِ

sources.gloss: By Allah, this verse was revealed, 'Have you not regarded those who were told, Keep your hands off, and maintain the prayer and give the zakat': it is only obedience to the Imam.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ الله وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَذَاكَ أَنِّي أَوْلَى بِحَسَنَاتِكَ مِنْكَ وَأَنْتَ أَوْلَى بِسَيِّئَاتِكَ مِنِّي

sources.gloss: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah and whatever ill befalls you is from yourself, and that is because I have more right to your good deeds than you, and you have more right to your evil deeds than I.

essay.en: The rebuke falls on the believers, not on their enemies: why should you be two groups concerning the hypocrites? Tabatabai reads verses 85 to 91 as a single stretch bearing on war with one party of the polytheists, and finds that they came down about men who professed faith before the believers, then went home and shared their people's idolatry, so that doubt fell over fighting them and the Muslims divided, some for war and some pleading on their behalf [1]. Al-Tusi records five accounts of the occasion, from the men who stayed behind at Uhud to a party who left Medina for Mecca and carried the idolaters' goods to al-Yamama [6]. The ruling follows: no friendship until they migrate, and if they turn their backs they are to be treated as open enemies. Then the exceptions arrive, and they are wide. Whoever joins a people bound to you by treaty is covered by that treaty; whoever comes with a heart too constricted to fight either side is left alone. Al-Tibyan reports Abu Ubayda's reading of join as tracing descent, and records the objection that descent never shielded Quraysh from being fought [8]. A third party wants safety from both camps and keeps sliding back into idolatry; only their refusal to withdraw, to offer peace and to hold their hands makes them liable. Al-Tusi reports Abu Ali choosing that the verse is not abrogated, since nothing proves it [9]. The line is drawn at conduct, not at profession.

note.en: Arkasahum means He turned them back: Ibn Abbas glossed it as returning them to the ruling of the disbelievers, Qatada as destroying them, Abu Muslim as forsaking them [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت في قوم قدموا المدينة من مكة فأظهروا للمسلمين الإسلام، ثم رجعوا إلى مكة لأنهم استوخموا المدينة فأظهروا الشرك، ثم سافروا ببضائع المشركين إلى اليمامة فأراد المسلمون أن يغزوهم فاختلفوا

text.en: It was revealed about a people who came to Medina from Mecca and showed the Muslims Islam, then went back to Mecca because Medina did not suit them and showed polytheism, then travelled with the idolaters' goods to al-Yamama; the Muslims wanted to raid them and fell into disagreement.

note.en: Until they migrate means until they leave the abode of shirk seeking Allah's religion; then, Ibn Abbas said, they become like you, with your rights and your duties [3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وَ إِنَّ لِشَيَاطِينِ الْإِنْسِ حِيلَةً وَ مَكْراً وَ خَدَائِعَ وَ وَسْوَسَةً بَعْضِهِمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ … إِرَادَةَ أَنْ يَسْتَوِيَ أَعْدَاءُ اللَّهِ وَ أَهْلُ الْحَقِّ فِي الشَّكِّ وَ الْإِنْكَارِ وَ التَّكْذِيبِ فَيَكُونُونَ سَوَاءً كَمَا وَصَفَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ وَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ كَما كَفَرُوا فَتَكُونُونَ سَواءً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Hafs al-Muadhdhin, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The satans among mankind have trickery, guile, deceits and whispering to one another, aiming that the enemies of Allah and the people of truth become equal in doubt and denial, so they are alike, as Allah described in His Book: They are eager that you should disbelieve like they have disbelieved.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: المراد بقولـه تعالى: { قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق } هو هلال بن عويمر السلمي واثق عن قومه رسول الله فقال في موادعته على أن لا تحيف يا محمد من أتانا، ولا نحيف من أتاك

text.en: What is meant by a people between whom and you there is a treaty is Hilal ibn Uwaymir al-Sulami. He pledged for his people to the Messenger of Allah, saying in his truce: that you wrong no one who comes to us, O Muhammad, and we wrong no one who comes to you.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت في بني مدلج جاؤوا إلى رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا انا قد حصرت صدورنا أن نشهد انك رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فلسنا معك ولا مع قومنا عليك فواعدهم إلى أن يفرغ من العرب ثم يدعوهم فإن أجابوا والا قاتلهم

text.en: It was revealed about Banu Mudlij. They came to the Messenger of Allah and said: our breasts are constrained to testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, so we are neither with you nor with our people against you. He set them a term, then would summon them; if they answered, well, otherwise he would fight them.

note.en: A clear sanction is a manifest argument, or a plain excuse for fighting; the word sultan is used because one prevails by an argument as one prevails through a ruler [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت في عيينة بن حصين الفزاري أَجدبت بلادهم فجاء إلى رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ووادعه على أن يقيم ببطن نخل ولا يتعرض له وكان منافقاً ملعوناً وهو الذي سماه رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم الأحمق المطاع

text.en: It was revealed about Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari. Their land was struck by drought, so he came to the Messenger of Allah and made a truce with him that he would stay at Batn Nakhl and not be harassed. He was an accursed hypocrite, whom the Messenger of Allah named the fool who is obeyed.

perspectives.en: Qurtubi carries both readings of the occasion. He opens with Muslim's report from Zayd ibn Thabit that the Companions split into two parties over the men who turned back at Uhud, gives after it Ibn Abbas's account of Meccans who believed and left off migration, and calls the first the sounder in transmission and the choice of al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi [21]. Tabrisi carries both as well, but leads with the report of men who professed Islam at Medina, returned to Mecca and then carried the idolaters' goods to al-Yamama, from Mujahid and al-Hasan and narrated from Imam al-Baqir, and places the Uhud report from Zayd ibn Thabit after it [2].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: ويظهر من التدبر فيها أنها نزلت في قوم من المشركين أظهروا الإِيمان للمؤمنين ثم عادوا إلى مقرهم وشاركوا المشركين في شركهم فوقع الريب في قتالهم، واختلفت أنظار المسلمين في أمرهم، فمن قائل يرى قتالهم، وآخر يمنع منه

sources.gloss: Reflection on them shows that they came down about a group of the polytheists who displayed faith to the believers, then returned to their own quarters and shared the polytheists' idolatry, so doubt fell over fighting them and the Muslims' views on their case differed: one said fight them, another forbade it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في قوم قدموا المدينة من مكة فأظهروا للمسلمين الإسلام ثم رجعوا إلى مكة … ثم سافروا ببضائع المشركين إلى اليمامة … عن مجاهد والحسن وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع. وقيل: نزلت في الذين تخلفوا عن أحد … فنزلت الآية عن زيد بن ثابت … { والله أركسهم بما كسبوا } أي ردَّهم إلى حكم الكفار بما أظهروا من الكفر عن ابن عباس. وقيل: معناه أهلكهم بكفرهم عن قتادة. وقيل: خذلهم فأقاموا على كفرهم وتردّدوا فيه فأخبر عن خذلانه إياهم بأنه أركسهم عن أبي مسلم

sources.gloss: It came down about a people who came to Medina from Mecca and showed the Muslims Islam, then went back to Mecca ... then travelled with the idolaters' goods to al-Yamama ... from Mujahid and al-Hasan, and it is what is narrated from Abu Jafar. And it is said: it came down about those who stayed behind at Uhud ... so the verse came down, from Zayd ibn Thabit. And Allah has made them relapse because of their deeds: that is, He returned them to the ruling of the disbelievers because of the unbelief they displayed, from Ibn Abbas. It is also said: He destroyed them for their unbelief, from Qatada. And: He forsook them, so they persisted in their unbelief and wavered in it, from Abu Muslim.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { حتى يهاجروا } أي حتى يخرجوا من دار الشرك ويفارقوا أهلها المشركين بالله { في سبيل الله } أي في ابتغاء دينه وهو سبيله فيصيروا عند ذلك مثلكم، لهم ما لكم وعليهم ما عليكم

sources.gloss: Until they migrate: until they leave the abode of polytheism and part from its idolatrous people, in the way of Allah, meaning seeking His religion, which is His way; then they become like you, having what you have and owing what you owe.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: المراد بقولـه تعالى: { قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق } هو هلال بن عويمر السلمي واثق عن قومه رسول الله فقال في موادعته على أن لا تحيف يا محمد من أتانا، ولا نحيف من أتاك

sources.gloss: What is meant by His words a people between whom and you there is a treaty is Hilal ibn Uwaymir al-Sulami, who pledged on behalf of his people to the Messenger of Allah, saying in his truce: that you wrong no one who comes to us, O Muhammad, and we wrong no one who comes to you.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطاناً مبيناً } أي حجة ظاهرة. وقيل: عذراًَ بيّناً في القتال

sources.gloss: And it is such against whom We have given you a clear sanction: that is, a manifest argument; and it is said: a plain excuse for fighting.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفيمن نزلت هذه الآية قيل فيه خمسة أقوال

sources.gloss: As to whom this verse came down about, five accounts have been given.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد ضعف هذا الجواب، لأن تعيين الانتساب لو أوجب أن يكون حكم المنتسب حكم من انتسب إليه ممن بينهم وبينهم ميثاق، لوجب ألا يقاتل النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قريشاً، لما بينهم وبين المؤمنين من الانتساب

sources.gloss: This answer has been weakened, because if tracing descent required that the one who traces it should take the ruling of those he traces it to among people bound by a treaty, then the Prophet would have had to refrain from fighting Quraysh, given the descent between them and the believers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ثم قال قوم: الآية منسوخة وان من لم يحارب مع المؤمنين، وجب قتاله. واختار هو أنها غير منسوخة. قال: لأنه لا دليل على ذلك

sources.gloss: Then a group said: the verse is abrogated, and whoever does not fight alongside the believers must be fought. But he chose that it is not abrogated, saying: because there is no evidence for that.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزلت في قوم قدموا المدينة من مكة فأظهروا للمسلمين الإسلام، ثم رجعوا إلى مكة لأنهم استوخموا المدينة فأظهروا الشرك، ثم سافروا ببضائع المشركين إلى اليمامة فأراد المسلمون أن يغزوهم فاختلفوا

sources.gloss: It came down about a people who came to Medina from Mecca and showed the Muslims Islam, then went back to Mecca because Medina did not suit them and showed polytheism, then travelled with the idolaters' goods to al-Yamama, so the Muslims wanted to raid them and fell into disagreement.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: نزلت في بني مدلج جاؤوا إلى رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقالوا انا قد حصرت صدورنا أن نشهد انك رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم فلسنا معك ولا مع قومنا عليك فواعدهم إلى أن يفرغ من العرب ثم يدعوهم فإن أجابوا والا قاتلهم

sources.gloss: It came down about Banu Mudlij, who came to the Messenger of Allah and said: our breasts are constrained to testify that you are the Messenger of Allah, so we are neither with you nor with our people against you. So he set them a term until he should be done with the Arabs and then call them; if they answered, well, otherwise he would fight them.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: نزلت في عيينة بن حصين الفزاري أَجدبت بلادهم فجاء إلى رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ووادعه على أن يقيم ببطن نخل ولا يتعرض له وكان منافقاً ملعوناً وهو الذي سماه رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم الأحمق المطاع

sources.gloss: It came down about Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari. Their land was struck by drought, so he came to the Messenger of Allah and made a truce with him that he would stay at Batn Nakhl and not be harassed. He was an accursed hypocrite, and he is the one the Messenger of Allah named the fool who is obeyed.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: روى مسلم عن زيد بن ثابت: " أن النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج إلى أُحد فرجع ناس ممن كان معه، فكان أصحاب النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم فرقتين فقال بعضهم: نقتلهم. وقال بعضهم: لا فنزلت { فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ } … وقال ابن عباس: هم قوم بمكة آمنوا وتركوا الهجرة … والأوّل أصح نقلاً، وهو اختيار البخاريّ ومسلم والترمذي

sources.gloss: Muslim related from Zayd ibn Thabit: the Prophet went out to Uhud and some of those with him turned back, and the Prophet's companions became two parties over them, some saying we kill them and some saying no; so there came down: Why should you be two groups concerning the hypocrites ... And Ibn Abbas said: they are a people at Mecca who believed and left off the migration ... And the first is the sounder in transmission, and it is the choice of al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni
grades: رواه بثلاثة أسانيد أولها مجهول. و ثانيها ضعيف عند القوم بابن سنان و عندي معتبر ، و السند الثالث ضعيف

excerpt.text: إِرَادَةَ أَنْ يَسْتَوِيَ أَعْدَاءُ اللَّهِ وَ أَهْلُ الْحَقِّ فِي الشَّكِّ وَ الْإِنْكَارِ وَ التَّكْذِيبِ فَيَكُونُونَ سَوَاءً كَمَا وَصَفَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ وَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ كَما كَفَرُوا فَتَكُونُونَ سَواءً

sources.gloss: Their aim being that the enemies of Allah and the people of truth should become equal in doubt, denial and belying, so that they are alike, as Allah the High described in His Book in His words: They are eager that you should disbelieve like they have disbelieved, so that you all become alike.

essay.en:
A believer may not kill another believer, unless it is by mistake. Tabatabai reads the opening as a denial that faith leaves room in a believer to kill his like, and holds the exception connected, where Tusi reports that most commentators call it broken off [1][7]. Tabrisi gives the occasion, a report narrated from Abu Jafar: Ayyash ibn Abi Rabia killed a man without knowing he had accepted Islam [3]. Tabatabai sets out the three cases: manumission with blood money; manumission alone when the dead man's people are hostile disbelievers who do not inherit; and, where a treaty stands, the blood money named first out of regard for the covenant [1].

Killing on purpose follows: Tabrisi glosses it as intending the death while knowing the man's faith and the inviolability of his blood [4]. Tusi records that all agree the threat does not reach one who repents [8].

Verse 94 disciplines the fighter's hand: ascertain. Tabrisi records a Kufan reading, 'make sure', and that the peace offered is read as the Muslim greeting or as surrender [5]. The closing pair weighs those who sit back against those who wage jihad, excepting whoever blindness, lameness or illness keeps at home [2]. Tabrisi reports that it came down about men who stayed behind at Tabuk, God excusing the people of disability, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum [6]. Yet the sitter is not left empty-handed: to each Allah has promised the best reward. The fighters keep the surplus: ranks, forgiveness, mercy.

note.en: Al-Qummi reads the exception otherwise: illa here stands in place of 'not', so the sense is that a believer kills a believer neither deliberately nor by mistake [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: العمد: كل ما اعتمد شيئا فأصابه بحديدة أو بحجر أو بعصا أو بوكزة، فهذا كله عمد، و الخطأ: من اعتمد شيئا فأصاب غيره
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Deliberate killing is whenever a man intends something and strikes it with iron, a stone, a stick or a blow: all of that is deliberate. Mistake is when he intends one thing and hits another.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كل العتق يجوز فيه المولود إلا في كفارة القتل، فإن الله عز و جل يقول: { فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ } يعني بذلك مقرة قد بلغت الحنث
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ibn Abi Umayr, both from Mu'ammar ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Every manumission admits a newborn except in the expiation for killing, for Allah says: the freeing of a believing slave, meaning by that one who affirms faith and has reached the age of accountability.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في الفقيه عن الصادق عليه السلام في رجل مسلم في أرض الشرك فقتله المسلمون ثم علم به الإمام بعد فقال يعتق مكانه رقبة مؤمنة وذلك قول الله عز وجل فان كان من قوم عدو لكم الآية

text.en: About a Muslim man in the land of polytheism whom the Muslims killed, the Imam learning of it afterwards, he said: he frees a believing slave in his place, and that is Allah's word, If he belongs to a people that are hostile to you.

note.en: Tusi reports that Shia narrators direct this verse at one who kills a believer for his faith, and such a man can only be a disbeliever [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سئل عن المؤمن يقتل المؤمن متعمداً أله توبة فقال ان كان قتله لإِيمانه فلا توبة لو أن كان قتله لغضب أو لسبب شيء من أشياء الدنيا فإن توبته أن يقاد منه وان لم يكن علم به انطلق إلى أولياء المقتول فأقر عندهم بقتل صاحبهم فان عفوا عنه فلم يقتلوه أعطاهم الدية واعتق نسمة وصام شهرين متتابعين واطعم ستين مسكيناً توبة إلى الله عز وجل

text.en: He was asked whether one who kills a believer deliberately can repent. He said: if he killed him for his faith, there is none. If out of anger or a worldly cause, his repentance is submitting to retaliation; if unknown, he confesses to the heirs, and if pardoned pays blood money, frees a slave, fasts two months, feeds sixty poor.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وَأَنْزَلَ فِي بَيَانِ الْقَاتِلِ وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خالِداً فِيها وَغَضِبَ الله عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذاباً عَظِيماً وَلا يَلْعَنُ الله مُؤْمِناً … وَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ فِي الْمَشِيئَةِ وَقَدْ أَلْحَقَ بِهِ حِينَ جَزَاهُ جَهَنَّمَ الْغَضَبَ وَاللَّعْنَةَ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Mihran, from al-Husayn ibn Maymun, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Concerning the killer He revealed: Should anyone kill a believer intentionally, his requital shall be hell, to remain in it, Allah wrathful at him and cursing him. And Allah does not curse a believer … How could it rest on His will, when in requiting him with hell He joined wrath and the curse to it?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عن أبي السفاتج عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام … قال: جزاؤه جهنم إن جازاه
narrations.chain: from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu al-Safatij, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: On Allah's words, Should anyone kill a believer intentionally, his requital shall be hell: he said, his requital is hell if He requites him.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: فقال له رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم قتلت رجلاً شهد أن لا إله إلا الله واني رسول الله فقال يا رسول الله انما قالها تعوذاً من القتل فقال رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم أفلا شققت الغطاء عن قلبه لا ما قال بلسانه قبلت ولا ما كان في نفسه علمت

text.en: You killed a man who bore witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. He said: he only said it seeking refuge from being killed. He said: Did you split open his heart? You neither accepted what his tongue said nor knew what was within him.

note.en: Al-Qummi glosses 'those who suffer from some disability' as the chronically disabled, since no blame rests on the blind [13].

narrations.speaker: Zayd ibn Thabit
narrations.arabic: روى زيد بن ثابت أنه لم يكن في آية نفي المساواة بين المجاهدين والقاعدين استثناء غير أولي الضرر فجاء ابن أم مكتوم وكان أعمى وهو يبكي فقال يا رسول الله كيف بمن لا يستطيع الجهاد فغشيه الوحي ثانياً ثم سرى عنه … فقال اقرأ غير أولي الضرر فالحقتها

text.en: The verse denying equality between the fighters and those who sit back had no exception for the people of disability. Ibn Umm Maktum came, blind and weeping: Messenger of Allah, what of one unable to fight? Revelation came over him … then he said: recite, excepting those who suffer from some disability. So I appended it.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: لقد خلفتم في المدينة أقواماً ما سرتم مسيراً ولا قطعتم وادياً الا كانوا معكم وهم الذين صحت نياتهم ونصحت جيوبهم وهوت أفئدتهم إلى الجهاد وقد منعهم من المسير ضرراً أو غيره

text.en: You have left behind in Medina men: you did not travel any distance nor cross a valley but they were with you. They are those whose intentions were sound and whose hearts yearned for jihad, kept from setting out by disability or by something else.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ الله سَبَّقَ بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَمَا يُسَبَّقُ بَيْنَ الْخَيْلِ يَوْمَ الرِّهَانِ ثُمَّ فَضَّلَهُمْ عَلَى دَرَجَاتِهِمْ فِي السَّبْقِ إِلَيْهِ … وَقَالَ فَضَّلَ الله الْمُجاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقاعِدِينَ أَجْراً عَظِيماً دَرَجاتٍ مِنْهُ وَمَغْفِرَةً وَرَحْمَةً
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Abu Amr al-Zubayri, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Allah has set a race among the believers as a race is set among horses on the day of the wager, then gave them precedence by their degrees in racing to Him … And He said: Allah has graced those who wage jihad over those who sit back with a great reward: ranks from Him, forgiveness, and mercy.

perspectives.en: Verse 93's threat divides the readings. Tusi answers the Mutazila, who took the verse as proof that the grave sinner stays in the fire forever, by reporting that Shia narrators direct it at one who kills a believer for his faith, and such a man can only be a disbeliever; he adds that all agree it does not cover one who repents [8]. Razi rejects that limit: the wording is general, so its coming down about a disbeliever does not narrow it [32]. Suyuti reports Ibn Abbas holding this the last verse revealed on the matter, unabrogated [36].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والمراد بالنفي في قوله { وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمناً } ، نفي الاقتضاء

sources.gloss: What is meant by the negation in His words, A believer may not kill another believer, is the denial of any inclination to it.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الضرر هو النقصان في الوجود المانع من القيام بأمر الجهاد والقتال كالعمى، والعرج، والمرض

sources.gloss: Harm is a deficiency in one's being that prevents undertaking jihad and fighting, such as blindness, lameness and illness.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في عياش بن أبي ربيعة المخزومي أخي أبي جهل لأمه لأنه كان أسلم وقتل بعد إسلامه رجلاً مسلماً وهو لا يعلم إسلامه، والمقتول الحارث بن يزيد بن أنسة العامري عن مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي قال: قتله بالحُرّة بعد الهجرة وكان من أحدّ مَن رده عن الهجرة، وكان يعذّب عياشاً مع أبي جهل وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر

sources.gloss: It came down about Ayyash ibn Abi Rabia al-Makhzumi, brother of Abu Jahl by his mother, who had accepted Islam and after his Islam killed a Muslim man without knowing he was Muslim. The slain man was al-Harith ibn Yazid ibn Ansa al-Amiri, on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrima and al-Suddi, who said he killed him at al-Harra after the migration, and he had been one of those who turned him back from migrating and used to torture Ayyash along with Abu Jahl; and this is what is narrated from Abu Jafar.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي قاصداً إلى قتله عالماً بإيمانه وحرمة قتله وعصمة دمه

sources.gloss: That is, intending his killing, knowing his faith, the unlawfulness of killing him and the inviolability of his blood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم فتثبتوا هنا في الموضعين بالثاء والتاء وفي الحجرات وقرأ الباقون فتبيَّنوا بالتاء والنون في الجميع

sources.gloss: The people of Kufa other than Asim read fa-tathabbatu here in both places and in al-Hujurat; the rest read fa-tabayyanu throughout.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت الآية في كعب بن مالك من بني سلمة ومرارة بن ربيع من بني عمرو بن عوف وهلال بن أُمية من بني واقف تخلَّفوا عن رسول الله يوم تبوك وعذر الله أولي الضرر وهو عبد الله بن أُم مكتوم

sources.gloss: The verse came down about Ka'b ibn Malik of Banu Salima, Murara ibn Rabi of Banu Amr ibn Awf and Hilal ibn Umayya of Banu Waqif, who stayed back from the Messenger of Allah on the day of Tabuk; and Allah excused the people of disability, that is Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقوله: { إلا خطأ } استثناء منقطع - في قول أكثر المفسرين

sources.gloss: His words, unless it is by mistake, are a disconnected exception, according to most of the commentators.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد روى أصحابنا أن الآية متوجهة إلى من يقتل المؤمن لايمانه، وذلك لا يكون إلا كافراً

sources.gloss: Our companions have narrated that the verse is directed at one who kills a believer for his faith, and such a one can only be a disbeliever.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي: لا عمداً ولا خطأ وإلا في موضع لا وليست باستثناء

sources.gloss: That is, neither deliberately nor by mistake; illa here stands in the place of not, and is no exception.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني الزمن كما ليس على الأعمى حرج

sources.gloss: Meaning the chronically disabled, just as there is no blame on the blind.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: العمد: كل ما اعتمد شيئا فأصابه بحديدة أو بحجر أو بعصا أو بوكزة، فهذا كله عمد، و الخطأ: من اعتمد شيئا فأصاب غيره

sources.gloss: The deliberate is whenever a man intends something and strikes it with iron, a stone, a stick or a blow: all of this is deliberate. Mistake is when he intends one thing and hits another.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في الفقيه عن الصادق عليه السلام في رجل مسلم في أرض الشرك فقتله المسلمون ثم علم به الإمام بعد فقال يعتق مكانه رقبة مؤمنة

sources.gloss: In al-Faqih, from al-Sadiq, about a Muslim man in the land of polytheism whom the Muslims killed, the Imam learning of it afterwards: he said, he frees a believing slave in his place.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ان كان قتله لإِيمانه فلا توبة لو أن كان قتله لغضب أو لسبب شيء من أشياء الدنيا فإن توبته أن يقاد منه

sources.gloss: If he killed him for his faith, there is no repentance; but if he killed him out of anger or for some worldly cause, his repentance is that he submit to retaliation.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: لقد خلفتم في المدينة أقواماً ما سرتم مسيراً ولا قطعتم وادياً الا كانوا معكم

sources.gloss: You have left behind in Medina men: you did not travel any distance nor cross a valley but they were with you.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فاذا ثبت أن اللفظ الدال على الاستغراق حاصل، فنزوله في حق الكفار لا يقدح في ذلك العموم

sources.gloss: Once it is established that the wording carries generality, its coming down concerning disbelievers does not impair that generality.

sources.author: Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti

excerpt.text: نزلت هذه الآية { ومن يقتل مؤمناً متعمداً فجزاؤه جهنم } هي آخر ما نزل، وما نسخها شيء

sources.gloss: This verse came down, Should anyone kill a believer intentionally, his requital shall be hell; it is the last thing revealed, and nothing abrogated it.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: قال: جزاؤه جهنم إن جازاه

sources.gloss: He said: his requital is hell if He requites him.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: وَلا يَلْعَنُ الله مُؤْمِناً قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِنَّ الله لَعَنَ الْكافِرِينَ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ سَعِيراً

sources.gloss: And Allah does not curse a believer. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Indeed Allah has cursed the faithless and prepared for them a blaze.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: إِنَّ الله سَبَّقَ بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كَمَا يُسَبَّقُ بَيْنَ الْخَيْلِ يَوْمَ الرِّهَانِ ثُمَّ فَضَّلَهُمْ عَلَى دَرَجَاتِهِمْ فِي السَّبْقِ إِلَيْهِ

sources.gloss: Allah has set a race among the believers as a race is set among horses on the day of the wager, then gave them precedence according to their degrees in racing to Him.

essay.en: Four verses turn from the field to the deathbed. Al-Mizan reads the verses just before as a goad, rousing believers to strive rather than sit back [1]. Here the angels take souls 'while they are wronging themselves' and put one question: 'What state were you in?' Al-Tabrisi calls it a question of reproach, and reads the wrong as a soul cheated of its reward and burdened with punishment [2]. The plea, 'We were oppressed in the land,' is refused; God's earth was wide. Al-Tusi reports that the verses came down about men in Mecca who had professed Islam to the Prophet, were turned by their families once he had emigrated, went out with the polytheists at Badr and were killed there [4]; Majma transmits a like account of Badr from Abu Hamza al-Thumali [2]. Then the exception, and it is exact: men, women and children with no means and no road. Of them God says only 'Maybe'. The last verse opens the road again. Al-Tabrisi glosses 'muragham' as somewhere to move to and room in provision, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak, while Mujahid and Qatada read it as passage from misguidance to guidance [3]. Whoever dies on the way has already been paid: al-Tabrisi tells of Jundub ibn Damra, gravely ill in Mecca, who said he was not among those God had excepted, had his sons carry him out on a bed, and died at al-Tan'im [3]. The excuse of the able is refused; the door stays open for the powerless.

note.en: The angels take away means their seizing of souls; al-Tabrisi notes that what the angels or the angel of death do may equally be ascribed to Allah, since they act by His command [2].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: نزلت في من اعتزل أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) و لم يقاتل معه، فقالت الملائكة لهم عند الموت: { فِيمَ كُنتُمْ قَالُواْ كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ } أي لم نعلم مع من الحق … أي دين الله و كتاب الله واسع، فتنظروا فيه

text.en: It came down about those who withdrew from Amir al-Muminin and did not fight with him. At death the angels said to them, What state were you in? They said, We were oppressed in the land, meaning: we did not know where the truth lay. God's religion and book are vast, so you might have looked into them.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: ان الله تعالى أجل وأعظم من أن يتولى ذلك بنفسه وفعل رسله وملائكته فعله لأنهم بأمره يعملون … فمن كان من أهل الطاعة تولت قبض روحه ملائكة الرحمة ومن كان من أهل المعصية تولت قبض روحه ملائكة النقمة
narrations.chain: In al-Ihtijaj, from Amir al-Muminin, when he was asked about these verses

text.en: God is too exalted and too great to undertake that Himself; the act of His messengers and angels is His act, for they work by His command. Whoever is of the people of obedience, the angels of mercy take his soul; whoever is of the people of disobedience, the angels of wrath take his soul.

note.en: Qarai's oppressed renders mustad'afin. Al-Tusi limits the exception to those who cannot leave for poverty and want of means, or who do not know the road out of Mecca [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: هو الذي لا يستطيع الكفر فيكفر ولا يهتدي سبيل الايمان فيؤمن، والصبيان، ومن كان من الرجال والنساء على مثل عقول الصبيان مرفوع عنهم القلم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: He is the one who cannot disbelieve so as to disbelieve, and is not guided to the path of faith so as to believe; and children, and those men and women whose minds are like the minds of children: the pen is lifted from them.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا سليمان في هؤلاء المستضعفين من هو أثخن رقبة منك، المستضعفون قوم يصومون ويصلون تعف بطونهم وفروجهم لا يرون أن الحق في غيرنا، آخذين بأغصان الشجرة
narrations.chain: al-Mudaffar ibn Jafar al-Alawi, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: O Sulayman, among these oppressed ones are men of thicker neck than you. The oppressed are a people who fast and pray, whose bellies and private parts are chaste, who do not hold that the truth lies with any other than us, taking hold of the branches of the tree.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يَا زُرَارَةُ قَوْلُ الله أَصْدَقُ مِنْ قَوْلِكَ فَأَيْنَ الَّذِينَ قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ وَالنِّساءِ وَالْوِلْدانِ لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلاً أَيْنَ الْمُرْجَوْنَ لأمْرِ الله أَيْنَ الَّذِينَ خَلَطُوا عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً أَيْنَ أَصْحَابُ الأعْرَافِ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: O Zurara, God's word is truer than your word. Where then are those God called the oppressed among men, women and children, who have no means and no way? Where are those deferred to God's command? Where are those who mixed a good deed with a bad one? Where are the people of the Heights?

note.en: Al-Tusi reads it so: perhaps Allah will pardon them for the poverty they are in, and favour them by overlooking their leaving migration undone, since they did not leave it by choice [4].
Zurara sent his son Ubayd to Medina for news of Abu al-Hasan and Abdullah, and Zurara died before his son returned to him [9].

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Ibrahim
narrations.arabic: أي: يجد خيراً إذا جاهد مع الإمام … قال إذا خرج إلى الإمام ثم مات قبل أن يبلغه

text.en: That is, he finds good when he strives alongside the Imam. It means: when he goes out to the Imam and then dies before reaching him.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما تقول في رجل دعا إلى هذا الأمر فعرفه و هو في أرض منقطعة إذ جاءه موت الإمام، فبينا هو ينتظر إذ جاءه الموت؟ … هو و الله بمنزلة من هاجر إلى الله و رسوله فمات، فقد وقع أجره على الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Abu al-Sabbah

text.en: What of a man called to this affair who came to know it, in a remote land, when the Imam's death reached him, and while waiting death came to him? He said: By God, he ranks with one who migrated to God and His Apostle and died; his reward has fallen on God.

narrations.speaker: Abu al-Hasan the First
