narrations.arabic: إني لأرجو أن يكون زرارة ممن قال الله: { وَمَن يَخْرُجْ مِن بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِراً إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ ٱلْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلىَ ٱللَّهِ }
narrations.chain: Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu al-Hasan the First

text.en: I hope that Zurara is among those of whom God said: And whoever leaves his home migrating toward Allah and His Apostle, and is then overtaken by death, his reward shall certainly fall on Allah.

perspectives.en: The two traditions carry the verse in different directions. Ali ibn Ibrahim takes it past Mecca: he holds it came down about those who withdrew from Amir al-Muminin and would not fight with him, and reads migrate in it as meaning that God's religion and book are wide enough to look into [8]. Ibn Kathir's tafsir generalizes instead into a ruling: the verse is general for everyone who settles among polytheists while able to migrate and unable to keep his religion, so that he wrongs himself and does what is forbidden by consensus [14]. Qurtubi adds that the exchange shows they died as Muslims who had wronged themselves by leaving migration undone [15].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وبالجملة ففي الكلام تحضيض للمؤمنين وتهييج لهم، وإيقاظ لروح إيمانهم لاستباق الخير والفضيلة

sources.gloss: In sum, the discourse urges the believers on and stirs them, and awakens the spirit of their faith to race toward good and excellence.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال أبو حمزة الثمالي بلغنا أن المشركين يوم بدر لم يخلفوا إذ خرجوا أحداً إلاَّ صبياً أو شيخاً كبيراً أو مريضاً فخرج معهم ناس ممن تكلم بالإسلام … الملائكة ملك الموت أو هو وغيره فإنَّ الملائكة تتوفى وملك الموت يتوفى والله يتوفى وما يفعله ملك الموت أو الملائكة يجوز أن يضاف إلى الله إذ فعلوه بأمره … { ظالمي أنفسهم } أي في حال هم فيها ظالموا أنفسهم إذ بخسوها حقَّها من الثواب وأدخلوا عليها العقاب بفعل الكفر { قالوا فيم كنتم } أي قالت لهم الملائكة فيم كنتم أي في أيّ شيء كنتم من دينكم على وجه التقرير لهم أو التوبيخ لفعلهم

sources.gloss: Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: it has reached us that on the day of Badr the polytheists left none behind when they went out except a boy, an old man or a sick man, and some who had professed Islam went out with them ... The angels: the angel of death, or he and others, for the angels take souls, the angel of death takes them and God takes them, and what the angel of death or the angels do may be ascribed to God, since they did it by His command ... Wronging themselves: in a state in which they wrong themselves, since they cheated them of their due of reward and brought punishment upon them by the act of unbelief. They ask, What state were you in: that is, the angels said to them, what were you in of your religion, by way of putting them to it or reproaching them for what they did.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل: لما نزلت آيات الهجرة سمعها رجل من المسلمين وهو جندع أو جندب بن ضمرة وكان بمكة فقال: والله ما أنا مما استثنى الله إني لأجد قوة وإني لعالم بالطريق وكان مريضاً شديد المرض … فخرجوا يحملونه على سرير حتى إذا بلغ التنعيم مات فنزلت الآية عن أبي حمزة الثمالي … { يجد في الأرض مراغماً كثيراً وسعة } أي متحولاً من الأرض وسعة في الرزق عن ابن عباس والضحاك والربيع. وقيل مزحزحاً عما يكره وسعة من الضلالة إلى الهدى عن مجاهد وقتادة

sources.gloss: It is said: when the verses of migration came down, a Muslim man in Mecca, Jundu or Jundub ibn Damra, heard them and said: by God, I am not of those God excepted; I find strength in myself and I know the road. He was gravely ill ... so they went out carrying him on a bed, and when he reached al-Tan'im he died, and the verse came down: from Abu Hamza al-Thumali ... He will find many havens and plenitude in the earth: that is, a place to move to in the earth and room in provision, from Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Rabi. And it is said: a removal from what he dislikes and room, from misguidance to guidance, from Mujahid and Qatada.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: هذه الآية نزلت في قوم أظهروا للنبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) الاسلام بمكة، فلما هاجر النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وهاجر أصحابه فتنوهم آباؤهم عن دينهم فافتتنوا وخرجوا مع المشركين يوم بدر فقتلوا كلهم … وهم الذين يعجزون عن الهجرة لاعسارهم وقلة حيلتهم { ولا يهتدون سبيلاً } يعني في الخلاص من مكة. وقيل معناه لا يهتدون لسوء معرفتهم بالطريق من أرضهم إلى أرض الاسلام … يعني لعل الله أن يعفو عنهم لما هم عليه من الفقر ويتفضل عليهم بالصفح عنهم في تركهم الهجرة من حيث لم يتركوها اختياراً

sources.gloss: This verse came down about a people who displayed Islam to the Prophet at Mecca; then, when the Prophet and his companions emigrated, their fathers tried them over their religion and they were turned, and they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr and were all killed ... They are those unable to migrate for their poverty and want of means. Nor are guided to any way: that is, in getting free of Mecca; and it is said its meaning is that they are not guided because of their poor knowledge of the road from their land to the land of Islam ... Maybe Allah will excuse them: that is, perhaps God will pardon them for the poverty they are in and grant them the favour of overlooking their leaving migration undone, since they did not leave it by choice.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: أي: يجد خيراً إذا جاهد مع الإمام … قال إذا خرج إلى الإمام ثم مات قبل أن يبلغه

sources.gloss: That is, he finds good when he strives alongside the Imam ... He said: when he goes out to the Imam and then dies before reaching him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نزلت في من اعتزل أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) و لم يقاتل معه … أي دين الله و كتاب الله واسع، فتنظروا فيه

sources.gloss: It came down about the one who withdrew from Amir al-Muminin and did not fight with him ... that is, God's religion and God's book are vast, so you might have looked into them.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو و الله بمنزلة من هاجر إلى الله و رسوله فمات، فقد وقع أجره على الله … وجه زرارة ابنه عبيدا إلى المدينة يستخبر له خبر أبي الحسن و عبد الله، فمات قبل أن يرجع إليه عبيد ابنه

sources.gloss: By God, he is in the rank of one who migrated to God and His Messenger and died: his reward has fallen on God ... Zurara sent his son Ubayd to Medina to seek him news of Abu al-Hasan and Abdullah, and he died before his son Ubayd returned to him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ان الله تعالى أجل وأعظم من أن يتولى ذلك بنفسه وفعل رسله وملائكته فعله لأنهم بأمره يعملون … فمن كان من أهل الطاعة تولت قبض روحه ملائكة الرحمة ومن كان من أهل المعصية تولت قبض روحه ملائكة النقمة

sources.gloss: God is too exalted and too great to undertake that Himself, and the act of His messengers and angels is His act, for they work by His command ... So whoever is of the people of obedience, the angels of mercy take his soul, and whoever is of the people of disobedience, the angels of wrath take his soul.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: يا سليمان في هؤلاء المستضعفين من هو أثخن رقبة منك، المستضعفون قوم يصومون ويصلون تعف بطونهم وفروجهم لا يرون أن الحق في غيرنا، آخذين بأغصان الشجرة

sources.gloss: O Sulayman, among these oppressed ones there is one with a thicker neck than you. The oppressed are a people who fast and pray, whose bellies and private parts are chaste, who do not hold that the truth is with any other than us, taking hold of the branches of the tree.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: هو الذي لا يستطيع الكفر فيكفر ولا يهتدي سبيل الايمان فيؤمن، والصبيان، ومن كان من الرجال والنساء على مثل عقول الصبيان مرفوع عنهم القلم

sources.gloss: He is the one who cannot disbelieve so as to disbelieve, nor is guided to the path of faith so as to believe; and children, and those men and women whose intellects are like those of children: the pen is lifted from them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: يَا زُرَارَةُ قَوْلُ الله أَصْدَقُ مِنْ قَوْلِكَ فَأَيْنَ الَّذِينَ قَالَ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِلا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجالِ وَالنِّساءِ وَالْوِلْدانِ لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلاً أَيْنَ الْمُرْجَوْنَ لأمْرِ الله

sources.gloss: O Zurara, the word of God is truer than your word. Where then are those of whom God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: except the oppressed among men, women and children, who have neither access to any means nor are guided to any way? Where are those deferred to God's command?

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: عامة في كل من أقام بين ظهراني المشركين، وهو قادر على الهجرة، وليس متمكناً من إقامة الدين، فهو ظالم لنفسه، مرتكب حراماً بالإجماع

sources.gloss: General for everyone who settles among the polytheists while able to migrate and not able to establish the religion: he is one who wrongs himself and commits something forbidden by consensus.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: ويفيد هذا السؤال والجواب أنهم ماتوا مسلمين ظالمين لأنفسهم في تركهم الهجرة، وإلاَّ فلو ماتوا كافرين لم يقل لهم شيء من هذا

sources.gloss: This question and answer show that they died as Muslims who wronged themselves in leaving migration undone; otherwise, had they died as unbelievers, none of this would have been said to them.

essay.en: These verses legislate two things at once: the shortening of the prayer on the road, and the shape of a congregation with an enemy in front of it. Tabatabai reads them as one movement, from the fear prayer and the shortening in travel to a closing call to keep after the polytheists, bound to the jihad verses before them [1]. The first verse lifts the blame: no sin in shortening when you journey and fear trouble from the faithless. Tusi glosses it as a cut in number, four-unit prayers prayed as two [6]. Tabrisi records this as the view of most jurists and the madhhab of Ahl al-Bayt, beside a second reading in which what is cut is the prayer's bounds, narrated, he says, for prayer under severe fear [2]. The wording makes fear the condition, but Tusi holds that nobody today reads it so: travel alone is the cause [6]. Then the choreography: one party prays armed while the other faces the enemy, and they change places. Tabrisi holds that the ones ordered to carry weapons are the ones praying [3]. When the prayer ends the remembrance goes on, standing, sitting, lying down; once the fear lifts, Tusi says, the prayer returns to its full bounds [8], and 'a timed prescription' is read both as an obligation, narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq, and as a duty fixed to its hours [4]. The last verse sends the wounded back out after Uhud [5]: both sides bleed, but only one hopes, for victory now and reward later [9].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل يقول: { وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُواْ مِنَ ٱلصَّلَٰوةِ } فصار التقصير في السفر واجبا كوجوب التمام في الحضر
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, by his isnad from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Allah says: 'When you journey in the land, there is no sin upon you in shortening the prayers.' So shortening in travel became obligatory, just as completing it is obligatory at home.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُواْ مِنَ ٱلصَّلَٰوةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَن يَفْتِنَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ } … في الركعتين تنقص منهما واحدة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: About 'there is no sin upon you in shortening the prayers, if you fear that the faithless may trouble you': it is in the two rak'ahs, one is reduced from them.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ستة لا يقصرون الصلاة، الجباة الذين يدورون في جبايتهم، والتاجر الذي يدور في تجارته من سوق إلى سوق والأمير الذي يدور في إمارته والراعي الذي يطلب مواقع القطر ومنبت الشجر والرجل يخرج في طلب الصيد يريد لهواً للدنيا والمحارب الذي يقطع الطريق
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: Six do not shorten the prayer: tax collectors who go about collecting, the merchant who goes from market to market, the commander who goes about his command, the shepherd seeking rainfall and pasture, the man who goes out hunting for worldly amusement, and the brigand who cuts the road.

note.en: Al-Qummi reports the verse came down on the road to Hudaybiyya, when Khalid ibn al-Walid lay in ambush with two hundred horsemen, waiting for the Muslims to be at prayer [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: صلى النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) بأصحابه في غزاة ذات الرقاع ففرق أصحابه فرقتين، فأقام فرقة بإزاء العدو و فرقة خلفه، فكبر و كبروا، فقرأ و أنصتوا، فركع و ركعوا، فسجد و سجدوا … ثم استمر رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) قائما فصلوا لأنفسهم ركعة، ثم سلم بعضهم على بعض، ثم خرجوا إلى أصحابهم فقاموا بإزاء العدو
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, by his isnad from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Sadiq

text.en: The Prophet prayed with his companions at the raid of Dhat al-Riqa. He set one group facing the enemy and one behind him; he bowed and they bowed, he prostrated and they prostrated, then he stayed standing while they completed a rak'ah alone, gave salam, and changed places with the others.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: من صلى المغرب في خوف بالقوم، صلى بالطائفة الاولى ركعة، و بالطائفة الثانية ركعتين

text.en: Whoever leads people in the maghrib prayer in a state of fear prays one rak'ah with the first group and two with the second.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يعني مفروضاً وليس يعني وقت فوتها إذ جاز ذلك الوقت ثم صلاها لم تكن صلاته هذه مؤداة ولو كان كذلك لهلك سليمان بن داود حين صلاها لغير وقتها ولكن متى ما ذكرها صلاها
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi and al-Ayyashi, from al-Baqir

text.en: It means obligatory. It does not mean an hour after which, once passed, a prayer then prayed would not count as performed; were that so, Sulayman ibn Dawud would have perished when he prayed outside its time. Whenever he remembers it, he prays it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: موقوتاً أي ثابتاً وليس ان عجلت قليلاً وأخرت قليلاً بالذي يضرك ما لم تضع تلك الإِضاعة فان الله عز وجل يقول لقوم أضاعوا الصلاة واتبعوا الشهوات فسوف يلقون غياً
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi, from al-Sadiq

text.en: 'Timed' means fixed. That you hasten a little or delay a little does not harm you, so long as you do not let it go to waste, for Allah says of a people: they neglected the prayer and followed lusts, so they will meet error.

note.en: Al-Qummi reads this command as joined to Al Imran 140, on the wound that touched the believers and touched the enemy alike [13].

narrations.speaker: Jibril
narrations.arabic: يا محمد ان الله يأمرك أن تخرج في أثر القوم ولا يخرج معك إلا من به جراحة

text.en: O Muhammad, Allah commands you to go out in pursuit of these people, and let no one go out with you except a man who carries a wound.

perspectives.en: Both traditions carry the shortening beyond the state of fear, but they weigh it differently. Tabrisi records al-Shafi'i holding it a dispensation and Abu Hanifa an obligation, and says the obligation is the madhhab of Ahl al-Bayt [2]; al-Baqir, asked how the traveller prays, answers that shortening on a journey binds exactly as completing binds at home [14]. Qurtubi reports that the well-known view of Malik, most of his companions and most scholars early and late is that shortening is a sunna, al-Shafi'i's view too, and that the Baghdadi Malikis made the traveller free to choose [26].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: الآيات تشرع صلاة الخوف والقصر في السفر، وتنتهي إلى ترغيب المؤمنين في تعقيب المشركين وابتغائهم، وهي مرتبطة بالآيات السابقة المتعرضة للجهاد وما لها من مختلف الشؤون

sources.gloss: These verses legislate the fear prayer and the shortening in travel, and end by urging the believers to pursue the polytheists; they are bound to the preceding verses on jihad.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: واختلف الفقهاء في قصر الصلاة في السفر فقال الشافعي: هي رخصة واختاره الجبائي. وقال أبو حنيفة: هو عزيمة وفرض وهذا مذهب أهل البيت

sources.gloss: The jurists differ over shortening the prayer in travel: al-Shafi'i said it is a dispensation, which al-Jubbai chose, and Abu Hanifa said it is binding and obligatory, and this is the madhhab of Ahl al-Bayt.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فقيل المأمور بأخذ السلاح الطائفة المصلية مع رسول الله يأخذون من السلاح مثل السيف يتقلدون به والخنجر يشدّونه إلى دروعهم وكذلك السكين ونحو ذلك وهو الصحيح

sources.gloss: It is said that the ones commanded to take up weapons are the group praying with the Messenger of Allah, weapons such as a sword worn at the side, a dagger fastened to the mail, a knife and the like, and this is the correct view.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: معناه إن الصَّلاة كانت على المؤمنين واجبة مفروضة عن ابن عباس وعطيَّة العوفي والسدي ومجاهد وهو المروي عن الباقر والصَّادق ع

sources.gloss: It means that the prayer was an obligation laid upon the believers, from Ibn Abbas, Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Suddi and Mujahid, and this is what is narrated from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قيل نزلت في الذهاب إلى بدر الصغرى لموعد أبي سفيان يوم أُحد وقيل: نزلت يوم أُحد في الذهاب خلف أبي سفيان وعسكره إلى حمراء الأسد عن عكرمة

sources.gloss: It is said the verse came down about the march to Badr al-Sughra for Abu Sufyan's appointment on the day of Uhud, and it is said it came down on the day of Uhud about going out after Abu Sufyan and his army to Hamra al-Asad, from Ikrima.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ولا خلاف اليوم أن الخوف ليس بشرط، لأن السفر المخصوص بانفراده سبب للتقصير

sources.gloss: There is no disagreement today that fear is not a condition, since travel by itself is the cause of the shortening.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وأقوى التأويلين قول من قال: إذا زال خوفكم من عدوكم، وأمنتم فأتموا الصلاة بحدودها غير قاصرين لها عن شيء من حدودها

sources.gloss: The stronger of the two readings is that of those who said: when your fear of your enemy has gone and you are safe, complete the prayer with its bounds, cutting nothing from them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وترجون } أنتم أيها المؤمنون { من الله } الظفر عاجلا والثواب آجلا

sources.gloss: 'And you expect', you the believers, 'from Allah' victory now and reward later.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ستة لا يقصرون الصلاة، الجباة الذين يدورون في جبايتهم، والتاجر الذي يدور في تجارته من سوق إلى سوق والأمير الذي يدور في إمارته والراعي الذي يطلب مواقع القطر ومنبت الشجر والرجل يخرج في طلب الصيد يريد لهواً للدنيا والمحارب الذي يقطع الطريق

sources.gloss: Six do not shorten the prayer: the tax collectors who go about their collecting, the merchant who moves from market to market, the commander who goes about his command, the shepherd who seeks rainfall and pasture, the man who goes out hunting for worldly amusement, and the brigand who cuts the road.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإنها نزلت لما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله إلى الحديبية يريد مكة فلما وقع الخبر إلى قريش بعثوا خالد بن الوليد في مائتي فارس كميناً

sources.gloss: It came down when the Messenger of Allah went out to Hudaybiyya making for Mecca, and when the news reached Quraysh they sent Khalid ibn al-Walid with two hundred horsemen as an ambush.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإنه معطوف على قوله في سورة آل عمران: { إن يمسكم قرح فقد مس القوم قرح مثله }

sources.gloss: It is joined to His words in Surah Al Imran: 'If a wound touches you, a like wound has already touched those people.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فصار التقصير في السفر واجبا كوجوب التمام في الحضر

sources.gloss: So shortening in travel became obligatory, just as completing the prayer is obligatory at home.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: صلى النبي (صلى الله عليه و آله) بأصحابه في غزاة ذات الرقاع ففرق أصحابه فرقتين، فأقام فرقة بإزاء العدو و فرقة خلفه

sources.gloss: The Prophet prayed with his companions at the raid of Dhat al-Riqa; he divided them into two groups, setting one facing the enemy and one behind him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: يعني مفروضاً وليس يعني وقت فوتها إذ جاز ذلك الوقت ثم صلاها لم تكن صلاته هذه مؤداة ولو كان كذلك لهلك سليمان بن داود حين صلاها لغير وقتها ولكن متى ما ذكرها صلاها

sources.gloss: It means obligatory, and it does not mean the hour of its lapse, such that if that hour passed and he then prayed it his prayer would not count as performed; were it so, Sulayman ibn Dawud would have perished when he prayed outside its time; rather, whenever he remembers it he prays it.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: ومشهور مذهبه وجُل أصحابه وأكثر العلماء من السلف والخلف أن القصر سنَّة، وهو قول الشافعيّ

sources.gloss: The well-known position of Malik, most of his companions and most scholars early and late is that shortening is a sunna, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i.

title.en: Do not plead for the traitors

essay.en:
The passage opens on the Book itself: "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you." Tabatabai reads these verses as one stretch of speech about justice in judgment, forbidding the judge to lean toward the party in the wrong and to wrong the party in the right, whoever they are [1].

The occasion the commentators give is small and human. Banu Ubayriq were three brothers, and Bashir, called Abu Tumah, broke into the upper room of Rifaah ibn Zayd and took food, a sword and a coat of mail; Rifaah complained to his nephew Qatadah ibn al-Numan, who carried it to the Prophet [2]. The family pointed instead at Labid ibn Sahl, a believing man, who took his sword and went out at them until they calmed him [12]. Then they sent an eloquent clansman, Usayr ibn Urwah, who told the Prophet that Qatadah had accused a house of standing and lineage; the Prophet rebuked Qatadah until he wished he had never spoken [5]. The verses came down.

"And plead to Allah for forgiveness." Al-Tusi holds that no disobedience occurred: the Prophet is above ugly deeds, the words discipline him not to argue for a party before the truth of it is clear, and his community is what is meant [5]. From the verses, Tabatabai adds, come the binding force of the Prophet's judgment and his infallibility [1].

The address then widens. Men who betray others betray themselves, since the harm of the betrayal returns upon them [3]. They screen themselves from people and not from God, while by night they settle on saying that the Jew stole the coat of mail and on swearing to it [7]. Verse 109 turns to those who walked to the Prophet for Banu Ubayriq [8]: you argued for them here; who will argue with God for them on the Day of Resurrection?

The close is an opening, not a curse. Whoever does evil and then asks forgiveness finds God forgiving; no one is seized for another's crime [10]; and whoever loads his own sin onto an innocent man carries a calumny. Bashir carried it, then disbelieved and fled to Mecca [13].

note.en: Al-Tusi: the prohibition is on taking the side of anyone who has betrayed a Muslim or a covenanted man in his person or property, and pushing away the one who claims his right [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: لا وَالله مَا فَوَّضَ الله إِلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ إِلا إِلَى رَسُولِ الله (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) وَإِلَى الائِمَّةِ قَالَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِما أَراكَ الله وَهِيَ جَارِيَةٌ فِي الاوْصِيَاءِ (عَلَيْهم السَّلام )
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from the Nawadir of Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: No, by Allah, Allah did not entrust the Book to any of His creation except to the Messenger of Allah and to the Imams. Allah said: "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you." It runs on in the successors.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إنه قال لأبي حنيفة وتزعم أنك صاحب راي وكان الرأي من رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم صواباً ومن دونه خطأ لأن الله قال فاحكم بينهم بما أراك الله ولم يقل ذلك لغيره

text.en: You claim to be a man of opinion. Opinion from the Messenger of Allah was correct, and from anyone below him it is error, because Allah said, "judge between them by what Allah has shown you," and He did not say that to anyone else.

note.en: Tabyit is a matter settled at night. Al-Zajjaj: what they settled was to say the Jew stole the coat of mail and to swear to it, expecting their oath accepted over his [7].

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin
narrations.arabic: وقد بين الله قصص المغيرين بقوله إذ يبيتون مالا يرضى من القول بعد فقد الرسول ما يقيمون به أود باطلهم حسب ما فعلته اليهود والنصارى بعد فقد موسى وعيسى من تغيير التوراة والإِنجيل وتحريف الكلم عن مواضعه

text.en: Allah has made plain the account of those who altered it in His words "when they conspire overnight with a discourse that He does not approve of" after the Messenger was gone, propping up their falsehood, as the Jews and Christians did after Moses and Jesus, changing the Torah and the Gospel and displacing words.

narrations.speaker: Harthama ibn Ayan
narrations.arabic: فَأَخَذَ عَلَيَّ الْعَهْدَ وَالْمِيثَاقَ وَأَكَّدَهُ عَلَيَّ قَالَ فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ عَنْهُ صَفَقَ بِيَدِهِ وَقَالَ يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَلا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ ما لا يَرْضى‏ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَكانَ اللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطاً
narrations.chain: Tamim ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Tatari, from Harthama ibn Ayan

text.en: Al-Mamun bound me by oath and covenant to keep this hidden. As I turned away from him he struck his hands together and recited: "They try to hide from people, but they do not try to hide from Allah, though He is with them when they conspire overnight."

note.en: Commentators differed whether this means the traitors or those who argued for them; al-Tusi prefers the general sense, covering everyone who does evil or wrongs himself [9].
Al-Tusi finds here the proof that no one is seized for another's crime and that children are not punished for the sins of their fathers, as in "no bearer shall bear another's burden" [10].
Al-Tusi reports disagreement over the innocent man: some name Labid ibn Sahl, a Muslim, others a Jew called Zayd ibn al-Samin, all agreeing the accuser was Ibn Ubayriq [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن أناساً من رهط بشير الادنين قالوا انطلقوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وقالوا نكلمه في صاحبنا ونعذره وإن صاحبنا بريء … فأقبلت رهط بشير فقال يا بشير استغفر الله وتب الله من الذنب فقال والذي أحلف به ما سرقها إلا لبيد
narrations.chain: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: Some of Bashir's nearest clansmen said: let us go to the Messenger of Allah and speak for our man and excuse him, for our man is innocent. They came to Bashir and said: seek Allah's forgiveness and repent of the sin. He said: by the One I swear by, none stole it but Labid.

perspectives.en: The command "plead to Allah for forgiveness" divides the readings. Al-Tusi holds that no disobedience occurred: the Prophet defended only what appeared, he is above ugly deeds, and the words are discipline whose real audience is his community [5]. Al-Tabari reads them as asking God to overlook the sin of disputing on behalf of the traitor, noting the report that the Prophet had only intended to do so [17]. Al-Qurtubi observes that this belongs to those who allow small sins to prophets, and quotes Ibn Atiyyah that it was no sin, since he defended what appeared while believing them innocent [27].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أنها ذات سياق واحد تتعرض للتوصية بالعدل في القضاء، والنهي عن أن يميل القاضي في قضائه، والحاكم في حكمه إلى المبطلين، ويجور على المحقين كائنين من كانوا

sources.gloss: They are of one context, urging justice in judging, and forbidding the judge in his verdict and the ruler in his ruling to lean toward the people of falsehood and wrong the people of truth, whoever they are.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: نزلت في بني أبيرق وكانوا ثلاثة إخوة بشر وبشير ومبشر وكان بشير يكنى أبا طعمة … فنقب أبو طعمة على عِليّة رفاعة بن زيد وأخذ له طعاماً وسيفاً ودرعاً فشكا ذلك إلى ابن أخيه قتادة بن النعمان

sources.gloss: It came down about Banu Ubayriq, three brothers, Bishr, Bashir and Mubashshir; Bashir was called Abu Tumah. Abu Tumah broke into the upper room of Rifaah ibn Zayd and took his food, a sword and a coat of mail, and he complained of it to his nephew Qatadah ibn al-Numan.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وإنما قال: يختانون أنفسهم وإن خانوا غيرهم لأَن ضرر خيانتهم كأنه راجع إليهم لاحق بهم

sources.gloss: He said only "they betray themselves", though they betrayed others, because the harm of their betrayal returns upon them and clings to them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: نهاه أن يكون لمن خان مسلماً أو معاهداً في نفسه أو ماله خصيماً … فلم يكن ذلك معصية، لأنه (ع) منزه عن القبائح فانما ذكر ذلك على وجه التأديب له في أن لا يبادر فيخاصم ويدفع عن خصم إلا بعد أن يبين الحق منه. والمراد بذلك امته

sources.gloss: He forbade him to be an adversary for one who betrayed a Muslim or a covenanted man in his person or his property ... That was no disobedience, for he is kept pure of ugly deeds; it was said only as discipline for him, that he not rush to dispute and defend a party before the truth of it is clear. His community is what is meant by it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الزجاج: الذي بيتوه قولهم إن اليهودي سارق الدرع وعزمهم على أن يحلفوا انهم ما سرقوا وان يمينهم تقبل دون يمين اليهودي

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj said: what they settled by night was their claim that the Jew was the one who stole the coat of mail, and their resolve to swear that they had not stolen it, and that their oath would be accepted rather than the Jew's.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والمعنى يا معاشر من جادل عن بني أبيرق في الحياة الدنيا

sources.gloss: The meaning is: O company of those who argued on behalf of Banu Ubayriq in the life of this world.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والاولى حمل الآية على عمومها في كل من عمل سوءاً أو ظلم نفسه، وان كان سبب نزولها فيمن تقدم ذكره من الخائنين أو المجادلين

sources.gloss: The better course is to carry the verse on its general sense, for everyone who does evil or wrongs himself, even if its occasion of revelation was about those already mentioned, the traitors or those who argued for them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وفي الآية دلالة على أنه لا يؤخذ أحد بجرم غيره، ولا يعاقب الاولاد بذنوب الآباء

sources.gloss: In the verse is proof that no one is seized for the crime of another, and that children are not punished for the sins of the fathers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: واختلفوا فيمن عنى به بقوله: { بريئاً } بعد إجماعهم على أن الرامي ابن أبيرق، فقال قوم: البريء رجل مسلم يقال له: لبيد بن سهل. وقال آخرون: بل هو رجل يهودي يقال له زيد بن السمين

sources.gloss: They differed over who is meant by His word "an innocent person", after agreeing that the accuser was Ibn Ubayriq. Some said the innocent one was a Muslim called Labid ibn Sahl; others said he was a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samin.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: وكان معهم في الرأي رجل مؤمن يقال له لبيد بن سهل فقال بنو ابيزق لقتادة هذا عمل لبيد بن سهل، فبلغ ذلك لبيدا فأخذ سيفه وخرج عليهم

sources.gloss: With them in the quarter was a believing man called Labid ibn Sahl. Banu Ubayriq said to Qatadah: this is the work of Labid ibn Sahl. Word of it reached Labid, so he took his sword and went out at them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ثم أن بشيراً كفر ولحق بمكة

sources.gloss: Then Bashir disbelieved and made his way to Mecca.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: إنه قال لأبي حنيفة وتزعم أنك صاحب راي وكان الرأي من رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم صواباً ومن دونه خطأ

sources.gloss: He said to Abu Hanifah: you claim to be a man of opinion? Opinion from the Messenger of Allah was correct, and from anyone below him it is error.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وقد بين الله قصص المغيرين بقوله إذ يبيتون مالا يرضى من القول بعد فقد الرسول ما يقيمون به أود باطلهم

sources.gloss: Allah has made plain the account of those who altered things by His word "when they conspire overnight with a discourse that He does not approve of", after the Messenger was gone, with what they prop up the crookedness of their falsehood.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وسله أن يصفح لك عن عقوبة ذنبك في مخاصمتك عن الخائن من خان مالاً لغيره … وقد قيل إن النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكن خاصم عن الخائن، ولكنه همّ بذلك، فأمره الله بالاستغفار مما همّ به من ذلك

sources.gloss: Ask Him to overlook for you the punishment of your sin in disputing on behalf of the traitor who betrayed another's property ... It has been said that the Prophet did not dispute on behalf of the traitor, but only intended to, so Allah commanded him to seek forgiveness for what he had intended.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: ذهب الطبري إلى أن المعنى. استغفر الله من ذنبك في خصامك للخائنين … وهذا مذهب من جوّز الصغائر على الأنبياء، صلوات الله عليهم. قال ابن عطية: وهذا ليس بذنب لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دافع على الظاهر وهو يعتقد براءتهم

sources.gloss: Al-Tabari held the meaning to be: seek Allah's forgiveness for your sin in disputing for the traitors ... This is the school of those who allow small sins to the prophets. Ibn Atiyyah said: this is no sin, because the Prophet defended only what appeared, believing them innocent.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: لا وَالله مَا فَوَّضَ الله إِلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ إِلا إِلَى رَسُولِ الله (صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِه) وَإِلَى الائِمَّةِ

sources.gloss: No, by Allah, Allah did not entrust it to any of His creation except to the Messenger of Allah and to the Imams.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: فَلَمَّا وَلَّيْتُ عَنْهُ صَفَقَ بِيَدِهِ وَقَالَ يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَلا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ

sources.gloss: When I turned away from him he struck his hands together and said: "They try to hide from people, but they do not try to hide from Allah."

essay.en:
These verses close a case that began at verse 105. Tabatabai reads the run as one argument for justice in judgment, and reconstructs the incident: a theft, a thief who blamed an innocent man, and kinsmen who pressed the Prophet to rule their way [1].

Verse 113 names what stood between the Prophet and that pressure. Tusi reads it as God shielding him by making the traitor's case plain, so that he held back from arguing for him, and identifies the party bent on making him slip as the traitors themselves [4]. Tabrisi records reported glosses of grace and mercy, from prophethood and aid by revelation to prophethood and safeguarding, and preserves a second reported occasion, a delegation from Thaqif who asked to keep al-Uzza a year, and were refused [2]. Fayd Kashani observes that the verse denies not their intent but its effect [13].

Verse 114 turns outward. Tusi takes their secret talks as people's private speech at large, so the exception marks the only talk that carries good: charity, what is right, reconciliation [5].

Verse 115 ends on the man who would not repent. Tusi glosses defiance as parting from the Messenger in enmity, and reports that the verse came down about Abu Tuma ibn al-Ubayriq when he refused repentance and joined the idolaters at Mecca, which is what is narrated from Imam al-Baqir [6]. Al-Qummi calls him Bashir [7]. It leaves a choice: the talk God rewards, or the road a man walks away on.

note.en: Tusi glosses the Book as the Quran and wisdom as the exposition of what the Book states in summary: its lawful and unlawful, its command and prohibition [4].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ان اناساً من رهط بشير الأدنين قالوا انطلقوا بنا إلى رسول الله صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم نكلمه في صاحبنا ونعذره … ثم ان بشيراً كفر ولحق بمكة وأنزل الله في النفر الذين أعذروا بشيراً وأتوا النبي صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم ليعذروه ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته
narrations.chain: al-Qummi, from al-Baqir

text.en: Some of Bashir's close kin said: Come with us to the Messenger of God to speak about our man and excuse him ... Then Bashir disbelieved and went to Mecca, and about the party who excused Bashir and came to the Prophet to plead for him God revealed: Were it not for Allah's grace and His mercy on you.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إنّ الأنبياء والأئمة صلوات الله عليهم يوفقهم الله ويؤتيهم من مخزون علمه وحكمه ما لا يؤتيه غيرهم، فيكون علمهم فوق علم أهل الزمان … وقال لنبيه وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَهَمَّتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُضِلُّوكَ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ۖ وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ۚ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ تَعْلَمُ ۚ وَكَانَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ عَظِيمًا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Ala al-Hamadani, raising it, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim

text.en: God grants the prophets and the Imams from His stored knowledge and wisdom what He gives no one else, so their knowledge is above that of the people of their age ... He said to His Prophet: Were it not for Allah's grace and His mercy on you ... He has taught you what you did not know.

note.en: Tabrisi cites al-Zajjaj: najwa is what a group or a pair keep to themselves, whether spoken in secret or openly [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله فرض التمحل في القرآن … أن يكون وجهك أعرض من وجه أخيك فتمحل له، و هو قول الله: { لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ }
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God has made contriving for others an obligation in the Quran ... that your face carry more weight than your brother's, so you contrive on his behalf; and that is God's word: There is no good in much of their secret talks.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) نهى عن القيل و القال، و فساد المال، و كثرة السؤال … إن الله عز و جل يقول: { لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ إِصْلاَحٍ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud

text.en: The Messenger of God forbade idle talk, the squandering of wealth and excessive questioning ... God says: There is no good in much of their secret talks, excepting him who enjoins charity or what is right or reconciliation between people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ } … يعني بالمعروف القرض
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: On There is no good in much of their secret talks, excepting him who enjoins charity or what is right, he said: by what is right is meant a loan.

note.en: Fayd Kashani reads the other way as anything besides the upright religion the faithful hold, and the abandoning as God forsaking a man to what he chose [14].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: اجعل لنا إماما يؤمنا في شهر رمضان، فقال: لا، و نهاهم أن يجتمعوا فيه … دعوهم و ما يريدون، ليصلي بهم من شاءوا، ثم قال: فمن { وَيَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ وَنُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ وَسَآءَتْ مَصِيراً }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Hurayz, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams

text.en: Appoint for us an imam to lead us in Ramadan. He said: No, and he forbade them to gather for it ... Leave them and what they want; let whoever they wish lead them. Then he said: so whoever follows a way other than that of the faithful, We shall abandon him to his devices ...

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: مر بنا ضب، فقال الأشعث و جرير: السلام عليك يا أمير المؤمنين … دعهما فهو إمامهما يوم القيامة، أما تسمع إلى الله و هو يقول: { نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ }
narrations.chain: from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from a man of the Ansar

text.en: A lizard passed by us, and al-Ashath and Jarir said: Peace be upon you, Commander of the Faithful ... Leave those two; it is their imam on the Day of Resurrection. Do you not hear God saying: We shall abandon him to his devices?

perspectives.en: The phrase a way other than that of the faithful is where the readings part. Qurtubi reports that the scholars take the verse as evidence for the soundness of holding by consensus [22], and Razi relays that al-Shafii, asked for a verse proving consensus, read the Quran three hundred times before finding this one [25]. Tabrisi answers that the verse will not carry that: its plain sense obliges following one who is a believer in reality, outwardly and inwardly, and where some apply it to a part of the community, others apply it to those whose infallibility is certain, the Imams of the family of Muhammad [3]. Tusi likewise allows that the believers here means the infallible Imams [6].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالتدبر يقرب أن القصة كأنها سرقة وقعت من بعضهم ثم رفع الأمر إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فرمى بها السارق غيره ممن هو بريء منها، ثم ألح قوم السارق عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ان يقضي لهم

sources.gloss: Reflection brings one close to the view that the story was a theft committed by one of them, and the matter was raised to the Prophet, and the thief cast it upon another who was innocent of it, and then the thief's people pressed the Prophet to judge in their favour.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقال الزجاج: النجوى في الكلام ما ينفرد به الجماعة أو الاثنان سرّاً كان أو ظاهراً … وقيل: نزلت في وفد من ثقيف قدموا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقالوا: يا محمد جئناك نبايعك على أن لا نكسر أصنامنا بأيدينا وعلى أن نمتع بالعزى سنة فلم يجبهم إلى ذلك وعصمه الله منه … قيل: { فضل الله } النبوة { ورحمته } نصرته إياه بالوحي. وقيل: { فضله } تأييده بألطافه { ورحمته } نعمته عن الجبائي. وقيل: { فضله } النبوة { ورحمته } العصمة

sources.gloss: Al-Zajjaj said: najwa in speech is what a group or a pair keep to themselves, whether secret or open ... It is said that it was revealed about a delegation from Thaqif who came to the Messenger of God and said: Muhammad, we have come to pledge to you on condition that we not break our idols with our own hands and that we enjoy al-Uzza for a year; he did not grant them that, and God protected him from it ... It is said: Allah's grace is prophethood and His mercy is His aiding him by revelation. And it is said: His grace is His support by His kindnesses and His mercy is His favour, from al-Jubbai. And it is said: His grace is prophethood and His mercy is the safeguarding.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والصحيح أنه لا يدل على ذلك لأَن ظاهر الآية يقتضي إيجاب متابعة من هو مؤمن على الحقيقة ظاهراً وباطناً … ومتى حملوا الآية على بعض الأَمة حملها غيرهم على من هو مقطوع على عصمته عنده من المؤمنين وهم الأَئمة من آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: The correct view is that it does not indicate that, because the plain sense of the verse requires making it obligatory to follow one who is a believer in reality, outwardly and inwardly ... And whenever they carry the verse upon a part of the community, others carry it upon those among the believers whose infallibility is certain to them, namely the Imams of the family of Muhammad.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى الآية أنه لولا أنه تعالى تفضل عليك يا محمد فعصمك بتوفيقه وبيانه لك أمر هذا الخائن حتى كففت عن الجدال عنه … ويعني بالفرقة التي همت من الخائنين أنفسهم … وانزل عليك الحكمة مضافة إلى الكتاب، وهي بيان ما ذكره في الكتاب مجملا من أحكام الكتاب: من الحلال والحرام، والامر والنهي

sources.gloss: The meaning of the verse is: were it not that God favoured you, Muhammad, and guarded you by His granting success and by His making plain to you the affair of this traitor, so that you refrained from disputing on his behalf ... and by the party who were bent on it He means the traitors themselves ... And He sent down upon you wisdom alongside the Book, and it is the exposition of what He mentioned in the Book in summary of its rulings: the lawful and the unlawful, the command and the prohibition.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أخبر الله تعالى: أنه لا خير في كثير من نجوى الناس جميعاً. والنجوى هو ما ينفرد به الاثنان أو الجماعة سراً كان أو جهراً.

sources.gloss: God has told us that there is no good in much of the private talk of people in general. Najwa is what two or a group keep to themselves, whether secret or spoken aloud.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: معنى يشاقق الرسول يباين الرسول معادياً له، فيفارقه على العداوة … ونزلت هذه الآية في الخائنين الذين ذكرهم الله في قوله: { ولا تكن للخائنين خصيماً } لما أبى التوبة أبو طعمة بن الابيرق ولحق بالمشركين من عبدة الاوثان بمكة مرتدا مفارقا رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وهو قول مجاهد وقتادة، واكثر المفسرين. وهو المروي عن أبى جعفر عليه السلام. … أو المؤمنين أراد به الائمة المعصومين

sources.gloss: The meaning of defying the Messenger is to part from the Messenger as his enemy, separating from him in enmity ... This verse was revealed about the traitors whom God mentioned in His word, do not be a contender on behalf of the traitors, when Abu Tuma ibn al-Ubayriq refused to repent and joined the idol-worshipping polytheists at Mecca as an apostate parting from the Messenger of God; that is the view of Mujahid and Qatada and most of the exegetes, and it is what is narrated from Abu Jafar ... or by the believers He meant the infallible Imams.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ونزلت في بشير وهو بمكة

sources.gloss: And it was revealed about Bashir while he was in Mecca.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أن يكون وجهك أعرض من وجه أخيك فتمحل له، و هو قول الله: { لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ }

sources.gloss: That your face carry more weight than your brother's, so you contrive on his behalf; and that is the word of God: There is no good in much of their secret talks.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: دعهما فهو إمامهما يوم القيامة، أما تسمع إلى الله و هو يقول: { نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ }

sources.gloss: Leave those two; it is their imam on the Day of Resurrection. Do you not hear God saying: We shall abandon him to his devices?

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وليس القصد فيه إلى نفي همهم بل إلى نفي تأثيره فيه

sources.gloss: The aim in it is not to deny that they were bent on it, but to deny that it had any effect on him.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: { وَيَتّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ } ما هم عليه من الدين الحنيفي { نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلّى } نجعله والياً لما تولى من الضلال بأن نخذله ونخلي بينه وبين ما اختاره

sources.gloss: And follows a way other than that of the faithful: other than the upright religion they hold to. We shall abandon him to his devices: We make him a client of the misguidance he took as guardian, by forsaking him and leaving him to what he chose.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: قال العلماء في قوله تعالى: { وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ } دليل على صحة القول بالإجماع

sources.gloss: The scholars said, concerning His word whoever defies the Apostle, that it is evidence for the soundness of holding by consensus.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: روي أن الشافعي رضي الله عنه سئل عن آية في كتاب الله تعالى تدل على أن الإجماع حجة، فقرأ القرآن ثلثمائة مرة حتى وجد هذه الآية

sources.gloss: It is narrated that al-Shafii was asked about a verse in the Book of God indicating that consensus is a proof, so he read the Quran three hundred times until he found this verse.

sources.author: abu abd allah muhammad b. ibrahim al-numani

excerpt.text: إنّ الأنبياء والأئمة صلوات الله عليهم يوفقهم الله ويؤتيهم من مخزون علمه وحكمه ما لا يؤتيه غيرهم، فيكون علمهم فوق علم أهل الزمان

sources.gloss: God grants the prophets and the Imams success and gives them of His stored knowledge and wisdom what He gives to no one besides them, so their knowledge is above the knowledge of the people of their age.

essay.en:
The passage opens on the one sin that admits no pardon; whatever is short of it lies under God's will. Tabatabai holds that these verses fit the reported occasion, the theft of Abu Tumah ibn al-Ubayriq, most closely, while warning that occasions of revelation are mostly transmitted stories applied to the verses that suit them [1]. Tabrisi glosses 'strayed into far error' as going from the path of truth and from the goal sought, the lasting bliss of the Garden, a departure whose farthest degree is ascribing partners to God [2].

The verses then expose what idolatry actually calls upon. Tusi records five readings of 'females': the idols the Arabs named with women's names, and, on al-Hasan's reading, whatever is dead and has no spirit in it, a dry stick or a dry stone [8]. Tabrisi cites Abu Hamza al-Thumali that in each idol sat a female satan who appeared to its keepers and spoke to them, the work of Iblis [3].

Satan then speaks in his own voice. Cursed, he claims a settled share and swears to mislead, to fill men with hopes, to have them slit the ears of cattle, the mark of the bahira [10], and to alter God's creation. Tusi reports the dispute over that last phrase: some read it as the gelding of animals, others as changing the religion God set in human nature, which is narrated from Abu Jafar and Abu Abdillah and which he judges strongest [10]. Against Satan's delusion stands a promise that cannot fail: Tabrisi reads the closing question as a denial, no one being truer than God in what He reports or promises [4].

The last verses turn on the gap between wishing and doing. Tusi prefers the reading that the hopes rebuked are those of Quraysh, who said they would be neither raised nor punished, since it is the disbelievers' hopes, not the Muslims', that the passage has just mentioned [12]. The promise stands open to all the accountable, male and female, and 'of the righteous deeds' is partitive, so that one who does some of them is admitted to the Garden [13]. The best religion is to hand over one's very self, wajh here meaning the person himself [6], and to follow Abraham, whom God took as a friend, khalil, from khulla, friendship, or khalla, need [14], not out of need, since whatever is in the heavens and the earth is already His [15].

note.en: Tusi draws from the verse the proof for what the Shia hold: that God may pardon those of the people of prayer who commit major sins, even if they have not repented [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ الله لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الْكَبَائِرَ فَمَا سِوَاهَا قَالَ قُلْتُ دَخَلَتِ الْكَبَائِرُ فِي الإسْتِثْنَاءِ قَالَ نَعَمْ.
narrations.chain: Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that any partner should be ascribed to Him, but He forgives anything besides that to whomever He wishes': the major sins and what is below them. I said: have the major sins entered into the exception? He said: yes.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: أَلاَ وَإنَّ الظُّلْمَ ثَلاَثَةٌ: فَظُلْمٌ لاَ يُغْفَرُ، وَظُلْمٌ لاَ يُتْرَكُ، وظُلْمٌ مَغْفُورٌ لاَ يُطْلَبُ. فَأَمَّا الظُّلْمُ الَّذِي لاَ يُغْفَرُ فَالشِّرْكُ بِاللهِ، قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّـهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾

text.en: Know that injustice is of three kinds: an injustice that is not forgiven, an injustice that is not left unquestioned, and an injustice forgiven without being sought out. As for the injustice that is not forgiven, it is ascribing partners to Allah. Allah has said: 'Indeed Allah does not forgive that any partner should be ascribed to Him.'

note.en: The one who swears is Iblis [17], and the settled share is a known portion, gathered by luring people off the right road [9].

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: في المجمع عن تفسير الثمالي عن النبي صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم في هذه الآية بني آدم تسعة وتسعون في النار وواحد في الجنة، وفي رواية أخرى من كل ألف واحد لله وسائرهم للنار ولإبليس.
narrations.chain: Majma al-Bayan, from the tafsir of al-Thumali, from the Prophet

text.en: On this verse: of the children of Adam, ninety-nine are in the Fire and one in the Garden. In another report: of every thousand, one is for Allah and the rest for the Fire and for Iblis.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، في قول الله: { وَلأَمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ ٱللَّهِ } ، قال: " دين الله
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from Abu Jafar

text.en: On the word of Allah, 'and I will prompt them to alter Allah's creation', he said: the religion of Allah.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: وفي المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام ليقطعن الأذن من أصلها
narrations.chain: Majma al-Bayan, from al-Sadiq

text.en: On 'they will slit the ears of cattle': let them cut the ear from its root.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا سفيان لا تذهبن بك المذاهب، عليك بالقصد، وعليك أن تتبع الهدى. قلت: يا ابن رسول الله وما اتباع الهدى؟ قال: كتاب الله ولزوم هذا الرجل. … يا سفيان إن أردت العروة الوثقى فعليك بعلي فإنه والله ينجيك
narrations.chain: Furat: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to me, with a chain, from Sufyan

text.en: O Sufyan, do not let the paths carry you off. Keep to the middle way, and follow the guidance. I said: what is following the guidance? He said: the Book of Allah and adherence to this man. … O Sufyan, if you want the firmest handhold, hold to Ali; by Allah, he will save you.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: فقال إبليس: رب هذا الذي كرمته علي و فضلته، و إن لم تفضل علي لم أقو عليه. قال: لا يولد له ولد إلا ولد لك ولدان. … قال: رب زدني. قال: تعدهم و تمنيهم { وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً }
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Jabir, from the Prophet

text.en: Iblis said: Lord, this one whom You honoured above me, unless You favour me I cannot overcome him. He said: no child is born to him but two are born to you. … He said: Lord, increase me. He said: you promise them and give them hopes, 'yet Satan does not promise them anything but delusion.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: لما نزلت هذه الآية { مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ } قال بعض أصحاب رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): ما أشدها من آية! فقال لهم رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): أما تبتلون في أموالكم و في أنفسكم و ذراريكم؟ قالوا: بلى. قال: هذا مما يكتب الله لكم به الحسنات، و يمحو به السيئات
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Jafar

text.en: When this verse came down, some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah said: how severe a verse! So the Messenger of Allah said to them: are you not tried in your wealth, your persons and your children? They said: yes. He said: this is of what Allah writes good deeds for you by, and effaces evil deeds by.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إسماعيل قال للصادق عليه السلام يا ابتاه ما تقول في المذنب منا ومن غيرنا فقال ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوء يجز به

text.en: Ismail said to him: father, what do you say about the sinner among us and among others? He said: 'It will be neither after your hopes nor the hopes of the People of the Book: whoever commits evil shall be requited for it.'

note.en: The speck is the dot on the back of the date-stone, of which it is said the palm grows; not the least of the reward owed is withheld [13].
'The creed of Abraham' is glossed as the ten practices of the Hanifiyya which Abraham brought, unabrogated until the Day of Resurrection [20].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قلت لأبي عبد الله (عليه السلام): لم اتخذ الله عز و جل إبراهيم خليلا؟ قال: " لكثرة سجوده على الأرض
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sadabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one he mentioned

text.en: I said to Abu Abdillah: why did Allah take Abraham as a dedicated friend? He said: for the abundance of his prostration upon the earth.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: سمعت أبي يحدث، عن أبيه (عليه السلام)، أنه قال: اتخذ الله عز و جل إبراهيم خليلا، لأنه لم يرد أحدا، و لم يسأل أحدا غير الله عز و جل
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar al-Hamadani, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: I heard my father relate from his father that he said: Allah took Abraham as a dedicated friend because he never turned anyone away and never asked anyone other than Allah.

narrations.speaker: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari
narrations.arabic: إنما اتخذ الله عز و جل إبراهيم خليلا لكثرة صلاته على محمد و أهل بيته (صلوات الله عليهم)
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sinani, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Asadi al-Kufi, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Abd al-Azim ibn Abdillah al-Hasani

text.en: Allah took Abraham as a dedicated friend only for the abundance of his blessings upon Muhammad and the people of his house.

perspectives.en: On 'whoever commits evil shall be requited for it', Tusi reports al-Hasan's reading that the requital is the disbelievers', and prefers it as suiting his school: the unbeliever is never forgiven, while a Muslim may be forgiven the punishment he deserves, so one cannot rule that every evil must be requited [12]. Qurtubi reports that the majority read the wording as general, covering believer and unbeliever alike: the unbeliever is requited with the Fire, the believer with the blows of this world, since every affliction that reaches a Muslim, even a thorn, is an expiation [47].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فالآيات أشد انطباقاً على ما روي في سبب النزول من قصة سرقة أبي طعمة بن الأبيرق، وإن كانت أسباب النزول - كما سمعت مراراً - في أغلب ما رويت من قبيل تطبيق القصص المأثورة على ما يناسبها من الآيات القرآنية.

sources.gloss: The verses fit most closely what is narrated as the occasion of revelation, the story of the theft of Abu Tumah ibn al-Ubayriq, although occasions of revelation, as you have heard repeatedly, are in most of what is narrated of the kind of applying transmitted stories to the Quranic verses that suit them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي ذهب عن طريق الحق والغرض المطلوب وهو النعيم المقيم في الجنة ذهاباً بعيداً لأَنَّ الذهاب عن نعيم الجنة يكون على مراتب أبعدها الشرك بالله.

sources.gloss: That is, he has gone from the path of truth and from the goal sought, which is the lasting bliss of the Garden, gone far, because going away from the bliss of the Garden has degrees, the farthest of them being to ascribe partners to Allah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: كان في كل واحدة منهن شيطانة أنثى تتراءى للسَدَنة وتكلّمهم وذلك من صنع إبليس وهو الشيطان الذي ذكره الله.

sources.gloss: In each one of them was a female satan who appeared to the temple keepers and spoke to them, and that was of the making of Iblis, and he is the Satan whom Allah mentioned.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { ومن أصدق } استفهام فيه معنى النفي أي لا أحد أصدق من الله قولاً فيما أخبره ووعداً فيما وعد.

sources.gloss: 'And who is truer' is a question carrying the sense of negation: that is, no one is truer than Allah in speech in what He reports, or in promise in what He promises.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي استسلم وجهه والمراد بقولـه وجهه هنا ذاته ونفسه

sources.gloss: That is, he surrendered his face; and what is meant by 'his face' here is his essence and his self.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقد بينا الاستدلال بذلك على ما نذهب اليه من جواز العفو عن مرتكبي الكبائر من أهل الصلاة، وإن لم يتوبوا

sources.gloss: We have already set out the proof drawn from this for what we hold, the permissibility of pardoning those of the people of prayer who commit the major sins, even if they do not repent.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: اختلفوا في تأويل هذه الآية على خمسة أقوال

sources.gloss: They differed over the interpretation of this verse into five views.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني قسما معلوماً وبه قال الضحاك. واتخاذ الشيطان النصيب من عباد الله يكون باغوائه اياهم عن قصد السبيل

sources.gloss: It means a known portion, and so said al-Dahhak. And Satan taking a share of the servants of Allah happens by his luring them away from the right road.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وأقوى الاقوال من قال: فليغيرن خلق الله بمعنى دين الله بدلالة قوله: { فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم }

sources.gloss: The strongest of the views is that of the one who said 'they will alter Allah's creation' means the religion of Allah, on the evidence of His word: the origination of Allah according to which He originated mankind; there is no altering Allah's creation; that is the upright religion.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وهو الذي يليق بمذهبنا، لانا نقطع على ان الكفار لا يغفر لهم على حال والمسلمون يجوز أن يغفر لهم ما يستحقونه من العقاب، فلا يمكننا القطع على أنه لا بد أن يجازي بكل سوءٍ.

sources.gloss: This is what suits our school, for we hold definitively that the disbelievers are not forgiven in any case, while the Muslims may be forgiven the punishment they deserve, so we cannot rule definitively that every evil must be requited.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وعد الله تعالى بهذه الآية جميع المكلفين من الذكور والاناث … ولا يبخسهم شيئاً مما يستحقونه من الثواب، وان كان مقدار نقير في الصغر، وهي النقطة التي في ظهر النواة، وقيل منها تنبت النخلة. … أن (من) في قوله: { من الصالحات } يقتضي أنه لو فعل بعض الصالحات لأدخل الجنة، لأنها للتبعيض.

sources.gloss: By this verse Allah promised all the accountable, male and female ... and He will not diminish anything of the reward they deserve, even were it the measure of a naqir in smallness, which is the dot on the back of the date-stone, and it is said that the palm grows from it ... 'min' in His word 'of the righteous deeds' entails that if one did some of the righteous deeds he would be admitted to the Garden, for it is partitive.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فاما الاشتقاق فالخلة بضم الخاء: الصداقة. والخلة بفتح الخاء: الحاجة

sources.gloss: As for the derivation: khulla, with a damma on the kha, is friendship, and khalla, with a fatha on the kha, is need.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وكيف يحتاج الى خلته من له ما فى السماوات والارض من قليل وكثير ملكا، ومع ذلك مستغن عن جميع خلقه.

sources.gloss: How could He need his friendship, when to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, little and much, as property, and He is besides that free of need of His whole creation.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قوله { لأتخذن من عبادك نصيباً مفروضاً } [118] يعني إبليس

sources.gloss: His word 'I will surely take of Your servants a settled share' means Iblis.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: هي الحنفية العشرة التي جاء بها إبراهيم التي لم تنسخ إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: It is the ten practices of the Hanifiyya which Abraham brought, which have not been abrogated until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر (عليه السلام)، في قول الله: { وَلأَمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ ٱللَّهِ } ، قال: " دين الله

sources.gloss: From Jabir, from Abu Jafar, on the word of Allah 'and I will prompt them to alter Allah's creation', he said: the religion of Allah.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: رب زدني. قال: تعدهم و تمنيهم { وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ إِلاَّ غُرُوراً }

sources.gloss: He said: Lord, increase me. He said: you promise them and give them hopes, yet Satan does not promise them anything but delusion.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هذا مما يكتب الله لكم به الحسنات، و يمحو به السيئات

sources.gloss: This is of what Allah writes down good deeds for you by, and effaces evil deeds by.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قلت لأبي عبد الله (عليه السلام): لم اتخذ الله عز و جل إبراهيم خليلا؟ قال: " لكثرة سجوده على الأرض

sources.gloss: I said to Abu Abdillah: why did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, take Abraham as a dedicated friend? He said: for the abundance of his prostration upon the earth.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: وفي المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام ليقطعن الأذن من أصلها

sources.gloss: And in al-Majma, from al-Sadiq: let them cut the ear from its root.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: في العيون أن إسماعيل قال للصادق عليه السلام يا ابتاه ما تقول في المذنب منا ومن غيرنا

sources.gloss: In al-Uyun, that Ismail said to al-Sadiq: father, what do you say about the sinner among us and among others?

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: يا سفيان إن أردت العروة الوثقى فعليك بعلي فإنه والله ينجيك

sources.gloss: O Sufyan, if you want the firmest handhold, then hold to Ali, for by Allah he will save you.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقال الجمهور: لفظ الآية عام، والكافر والمؤمن مجاز بعمله السوء، فأما مجازاة الكافر فالنار لأن كفره أوْبَقَه، وأما المؤمن فبنكبات الدنيا

sources.gloss: The majority said: the wording of the verse is general, and the disbeliever and the believer are both requited for their evil deed; as for the requital of the disbeliever it is the Fire, since his disbelief has destroyed him, and as for the believer it is by the blows of this world.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: قُلْتُ دَخَلَتِ الْكَبَائِرُ فِي الإسْتِثْنَاءِ قَالَ نَعَمْ.

sources.gloss: I said: have the major sins entered into the exception? He said: yes.

sources.author: al-sharif al-radi

excerpt.text: فَأَمَّا الظُّلْمُ الَّذِي لاَ يُغْفَرُ فَالشِّرْكُ بِاللهِ

sources.gloss: As for the injustice that is not forgiven, it is ascribing partners to Allah.

essay.en:
The passage opens with a question the Prophet is not the one to answer. Tabatabai reads these verses as coming after the rulings at the head of the surah, which revived rights of women that people had let die; when they came down the people brought the matter to the Prophet, and God ordered him to reply that what He has settled for them upon men is a divine ruling in which he himself has no say [1]. What has been prescribed for the orphan girls and withheld from them is, on the first reading al-Tabrisi records, their inheritance, from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, and narrated from Abu Ja'far; a second reading makes it the dowry [2]. Al-Tusi records a further reading, from Aisha, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others: the guardian who holds such a girl back from marriage for her property, hoping she will die and he will inherit [7].

Then the passage goes inside a marriage. A wife fears her husband's misconduct or desertion: his raising himself above her toward another, or turning away his face and the benefits she had from him [8]. What is offered is not a court but a settlement: she gives up her day, or waives part of the maintenance or clothing owed her, to keep her place in the marriage, and that, al-Tusi says, is better than seeking separation [8].

Verse 129 then concedes what no law can command. Al-Tusi is precise: what is denied is equality in love and inclination, which follows desire and is God's doing, not equality in maintenance, clothing and the turn, which God commanded and would not command if it were beyond a servant's capacity [9]. What is forbidden is leaving the unloved wife as if in suspense, neither having a husband nor free, as al-Tabrisi reports from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah [4].

And if the marriage ends, God suffices each of them: proof, for al-Tusi, that all provision is in God's hand [10]. The horizon then widens. To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, said three times: for emphasis, al-Tabrisi notes, or for three grounds, obedience owed Him, His freedom from need, His keeping of what He owns [5]. Al-Tusi hears in the close a rebuke of the men who betrayed the coat of mail and a warning to the rest: God can take them away and bring a people who will help His prophet [11].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فإن نبي الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) سئل عن النساء ما لهن من الميراث؟ فأنزل الله الربع و الثمن
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The Prophet of God was asked about women, what they have of inheritance, and God sent down the quarter and the eighth.

narrations.speaker: the Messenger of God
narrations.arabic: قالوا: يا رسول الله، للجارية نصف ما ترك أبوها و أخوها، و يعطى الصبي الصغير الميراث، و ليس أحد منهما يركب الفرس، و لا يحوز الغنيمة، و لا يقاتل العدو؟! فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): " بذلك أمرت "

text.en: They said: Messenger of God, the girl takes half of what her father and her brother left, and the small boy is given inheritance, and neither of them rides a horse or takes spoils or fights an enemy. He said: With that I was commanded.

note.en: Al-Tusi holds this stands only when it comes from her own goodwill; otherwise the husband owes her clothing, maintenance and her turn, or else he divorces her [8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هي المرأة تكون عند الرجل فيكرهها، فيقول لها: إني أريد أن أطلقك، فتقول له: لا تفعل، إني أكره أن يشمت بي، و لكن انظر في ليلتي فاصنع بها ما شئت، و ما كان سوى ذلك من شيء فهو لك، و دعني على حالتي
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: She is the woman with a man who dislikes her, and he says to her: I want to divorce you. She says: Do not; I hate to be gloated over. But look to my night and do with it what you wish, and whatever else there is is yours, and leave me as I am.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: نشوز الرجل يهم بطلاق امرأته، فتقول له: أدع ما على ظهرك، و أعطيك كذا و كذا، و أحللك من يومي و ليلتي على ما اصطلحا، فهو جائز
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: The misconduct of the man is that he means to divorce his wife, and she says to him: Let go what you owe me, and I will give you such and such, and I make my day and my night lawful to you. Whatever they settle on is permitted.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أَمَّا قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فَانْكِحُوا ما طابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّساءِ مَثْنى‏ وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلا تَعْدِلُوا فَواحِدَةً يَعْنِي فِي النَّفَقَةِ وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُ وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّساءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوها كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ يَعْنِي فِي الْمَوَدَّةِ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nuh ibn Shuayb and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan

text.en: As for His words, marry such women as you like, two, three or four, but if you fear you will not be fair, then only one: that means in maintenance. And as for His words, you will not be able to be fair between wives even if you are eager: that means in affection.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: كنت عند أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) فأتاه رجل فشكا إليه الحاجة فأمره بالتزويج. قال: فاشتدت به الحاجة، فأتى أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) فسأله عن حاله، فقال له: اشتدت بي الحاجة، قال: " فارق " ففارق. قال: ثم أتاه فسأله عن حاله، فقال: أثريت و حسن حالي … إني أمرتك بأمرين أمر الله بهما، قال الله عز و جل: { وَأَنْكِحُواْ ٱلأَيَامَىٰ مِنْكُمْ وَٱلصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ } إلى قوله: { وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ } [النور: 32] و قال: { وَإِن يَتَفَرَّقَا يُغْنِ ٱللَّهُ كُلاًّ مِّن سَعَتِهِ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, by his chain from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Hamdawayh ibn Imran, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Asim ibn Humayd

text.en: A man complained to him of need; he told him to marry. The need grew worse; he said: Separate. He did, and prospered. The Imam said: I commanded you two things God commanded. God said, marry off those of you who are single, and He said, if they separate, Allah will suffice each of them out of His bounty.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قد جمع الله ما يتواصى به المتواصون من الأولين والآخرين في خصلة واحدة وهي التقوى وفيه جماع كل عبادة صالحة وبه وصل من وصل إلى الدرجات العلى

text.en: God has gathered all that those who counsel one another have counselled, from the first of them to the last, into one trait, and it is God-wariness. In it is the whole of every sound act of worship, and by it whoever has arrived has arrived at the highest degrees.

narrations.speaker: the Messenger of God
narrations.arabic: ويروى أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية ضرب النبي صلّى الله عليه وآله وسلم يده على ظهر سلمان رضي الله عنه وقال هم قوم هذا يعني عجم الفرس

text.en: It is related that when this verse came down, the Prophet struck his hand on the back of Salman and said: They are the people of this man. That is, the Persians.

note.en: Al-Tabrisi gives two readings: al-Jubbai has the fighter seek both rewards from God, who owns them; others read a threat to the hypocrites, whose worldly reward is spoils and whose reward hereafter is the Fire [6].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: كانت الحكماء والفقهاء إذا كاتب بعضهم بعضاً كتبوا بثلاث ليس معهن رابعة من كانت الآخرة همته كفاه الله همته من الدنيا ومن اصلح سريرته أصلح الله علانيته ومن اصلح فيما بينه وبين الله اصلح الله فيما بينه وبين الناس
narrations.chain: In al-Kafi and al-Khisal, from al-Sadiq, from his father, from his forefathers, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: The wise and the jurists, when they wrote to one another, wrote three things and no fourth: whoever's concern is the Hereafter, God suffices him his concern from this world; whoever sets right his inward, God sets right his outward; and whoever sets right what is between him and God, God sets right what is between him and people.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الدنيا طالبة ومطلوبة فمن طلب الدنيا طلبه الموت حتى يخرجه منها ومن طلب الآخرة طلبته الدنيا حتى توفيه رزقه

text.en: The world is a seeker and a sought. Whoever seeks the world, death seeks him until it takes him out of it; and whoever seeks the Hereafter, the world seeks him until it pays him his provision in full.

perspectives.en: Both traditions read verse 128 through an occasion of revelation, and they anchor it in different marriages. Al-Qummi says it came down about the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah, an older wife whose husband married a young woman he found more pleasing [12]; al-Tabrisi reports the same case from Abu Ja'far and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and gives Sawda bint Zam'a only as a second report, from Ibn Abbas [3]. Ibn Kathir leads with Sawda: when she grew old and the Messenger of God resolved to part from her, she settled with him on his keeping her while she gave her day to Aisha [29].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فأمره الله سبحانه أن يجيبهم ان الذي قرَّره لهنَّ على الرجال من احكام إنما هو فتيا إلهية ليس له في ذلك من الأمر شيء

sources.gloss: So God commanded him to answer them that what He has settled for women as rulings upon men is a divine ruling in which he has no part in the matter.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي من الميراث عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر ع، وثانيها: أن المعنى اللاتي لا تؤتونهنّ ما وجب لهن من الصداق

sources.gloss: That is, of the inheritance: from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, and it is what is narrated from Abu Ja'far. The second reading is that it means those whom you do not give what is due to them of the dowry.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: كانت بنت محمد بن سلمة عند رافع بن خديج وكانت قد دخلت في السن وكانت عنده امرأة شابة سواها فطلَّقها تطليقة حتى إذا بقي من أجلها يسير قال: إن شئتِ راجعتكِ وصبرتِ على الأَثرة وإن شئت تركتك. قالت: بل راجعني واصبرُ على الأثرة فراجعها فذلك الصلح الذي بلغنا إن الله تعالى أنزل فيه هذه الآية عن أبي جعفر وسعيد بن المسيب. وقيل: خشيت سودة بنت زمعة أن يطلِّقها رسول الله. فقالت لا تطلقني وأجلسني مع نسائك ولا تقسم لي واجعل يومي لعائشة فنزلت الآية عن ابن عباس

sources.gloss: The daughter of Muhammad ibn Salamah was with Rafi ibn Khadij, and she had grown on in years, and he had another wife, a young one. He divorced her once, and when little of her term remained he said: if you wish I take you back and you bear being second, and if you wish I leave you. She said: rather take me back and I will bear it. So he took her back. That is the reconciliation about which we are told God sent down this verse, from Abu Ja'far and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. And it is said: Sawda bint Zam'a feared that the Messenger of God would divorce her, so she said, do not divorce me, seat me with your wives and apportion no turn to me, and give my day to Aisha. So the verse came down, from Ibn Abbas.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فتذروها كالمعلقة } أي تذروا التي لا تميلون إليها كالتي هي لا ذات زوج ولا أيّم عن ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وغيرهم، وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله

sources.gloss: That is, you leave the one you do not incline to like a woman who is neither married nor unmarried: from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and others, and it is what is narrated from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وأما وجه التكرار لقولـه: { ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض } في الآيتين ثلاث مرات فقد قيل: إنه للتأكيد والتذكير. وقيل: إنه للإبانة عن علل ثلاث أحدها: بيان إيجاب طاعته فيما قضى به لأن له ملك السماوات والأرض والثاني: بيان غناه عن خلقه وحاجتهم إليه واستحقاقه الحمد على النعم لأن له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض والثالث: بيان حفظه إياهم وتدبيره لهم

sources.gloss: As for the reason the words to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth are repeated three times in the two verses, it is said that it is for emphasis and reminder; and it is said that it is to make plain three grounds: first, that obedience to Him is due in what He decrees, since the kingdom of the heavens and the earth is His; second, His freedom from need of His creation, their need of Him and His deserving of praise for His favours; third, His keeping of them and His governing of them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة } أي يملك سبحانه الدنيا والآخرة فيطلب المجاهد الثوابين عند الله عند أبي علي الجبائي. وقيل: إنه وعيد للمنافقين وثوابهم في الدنيا ما يأخذونه من الفيء والغنيمة إذا شهدوا الحرب مع المسلمين وأمنهم على نفوسهم وأموالهم وذراريهم وثوابهم في الآخرة النار

sources.gloss: With Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter: that is, He owns this world and the Hereafter, so let the fighter seek both rewards from God. This is al-Jubbai's view. And it is said that it is a threat to the hypocrites, whose reward in this world is what they take of the spoils when they are present at war alongside the Muslims, and whose reward in the Hereafter is the Fire.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi
